Described as heavenly (दिव्य) 6. 116. 38; used by Arjuna against the Gandharvas, who had captured the Kauravas, to ward off the showers of arrows released by them; the Gandharvas felt burnt by the arrows (दह्य-मानाः) of Arjuna 3. 234. 17-18; according to Bhīṣma's information, only Arjuna, among men, knew this missile, and perhaps Kṛṣṇa 6. 116. 38-39.
सौर: Saura astra nt.: Name of a missile related to Sūra. Used by Arjuna against the Gandharvas, who had captured the Kauravas, to ward off the showers of arrows released by them; the Gandharvas felt burnt by the arrows (दह्य-मानाः) of Arjuna 3. 234. 17-18; [See Bhāskara astra].
स्थूणाकर्ण: Sthūṇākarṇa nt.: Name of a missile, apparently known to very few heroes. According to Nīlakaṇṭha, it is related to Śaṅkukarṇa, one of the incarnations of Rudra (स्थूणाकर्ण इति शङ्कुकर्णाख्यो रुद्रावतारभेदस् तद्दैवत्यम् अस्त्रम् on 3. 167. 33 Bom. Ed.); it seems to have been a very important missile since it is mentioned along with the Pāśupata and the Brahmāstra 5. 47. 100; 5. 139. 31 (also Aindra); Arjuna, in his message sent through Saṃjaya, threatened to use Sthūṇākarṇa against the Kaurava warriors in the war 5. 47. 100; Karṇa, too, was sure that Arjuna would use Sthūṇākarṇa in the war with the employment of proper मन्त्रस् on his arrow (मन्त्रास् तत्र भविष्यन्ति प्रयुक्ताः सव्यसाचिना) 5. 139. 31; but its use by Arjuna in the war is not recorded; on the other hand Karṇa him-self, while inciting the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra who were attacking Yudhiṣṭhira to kill him, released Sthūṇākarṇa, along with Indrajāla and Pāśupata, to overpower Yudhiṣṭhira 8. 43. 20-21; outside the epic war, Arjuna used it against the Kirāta (Śiva) who swallowed it up 3. 163. 32; Arjuna used it also against the Gandharvas who had captured the Kauravas; the Gandharvas were tormented by the heat (दह्यमानाः) of the arrows released by the use of the missile 3. 234. 17-18; Balarāma had released Sthūṇākarṇa missile to repulse a very powerful गदा hurled against him and Kṛṣṇa by Jarāsandha; the गदा, when met with force by the missile, fell on the earth tearing it open and the impact produced by it shook the mountains; the Rākṣasī Jarā (who had joined the two parts of the body of Jarāsandha) lay concealed under the ground; she, together with her sons and relatives, was killed due to the impact of the गदा and the Sthūṇākarṇa missile on the earth 7. 156. 10-14.
संवर्तमरुत्तीय: Saṃvartamaruttīya nt.: Name of an आख्यान 1. 2. 206. Described as one not excelled by any other आख्यान (अनुत्तम), it occurs as a part of the 14th Aśvamedhika parvan 1. 2. 206; in the Āśvamedhikaparvan it is alluded to as a कथा 14. 4. 1, or an old इतिहाष and a संवाद between Bṛhaspati and Marutta (अत्राप्य् उदाहरन्तीमम् इतिहासं पुरातनम् । बृहस्पतेश् च संवादं मरुत्तस्य च भारत) 14. 6. 1; related to the अध्यायस् 14. 4-10; also cf. 14. 3. 20-22.
संशप्तकवध: Saṃśaptakavadha m.: Name of the 66th पर्वन् in the list of a hundred sub-पर्वन्स् of the Bhārata supposed to have been made by Vyāsa in the Parvasaṃgraha 1. 2. 56, 33, 70. The incident is referred to while listing the contents of the Droṇaparvan as: where the Saṃśaptakas took Arjuna away from the battle-field (यत्र शंशप्तकाः पार्थम् अपनिन्यू रणाजिरात्) 1. 2. 160, and where Arjuna completely annihilated what remained of the Saṃśaptakas after he killed Jayadratha (हतो राजा जयद्रथः । संशप्तकाव-शेषं च कृतं निःशेषम् आहवे) 1. 2. 163; the incident is referred to by Dhṛtarāṣṭra in his summary of the events made for Saṃjaya 1. 1. 131; related to the अध्यायस् 7. 16-31.
सञ्जययान: Saṃjayayāna nt.: Name of the 50th पर्वन् in the list of a hundred sub-पर्वन्स् of the Bhārata supposed to have been made by Vyāsa in the Parvasaṃgraha (ततः संजययानाख्यं पर्व ज्ञेयम् अतः परम्) 1. 2. 50, 33, 70. The incident is mentioned in the summary of the contents of the Udyogaparvan as follows: where Dhṛtarāṣṭra sent Saṃjaya as his messenger to make peace with the Pāṇḍa-vas 1. 2. 140; related to the अध्यायस् 5. 22-32.
संजययान: Saṃjayayāna nt.: Name of the 50th पर्वन् in the list of a hundred sub-पर्वन्स् of the Bhārata supposed to have been made by Vyāsa in the Parvasaṃgraha (ततः संजययानाख्यं पर्व ज्ञेयम् अतः परम्) 1. 2. 50, 33, 70. The incident is mentioned in the summary of the contents of the Udyogaparvan as follows: where Dhṛtarāṣṭra sent Saṃjaya as his messenger to make peace with the Pāṇḍa-vas 1. 2. 140; related to the अध्यायस् 5. 22-32.
सभापर्वन्: Sabhāparvan1 nt.: Name of the 20th पर्वन् in the list of a hundred sub-पर्वन्स् of the Bhārata supposed to have been made by Vyāsa in the Parvasaṃgraha 1. 2. 39, 33, 70. Related to the अध्यायस् 2. 1-11. [See Sabhāparvan2]

Sabhāparvan2 nt.: Name of the 2nd पर्वन् among the 18 major पर्वन्स् of the Bhārata 1. 2. 97, 103. Described as having many events (बहु-वृत्तान्त) 1. 2. 97; its contents are summa-rized as follows: (where we hear) the con-struction of the सभा of the Pāṇḍavas; the appearance of the किङ्करस्; the description by Nārada of the सभास् of the guardians of the world; the undertaking of the Rāja-sūya; the killing of Jarāsandha; the release by Kṛṣṇa of the kings imprisoned in the Girivraja; the killing of Śiśupāla over the dispute regarding the guest worship at the Rājasūya; derision of Duryodhana by Bhīma on the floor of the सभा; Duryodhana griev-ed and angered at the riches gathered by the Pāṇḍavas for the sacrifice; where angry Duryodhana forced a game of dice (on the Pāṇḍavas); where gambler Śakuni defeated Yudhiṣṭhira at the game of dice; where Draupadī saved the Pāṇḍavas, as a boat (saves one) in an ocean; where Duryodhana challenged the Pāṇḍvas to a second game of dice 1. 2. 97-102; all this constitutes the Sabhāparvan and it was narrated by the great sage (एतत् सर्वं सभापर्व समाख्यातं महात्मना) 1. 2. 103; its अध्यायस् are known to be 72 (अध्यायाः … ज्ञेयाः) and the number of श्लोकस् are declared to be 2511 (श्लोकाश् च … ज्ञेयाः पर्वण्य् अस्मिन् प्रकी-र्तिताः) 1. 2. 103-104; the incidents of the Sabhāparvan are referred to in Dhṛtarāṣṭra's summary of the events made for Saṃjaya 1. 1. 105-107, and by Vaiśaṃpāyana in his summary made for Janamejaya 1. 55. 38-40. [See Sabhāparvan1]
सम्भवपर्वन्: Saṃbhavaparvan nt.: Name of the 7th पर्वन् in the list of a hundred sub-पर्वन्स् of the Bhārata supposed to have been made by Vyāsa in the Parvasaṃgraha 1. 2. 35, 33, 70. Described as wonderful (अद्भुत) and created by the gods (देवनिर्मित) 1. 2. 35; its contents are summarized as follows: (where we are told) the birth of the Vasus as sons of Bhāgīrathī (Gaṅgā) in the house of Śaṃtanu and their rise to heaven again; birth of Bhīṣma from the combi-nation of the portions of the lustre of the Vasus (तेजोंशानां च संघाताद् भीष्म-स्याप्य् अत्र संभवः 1. 2. 79); Bhīṣma's renouncing the kingdom and his determina-tion to remain celibate; Bhīṣma's fulfilling his vow and his guardianship of Citrāṅgada; at the death of Citrāṅgada, Bhīṣma's giving protection to the younger brother (Vicitra-vīrya) and putting him on to the throne; birth of Dharma among men as a result of the curse of sage Aṇīmāṇḍavya and birth of Dhṛtarāṣṭra and Pāṇḍu from Kṛṣṇa-dvaipā-yana as a result of a boon, and birth of the Pāṇḍavas 1. 2. 78-82; the incidents are referr-ed to in Sūta's summary of the events made for the sages assembled in the Naimiṣa forest 1. 1. 53-55; 67-69; the पर्वन् is related to the अध्यायस् 1. 62-123.
संभवपर्वन्: Saṃbhavaparvan nt.: Name of the 7th पर्वन् in the list of a hundred sub-पर्वन्स् of the Bhārata supposed to have been made by Vyāsa in the Parvasaṃgraha 1. 2. 35, 33, 70. Described as wonderful (अद्भुत) and created by the gods (देवनिर्मित) 1. 2. 35; its contents are summarized as follows: (where we are told) the birth of the Vasus as sons of Bhāgīrathī (Gaṅgā) in the house of Śaṃtanu and their rise to heaven again; birth of Bhīṣma from the combi-nation of the portions of the lustre of the Vasus (तेजोंशानां च संघाताद् भीष्म-स्याप्य् अत्र संभवः 1. 2. 79); Bhīṣma's renouncing the kingdom and his determina-tion to remain celibate; Bhīṣma's fulfilling his vow and his guardianship of Citrāṅgada; at the death of Citrāṅgada, Bhīṣma's giving protection to the younger brother (Vicitra-vīrya) and putting him on to the throne; birth of Dharma among men as a result of the curse of sage Aṇīmāṇḍavya and birth of Dhṛtarāṣṭra and Pāṇḍu from Kṛṣṇa-dvaipā-yana as a result of a boon, and birth of the Pāṇḍavas 1. 2. 78-82; the incidents are referr-ed to in Sūta's summary of the events made for the sages assembled in the Naimiṣa forest 1. 1. 53-55; 67-69; the पर्वन् is related to the अध्यायस् 1. 62-123.
सम्यङ्मनस्: Samyaṅmanas nt.: Name of a शास्त्र dealing with renunciation (तत्र सम्यङ्-मनो नाम त्यागशास्त्रम्) 12. 212. 16. Described as unexcelled (अनुत्तम) 12. 212. 16; it was taught to Janaka Janadeva, king of Mithilā, (12. 212. 1; 12. 211. 1) by कवि Pañcaśikha Kāpileya (12. 211. 6, 15-16), the pupil of Āsuri (12. 211. 10); the nature of त्याग was expounded by Pañcaśikha to the king so that he might attain emancipation (शृणु यत् तव मोक्षाय भाष्यमाणं भविष्यति) 12. 212. 16; the exposition of the शास्त्र is found in 12. 212. 17-43; one who knows this knowledge leading to emancipation and one who, with-out making a mistake, seeks the soul is not tainted by the undesirable fruits of his acts (इमां तु यो वेद विमोक्षबुद्धिम् आत्मानम् अन्विच्छति चाप्रमत्तः । न लिप्यते कर्मफलैर् अनिष्टैः पत्रं बिस-स्येव जलेन सिक्तम्) 12. 212. 44; the condi-tion of such a person is described in 12. 212. 45-50; when the king of Videha (Janaka Janadeva) was taught the state of immortality (अमृतपदम्), he lived very happily and was freed from sorrow 12. 212, 51; one who reads this established doctrine on emancipation (विमोक्षनिश्चय) does not experience calamities and is freed (of all bonds, cf. 12. 212. 45) 12. 212. 52.
सानत्सुजात: Sānatsujāta nt.: Name of the 52nd पर्वन् in the list of a hundred sub-पर्वन्स् of the Bhārata supposed to have been made by Vyāsa in the Parvasaṃgraha 1. 2. 51, 33, 70. A section of the Udyogaparvan is so called; in this sub-पर्वन् the grieved king Dhṛtarāṣṭra was instructed by Sanatsujāta in the excellent doctrine concerning आत्मन् (तथा सनत्सुजातेन यत्राध्यात्मम् अनु-त्तमम् । मनस्तापान्वितो राजा श्रावितः शोकलालसः) 1. 2. 143; related to the अध्यायस् 5. 42-45.
सामन्: Sāman nt. (mostly plural): Stands for the Sāmaveda, or a hymn or stanzas of that Veda (in this sense it often occurs along with ऋच् and यजुस्); a melody in which the stanzas of the Sāmaveda are sung. A. Relationship with Bhagāvān: Bhaga-vān told Arjuna that those who knew the Veda called him the Sāmaveda of a thousand branches (मां प्रचक्षते । सहस्रशाखं यत् साम ये वै वेदविदो जनाः) 12. 330. 32; in the stanzas of the Sāmaveda, as in the other three Vedas and many other texts, many names of Bhagavān have been enumerated by the great sages (ऋग्वेदे सयजुर्वेदे तथै-वाथर्वसामसु । … बहूनि मम नामानि कीर्तितानि महर्षिभिः) 12. 328. 8. B. Sing-ing of सामन् as daily routine: The आश्रम of Dadhīca on the other bank of Sarasvatī hummed with the sound of bees as with the chantings of सामन्- singers (षट्पदोद्गीत-निनदैर् विघुष्ट्ं सामगैर् इव) 3. 98. 13; on the Gandhamādana mountain the Pāṇḍavas could hear the sound of the songs and of the clapping of hands (by the Gandharvas and the Kiṃpuruṣas) which sounded like the melody of the सामन् chants (गीतानां तलतालानां यथा साम्नां च निस्वनः) 3. 155. 84; the precincts of the आश्रम of Upamanyu resounded with the auspicious melodies of सामन्-singers (शुभैः सामगानां च वीर) 13. 14. 35. C. Employment in sacrifices: In the Rājasūya of Yudhiṣṭhira the six fires were piled up with the chanting of सामन् by those who had observed the vows (साम्ना षडग्नयो यस्मिंश् चीयन्ते संशितव्रतैः) 2. 12. 13; in this sacrifice Susāman, the chief of the Dhanaṃjayas, acted as the chanter of the सामन्स् 2. 30. 34 (धनंजयानां ऋषभः सुसामा सामगो ऽभवत् । ) Nī. on Bom. Ed. 2. 33. 34: धनंजयानां धनंजयगोत्राणां म-ध्ये श्रेष्ठः सुसामा नाम आङ्गिरसः); in the sacrifice of Janaka the excellent Ukthya sāman was sung 3. 134. 36; Bhīṣma told Yudhiṣṭhira that in a sacrifice the सामन्-singers praise employing the Rathantara melody (रथन्तरे सामगाश् च स्तुवन्ति) 13. 143. 15; Ṛṣi Gṛtsamada told Yudhiṣṭhira that once, when Indra's long sacrificial session lasting for a thousand years was in progress, Vasiṣṭha, the son of Manu Cākṣuṣa, found fault the way Gṛtsamada was singing the Rathantara chant; Vasiṣṭha asked Gṛtsamada to set his jubilation aside and again think over what he had done (रथन्तरं द्विज-श्रेष्ठ न सम्यग् इति वर्तते । समीक्षस्व पुनर् बुद्ध्या हर्षं त्यक्त्वा द्विजोत्तम); (he charged Gṛtsamada that by his in-correct singing he had committed a sin which would not carry the sacrifice to the gods; for this fault Gṛtsamada was cursed to be a deer) 13. 18. 15-17; Vālmīki told Yudhi-ṣṭhira that in a certain dispute regarding सामन् (-chanting) the sages pronounced the judgement that Vasiṣṭha had incurred the sin of killing a Brāhmaṇa and he was instantly seized by that sin (वीवादे साम्नि मुनिभिर् ब्रह्मघ्नो वै भवान् इति । उक्तः क्षणेन चाविष्टस् तेनाधर्मेण भारत) 13. 18. 7. Trita, when he wanted to offer a sacrifice in the well, thought of ऋच्स्, यजुसेस् and सामन्स् for using them in the rites 9. 35. 33; in the metaphorical sacrifice (संग्रामयज्ञ 12. 99. 12) performed by a warrior (i. e. in a war) the words ‘cut, break’ uttered by the fighters in a war serve the purpose of the सामन्स् chanted by the सामन्- singers in the abode of Yama (cf. the next section D) (छिन्धि भिन्धीति यस्यैतच् छ्रूयते वाहिनी-मुखे । सामानि सामगास् तस्य गायन्ति यमसादने) 12. 99. 22; सामन्स् were sung when formerly animals were bound for god Nārāyaṇa—this is mentioned in the ऋच्स् recited by those who know Nārāyaṇa and these are cited as an instance (ऋचश् चाप्य् अत्र शंसन्ति नारायणविदो जनाः नारा-यनाय देवाय यद् अब्दह्नन् पशून् पुरा ॥ तत्र सामानि गायन्ति तानि चाहुर् निदर्श-नम् ॥ ) 14. 25. 16-17 (see however Nī. cited under ऋच् p. 175. 2 above). D. Employ-ment in funeral rites: When the Pāṇḍavas set out for the forest Dhaumya, their Puro-hita, accompanied them chanting on the way the terrible सामन्स् addressed to Yama and holding in his hand कुश grass directed to-wards the Nairṛtya direction (धौम्यो याम्यानि सामानि रौद्राणि च विशां पते । गायन् गच्छति मार्गेषु कुशान् आदाय पाणिना ॥ ) 2. 71. 7 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 2. 80. 7: याम्यानि यमदैवत्यानि); (कृत्वा तु नैरृतान् दर्भान् धीरो धौम्यः पुरो-हितः । सामानि गायन् याम्यानि पुरतो याति भारत) 2. 71. 21 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 2. 80. 22: नैरृतान् निरृतिकोणगान्); he thereby wanted to indicate that when the Bhāratas will be killed in the war the priests of the Kurus will similarly chant the सामन्स् (addressed to Yama) 2. 71. 22; at the cremation of Droṇa the सामन्-singers sang three सामन्स् when his body was placed on the funeral pyre (द्रोणम् आधाय गायन्ति त्रीणि सामानि सामगाः) 11. 23. 38; when the pyre was lit, others followed them reciting the three सामन्स् in subdued voices (see Cr. Ed. Vol. 12. p. 119 note on 11. 23. 41) (सामभिस् त्रिभिर् अन्तःस्थैर् अनुशंसन्ति चापरे । अग्नाव् अग्निम् इवाधाय द्रोणं हुत्वा हुताशने) 11. 23. 41; सामन्स् were sung at the Pitṛ-medha rites of some of those fallen in the war; due to the sound of the सामन्स् and the ऋच्स्, as also due to the lamentations of women, all beings were stupefied during the night (पितृ-मेधाश् च केषांचिद् अवर्तन्त महात्मनाम् । सामभिश् चाप्य् अगायन्त … ॥ साम्नां ऋचां च नादेन स्त्रीणां च रुदितस्वनैः । कश्म-लं सर्वभूतानां निशायाम् समपद्यत) 11. 26. 39-40; at the Pitṛmedha rites of Bhīṣma the सामन्-singers sang the chants 13. 154. 12; during the Pitṛmedha rites, at the cremation of Vasudeva, when the funeral pyre was lit there was a loud sound produced by the सामन्-singers (सामगानां च निर्घोषः) 16. 8. 23, 25-26. E. Use in the praise of deities: (1) Indra: Arjuna saw Indra praised by excellent द्विजस् with praises consisting of ऋच्स्, यजुसेस् and सामन्स् 3. 44. 18; when Arjuna and Indra sat on the same throne, Gandharvas led by Tumburu, skilled in songs and chants, sang गाथास् in very agreeable melody (तत्र स्म गाथा गायन्ति साम्ना परमवल्गुना । गन्धर्वास् तुम्बु-रुश्रेष्ठाः कुशला गीतसामसु) 3. 44. 28; (2) Kubera: On the Gandhamādana mountain the sound of सामन्- singing by Tumburu, who waits on Dhanada (Kubera) was heard on the junctions of the four changes of the moon (पर्वसधिषु) 3. 156. 28; (3) Śiva: Upamanyu in his praise of Śiva said that the god was sung with chants by the सामन्-singers (सामभिर् यं च गायन्ति सामगाः शुद्धबुद्धयः) 13. 16. 49; Śatakratu (Indra) and Viṣṇu (who are the two sons of Aditi), and god Brahman sing the Rathantara melody near Bhava (Śiva) (शत-क्रतुस् च भगवान् विष्णुश् चादितिनन्दनौ । ब्रह्मा रथन्तरं साम ईरयन्ति भावा-न्तिके) 13. 15. 16; (however, the Editor's note, Cr. Ed. Vol. 17, p. 1061 on 13. 15. 16, says: अदितिनन्दनौ = Mitra and Varuṇa ?) (4) Deity not named: in the south, in the bowers of Mandara mountain and in the houses of the Viprarṣis, the Gandharvas sing enchanting गाथास् sung in different melodies (गन्ध-र्वा गान्ति गाथा वै चित्तबुद्धिहरा द्विज । अत्र सामानि गाथाभिः श्रुत्वा गीतानि ॥ ) 5. 107. 9-10. F. Importance: While des-cribing his विभूतिस्, Bhagavān told Arjuna that he was the Bṛhatsāman chant among the melodies (बृहत्साम् तथा साम्नाम्) 6. 32. 35; Bhīṣma praised Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa, who is sung in सामन्स् that are true, as one whose actions are true and who is truth (यं … गृणन्ति सत्यकर्माणं सत्यं सत्येषु सामसु) 12. 47. 16 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 12. 47. 26: गृणन्ति ध्यायन्ति सत्यम् अबा-धितं सत्येषु अबाधितार्थेषु सामसु ज्येष्ठसामादिषु). G. Personfication: The Sāmans along with the Yajuses and the Ṛgveda, in bodily form, attended the sacrifice of Mahādeva (Śiva) who had assumed the form of Varuṇa (मूर्तिमन्ति च सामानि यजूंषि च सहस्रश्ः । ऋग्वेदश् चागमत् तत्र) 13. 85. 4, (देवस्य महतस् तात वारुणीं बिभ्रतस् तनुम्) 13. 85. 2, (आज-ग्मुः … यज्ञं पशुपतेः प्रीता वरुणस्य महात्मनः) 13. 85. 7-8. H. Mystic interpretation: The Yakṣa asked Yudhi-ṣṭhira: “What is the one सामन् suited for sacrifice ?” Yudhiṣṭhira replied: “Prāṇa is the one सामन् suited for sacrifice” (किम् एकम् यज्ञियं साम) 3. 297. 34, (प्राणो वै यज्ञियं साम) 3. 297. 35; Bhīṣma declared to Yudhiṣṭhira: There was but one सामन् (एकं साम) 12. 60. 45 (Nī. on 12. 60 47: अकारो वै सर्वा वाक् सैषा स्पर्शोष्म-भिर् व्यज्यमाना भवी नानारूपा भवतीति श्रुतेर् एकं अकाररूपम् एव अक्षरं यथा सामादिरूपं) I. Relationship with Yugas: According to Hanūmant there were neither सामन्स्, यजुसेस् nor ऋच्स् in the Kṛtayuga (नासन् कृतयुगे तात … न साम-यजुऋग्वर्णाः) 3. 148. 12-13 (See Nīla-kaṇṭha on this passage cited under Yajus p. 207. 1; for such other information common to ऋच्स् and यजुसेस् see Ṛc, especially 3. 27. 3; 5. 43. 1-3; 5. 44. 21; 6. 31. 17; 12. 52. 22; 12. 60. 42; 12. 194. 8; 12. 199. 16-18; 12. 224. 63; 12. 227. 1; 12. 230. 8; 12. 243. 2; 12. 260. 26, 36; 12. 297. 15; 12. 322. 37). [See Sāmaveda]
सामवेद: Sāmaveda m.: Name of one of the four Vedic Saṃhitās. A. Relationship with Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa: Nārāyaṇa told the sage Mārkaṇḍeya that the Sāmaveda, along with the other three Vedas, arise from him and enter into him (मत्तः प्रादुर्भवन्त्य् एते माम् एव प्रविशन्ति च) 3. 187. 14. B. Importance: (1) In the Vibhūtiyoga of the Gītā, Bhagavān told Arjuna that he was the Sāmaveda of the (four) Vedas (वेदानाम् सामवेदो ऽस्मि) 6. 32. 22; (2) Upamanyu, in his praise of Śiva, described Śiva as the Sāmaveda of the (four) Vedas (सामवेदश् च वेदानाम्) 13. 14. 159; (3) The धर्म of the एका-न्तिन्स् (12. 336. 7, 57), expounded by Nārada for the benefit of Yudhiṣṭhira, was equal to the Sāmaveda and was preserved by god Nārāyaṇa himself (गहनो ह्य् एष धर्मो वै … संमितः सामवेदेन । धार्यते स्वयम् ईशेन राजन् नारायणेन ह ॥ ) (12. 336. 9-10); this धर्म was learnt and taught by Brahman to the Barhiṣad sages from whom it went to a द्विज called Jyeṣṭha who was versed in the Sāmaveda (अऋहीतो ब्रह्मणा राजन् … अध्यापिताश् च मुनयो नाम्ना बर्हिषदो नृप ॥ बर्हिष-द्भ्यश् च संक्रान्तः सामवेदान्तगं द्विजम् । ज्येष्ठं नाम्नाभिविख्यातम् … ) 12. 336. 41-42. C. Personified: (1) Sāmaveda, along with the Ṛgveda and the Purāṇas, moved in front of the chariot of Śiva when he got ready to destroy the Tripuras 8. 24. 80; (2) Sāmaveda, along with the other three Vedas, visit the Sabhā of Brahmadeva 2. 11. 23. D. Limita-tions: Dhṛtarāṣṭra asked Sanatsujāta whether one who committed sin was absolved of it if he studied the Sāmaveda (and the ऋच्स् and यजुसेस्) 5. 43. 1 (the reply was in the negative 5. 43. 2). [See Sāman]
सारस्वत: Sārasvata nt.: Name of the 77th पर्वन् in the list of a hundred sub-पर्वन्स् of the Bhārata supposed to have been made by Vyāsa in the Parvasaṃgraha 1. 2. 60, 33, 70. Described as detailing the merits of a group of तीर्थस् (तीर्थवंशगुणान्वित) 1. 2. 60; referred to while listing the contents of the Śalyaparvan as one in which was describ-ed the holiness of river Sarasvatī and of the तीर्थस् (सरस्वत्याश् च तीर्थानां पुण्यता परिकीर्तिता) 1. 2. 175; related to the अध्यायस् 9. 29-53 (called Tīrthayātrā-parvan in the colophon; actually this पर्वन् precedes the Gadāyuddhaparvan and does not follow it as stated in 1. 2. 60 (गदायुद्धम् अतः परम् । सारस्वतं ततः पर्व) and in 1. 2. 175).

Sārasvata m. (pl.): Name of a people. According to the report of Saṃjaya to Dhṛtarāṣṭra before the war, Nakula was supposed to fight against Ulūka and the Sārasvata hordes (उलूकं चापि कैतव्यं ये च सारस्वता गणाः । नकुलःकल्पयाम् आस भागं … ) 5. 56. 23.
सावित्री: Sāvitrī1 f.: Name of a मन्त्र (ṚV, 3. 62. 10) so called because it is related to god Savitṛ; also called Gāyatrī (3. 83. 27: 6. 5. 18-19) because the मन्त्र is composed in the Gāyatrī metre. A. Description: holy (पुण्या) 6. 5. 18; best (उत्तमा) 13. 145. 27; having all quali-ties (सर्वगुणान्विता) 6. 5. 18; enabling the reciter to get over difficult situations (दुर्ग-तरणी) 2. 11. 25; highly honoured in the worlds (लोकसंमता) 6. 5. 18. B. Im-portance and significance: Sāvitrī was con-sidered to be the beginning of all sciences (आदिर् इष्यते । सावित्री सर्वविद्यानाम्) 14. 44. 4-5; the nineteen classes of beings (7 ग्राम्य पशुस्, 7 आरण्य पशुस्, 5 उद्-भिज्जस्) and the five महाभूतस्, which make a total of twenty-four are identi-fied with (the twenty-four syllables of) the Gāyatrī (एषां विंशतिर् एकोना महाभूतेषु पञ्चसु । चतुर्विंशतिर् उद्दिष्टा गायत्री लोकसंमता ॥ ) 6. 5. 15-18. C. Its close association with the Vedas used for a simile: As the Sāvitrī मन्त्र does not forsake the Vedas, so did Yājñasenī (Drau-padī) not forsake the Pāṇḍavas 3. 80. 4. D. Relationship with deities: (1) Savitṛ: Sāvitrī was (first) pronounced in the east by god Savitṛ to the ब्रह्मवादिन्स् 5. 106. 10; 3. 110. 5 (? सावित्रीं सविता यथा (ददौ)); (2) Nārāyaṇa: On the Śveta Dvīpa, Nārada saw ओंकार, followed by Sāvitrī, coming out of the mouth of Nārāyaṇa 12. 326. 7; (3) Śiva: when Rudra got ready to destroy the Tripuras he made the Vedas his bow and the Sāvitrī मन्त्र his bow-string 13 145. 27; E. Personification: (1) Sāvitrī, in bodily form, present in the Sabhā of Brahmadeva 2. 11. 25; Sāvitrī, along with the Vedas and the Upaniṣads attended the sacrifice of Śiva when he had assumed the form of Varuṇa 13. 85. 6. F. Uses: (1) In श्राद्ध: One should atten-tively recite the Sāvitrī prayer at each oblation given to the manes at the श्राद्ध (ब्रूयाच् छ्राद्धे च सावित्रीं पिण्डे पिण्डे समा-हितः) 13. 92. 14; (cf. Śāṅkh Gṛ. Sū. 4. 1. 8 for a slightly different use: भुञ्जानेषु महाव्याहृतीः सावित्रीम् मधुवातीयाः पितृ-देवत्याः पावमानीश् च जपेत्); (2) for use as a test (?): If a person born of a mixture of castes recites Gāyatrī at the renowned तीर्थ called Gāyatryāḥ sthānam it sounds like a गाथा (a non-Vedic stanza) or an ordinary song. This was a direct proof available for a Brāhmaṇa to prove that he was not of mixed origin (निदर्शनं च प्रत्यक्षं ब्राह्-मणानां नराधिप । गायत्रीं पठते यस् तु योनिसंकरजस् तथा । गाथा वा गीतिका वापि तस्य संपद्यते नृप ॥ Nī., however, on Bom. Ed. 3. 85. 29: निदर्शानम् उदा-हरणम्); (3) As a benediction: Jāmbavatī invoked Sāvitrī mantra for the protection of Kṛṣṇa when he set out for the Himavant to meet Śiva (सावित्री ब्रह्मविद्या च ऋतवो वत्सराः क्षपाः । … रक्षन्तु सर्वत्र गतं त्वाम् यादव सुखावहम् ॥ 13. 14. 22-23). G. Qualifications and rewards obtained by its knowledge and recitation: Brāhmaṇas who know Sāvitrī, so also the one who recites Sāvitrī three times a day, are worthy of being invited for a श्राद्ध (सावित्रीज्ञाः क्रिया-वन्तस् ते राजन् केतनक्षमाः) 13. 24. 25, (सावित्रीं जपते यस् तु त्रिकालम् … स राजन् केतनक्षमः) 13. 24. 28; one who recites Sāvitrī on a sacred spot, eating limited food, not injuring others, alert (? अमन्दकः), not talking to any one is freed of all sins 12. 36. 33 (Nī., however, on Bom. Ed. 12. 35. 37: मन्द इव मन्दकः रागद्वेषमानाप-मानशून्यः); one who knows the real nature of Gāyatrī (i. e. the identification of its 24 syllables with 19 kinds of beings and 5 महाभूतस्) is never deprived of the world due to him (य एतां वेद गायत्रीं … तत्त्वेन भरतश्रेष्ठ स लोकान् न प्रण-श्यति) 6. 5. 19. [See Sāvitrī2, Bhārata-sāvitrī]

Sāvitrī2 f.: Name of a मन्त्र related to god Savitṛ. The मन्त्र is recited in the ceremony to be performed after the birth of a child and before cutting the navel string; at that time the Sāvitrī mantra is the child's mother and the teacher is its father (प्राङ्नाभिवर्ध-नात् पुंसो जातकर्म विधीयते । तत्रास्य माता सावित्री पिता त्व् आचार्य उच्यते) 3. 177. 29 (cf. Āśva. Gṛ. Sū. 1. 15. 1: प्र ते ददामि मधुनो घृतस्य वेदं सवित्रा प्रसूतं मघोनाम् । आयुष्मान् गुप्तो देवताभिह् शतं जीव शरदो लोके अस्मिन्; Śāṅkh. Gṛ. Sū. 1. 24. 4: प्र ते यच्छामि मधु-मन् मखाय वेदं प्रसूतं सवित्रा मघोना । … ). [See Sāvitrī1]

Sāvitrī°3: Name of an Upākhyāna. Mentioned in the contents of the Āraṇyakaparvan (सावित्र्यौद्दालकीयं च) 1. 2. 126; related to the अध्यायस् 3. 277-283 (occurs as a section of the Draupadīharaṇa-parvan).
सुनीथ: Sunītha m.: Name of a मन्त्र (? or of a sage ?) 1. 53. 23. One who brings to mind the Sunītha मन्त्र along with Asita and Ārtimant need have no fear from serpents either by day or at night 1. 53. 23 (असितं चार्तिमन्तं च सुनीथम् चापि यः स्मरेत् । दिवा वा यदि वा रात्रौ नास्य सर्पभयं भवेत्); cf. Nī. on Bom. Ed. 1. 58. 23 cited under Asita on p. 169 above. [See Asita, Ārtimant]
सुन्दोपसुन्दयोर्: Sundopasundayor upākhyānam nt.: Designation of an उपाख्यान। Mentioned in the list of the contents of the Ādiparvan (सुन्दोपसुन्दयोस् तत्र उपा-ख्यानं प्रकीर्तितम्) 1. 2. 90; related to the अध्यायस् 1. 201-204.
सुभद्राहरण: Subhadrāharaṇa nt.: Name of the 17th पर्वन् in the list of a hundred sub-पर्वन्स् of the Bhārata supposed to have been made by Vyāsa in the Parvasaṃgraha 1. 2. 38, 33, 70. Referred to in the list of the contents of the Ādiparvan as ‘where at Dvārakā the loving Subhadrā was obtained by Kirīṭin (Arjuna), who longed for her, with the consent of Vāsudeva’ 1. 2. 92; the incident is mentioned by Dhṛtarāṣṭra in his summary of the events made for Saṃjaya 1. 1. 103 and by Vaiśaṃpāyana in his summary made for Janamejaya 1. 55. 32-34.
सौकन्य: Saukanya nt.: Name of an आख्यान। Mentioned while listing the contents of the Āraṇyakaparvan; in this Ākhyāna we are told that the sage Cyavana of the Bhṛgu family enabled the Nāsatyā (the Aśvinā) to have a share in Soma in the sacrifice of Śaryāti and in return the deities conferred youth on the sage. 1. 2. 117-118; related to the अध्यायस् 3. 122-125.
सौप्तिक: Sauptika1 nt.: Name of the 78th पर्वन् in the list of a hundred sub-पर्वन्स् of the Bhārata supposed to have been made by Vyāsa in the Parvasaṃgraha 1. 2. 60, 33, 70. Described as disgusting (बीभत्स) 1. 2. 60; referred to in the summary of the events made by Dhṛtarāṣṭra for Saṃjaya 1. 1. 153; related to the अध्यायस् 10. 1-9.

Sauptika2 nt.: Name of the tenth पर्वन् among the eighteen major पर्वन्स् of the Bhārata 1. 2. 178, 188. Described as dreadful (दारुण) 1. 2. 178; its contents are summarized as follows: where Duryodhana, whose thighs were broken, was approached after the Pāṇḍavas had left, by Kṛtavarman, Kṛpa and Drauṇi (Aśvatthāman); where the enraged Drauṇi vowed that he would not take off his armour unless he had killed all the Pāñcālas led by Dhṛṣtadyumna and the Pāṇḍavas with their house attendants (अहत्वा सर्वपाञ्चालान् धृष्टद्युम्नपुरोगमान् । पाण्डवांश् च सहामात्यान् न विमोक्ष्यामि दंशनम्) 1. 2. 180; where the trio, led by Drauṇi, killed the Pāñcālas and their attendants while they were confidently asleep at night; where the five Pāṇḍavas and Sātyaki were saved as they were protected by the might of Kṛṣṇa (कृष्णबलाश्रयात् 1. 2. 182) and all the rest perished; where Draupadī, grieved by the death of her sons, and pained at the killing of her father and brothers, resolved to fast unto death; where, at the instance of Draupadī, Bhīma pursued Aśvatthāman; where Aśvatthāman, afraid of Bhīmasena, released the missile (Brahmaśiras) against him saying it was for the destruction of the Pāṇḍava’ (अपाण्डवायेति रुषा द्रौणिर् अस्त्रम् अवासृजत् 1. 2. 185); but Kṛṣṇa, wanting to neutralize (the effect of) those words said ‘let that not happen’ (मैवम् इत्य् अब्रवीत् कृष्णः शमयंस् तस्य तद् वचः 1. 2. 186); whereupon Phālguna (Arjuna) neutralized Aśvatthāman's missile by his missile (Brahmaśiras) (यत्रास्त्रम् अस्त्रेण च तच् छमयाम् आस फाल्गुनः 1. 2. 186); Aśvatthāman, (Kṛṣṇa) Dvai-pāyana and others uttered curses provoked by one another (द्रौणिद्वैपायनादीनां शापाश् चान्योन्यकारिताः) 1. 2. 187); where the oblations of water to all kings (killed in the war) were offered (तोयकर्माणि सर्वेषां राज्ञाम् उदकदानिके 1. 2. 187); where Pṛthā (Kuntī) narrated the birth of her son who was secretly born 1. 2. 188; the high-souled sage of infinite intelligence (Vyāsa) has declared that the Sauptika and the Aiṣilka parvans together (सौप्तिकैषीकसंबन्धे) have eighteen अध्यायस् and he has counted the श्लोकस् to be eight hundred and seventy 1. 2. 189-190; the पर्वन् (? or the incident described in it ?) is referred to by Sātyaki while blaming Kṛtavarman who, in association with the son of Droṇa (Aśvatthāman), killed those who were asleep (सौप्तिके ये च निहताः सुप्तानेन दुरात्मना ॥ द्रोणपुत्रसहायेन पापेन कृतवर्मणा) 16. 4. 25-26.
सौभवधाख्यान: Saubhavadhākhyāna nt.: Name of an आख्यान। Mentioned while listing the contents of the Āraṇyakaparvan 1. 2. 106; related to the अध्यायस् 3. 15-23.
स्तवराज: Stavarāja m.: Name (?) of a collect-ion of names (नामसंहारम् 13. 17. 1; नामसमुद्देशम् 13. 17. 12, 11) of Śiva 13. 17. 21; these are one thousand and eight names of Śarva 13. 17. 29; the names are listed in 13. 17. 30-150. A. Original composer and transmission: Originally Brahmā sang the Stava (यत् पुरा लोककृज् जगौ) 13. 16. 66; यद् उक्तं पद्मयोनिना 13. 17. 12) and himself preserved the Stava of Bhagavān (Śiva) (स्तवम् एतं भगवतो ब्रह्मा स्वयम् अधारयत्) 13. 17. 164; 13. 17. 154; 13. 17. 5; 13. 16. 66; from him it went successively to Śakra (Indra) and others 13. 17. 164-168; one of the receivers in this line was Taṇḍi who obtained it in the abode of Brahman after he had performed severe austerities 13. 17. 165; he handed it over to Śukra Bhārgava 13. 16. 66; 13. 16. 75 (?); at the end of the line of transmission stood Mārkaṇḍeya who taught it to Upamanyu when the latter had observed certain rules (मार्कण्डेयान् मया प्राप्तं नियमेन जनार्दन 13. 17. 169) and Upamanyu gave it to Janārdana (Kṛṣṇa) 13. 17. 168-169; 13. 17. 1, 5-6; since, in bygone days, it was once taught by Taṇḍi it also came to be looked upon as composed by Taṇḍi; moreover Taṇḍi had brought it down from heaven to this world (यस्मात् तण्डिः पुरा प्राह तेन तण्डिकृतो ऽभवत् । स्वर्गाच् चैवात्र भूलोकं तण्डिना ह्य् अवतारि-तः ॥ ) 13. 17. 22; 13. 16. 66. 75; 13. 17. 3; the Stavarāja was brought down (to this world) from the Brahmaloka 13. 17. 21, 4; Upamanyu is also said to have received it directly from Taṇḍi (तण्डिर् आख्यातवान् मम । नामानि) 13. 16. 73, 72. B. Activity of Upamanyu: Pitāmaha (Brahmadeva) had mentioned ten thousand names of Sarva (Śiva) in the Vedas and one thousand names of Śarva (Śiva) in the Śāstras (दश नामसहस्राणि वेदेष्व् आह पितामहः । शर्वस्य शास्त्रेषु तथा दश नामशतानि वै ॥ ) 13. 16. 74; 13. 17. 13; Upamanyu made an abridgement (in the form of Stavarāja) out of the ten thousand names as one churns घृत from curds (नाम्नां कंचित् समुद्देशं वक्ष्ये ह्य् अव्यक्तयोनिनः … दश नामसकस्राणि यान्य् आह प्रपितामहः । तानि निर्मथ्य मनसा दध्नो घृतम् इवोद्धृतम्) 13. 17. 11, 13. (for other similes cf. 13. 17. 14); Upa-manyu gave to Kṛṣṇa this form of the स्तव, which constituted Mahādeva's (Śiva's) चरित, having fewer words (and syllables) and being concise in meaning (किं तु दे-वस्य महतः संक्षिप्तार्थपदाक्षरम् । शक्तितश् चरितं वक्ष्ये) 13. 17. 9; this abridged form looked upon as the essence of the original (तथैतत् सारम् उद्धृतम्) 13. 17. 14. C. Its name: After its composition Brahmā destined it to be the king of all the divine स्तवस्; since then it came to be known as Stavarāja of Īśvara (सर्वस्तवानां दिव्यानां राजत्वे समकल्पयत् ॥ तदाप्रभृति चैवायम् ईश्व-रस्य महात्मनः । स्तवराजेति वीख्यातः) 13. 17. 20-21. D. Description: The best of all स्तवस् (स्तवानाम् उत्तमं स्तवम्) 13. 17. 19, 23; famous (विश्रुत) 13. 17. 169; excellent (प्रवर) 13. 17. 4; of the first rank (प्रथम) 13. 17. 4; associated with the four vedas (चतुर्वेद-समन्वित) 13. 17. 15; means of purifying (पावन) 13. 17. 15; (पवित्र) 13. 17. 19; destroyer of all sins (सर्वपापामापह) 13. 17. 15; (सर्वपापप्रणाशन) 13. 17. 23; killer of demons (रक्षोघ्न) 13. 17. 15; auspicious (मङ्गल) 13. 17. 19; holy (शुभ) 13. 17. 4; the best among auspicious (सर्वमङ्गलमङ्गल्य) 13. 17. 23; holy (पुण्य) 13. 17. 19; most beneficial (कल्याणम् उत्तमम्) 13. 17. 19; leading to heaven (स्वर्ग्य) 13. 17. 4, 169; giving calmness of mind (शान्तिद) 13. 17. 15; con-ferring health (आरोग्य), long life (आयुष्य), wealth (धन्य) and strength (बल्य) 13. 17. 169; conferring welfare (पौष्टिक) 13. 17. 15; beneficial to all beings (सर्वभूत-हित) 13. 17. 4; looked upon as the highest ब्रह्मन् (परमं ब्रह्म) 13. 17. 154; 13. 16. 66, as eternal ब्रह्मन् (ब्रह्म सना-तनम्) 13. 17. 6. E. Importance: This Stavarāja is equal to meditation, practice of Yoga, the best thing to meditate on; it deserves to be recited; it is itself knowledge and the highest secret; if one knows it even at the end of one's life one can attain the highest state after life (इदं ध्यानम् इदं योगम् इदं ध्येयम् अनुत्तमम् । इदं जप्यम् इदं ज्ञानं रहस्यम् इदम् उत्तमम् । इदं ज्ञात्वान्तकाते ऽपि गच्छेद् धि परमां गतिम् ॥ ) 13. 17. 18; this great, eternal secret was proclaimed by Brahman himself (यत् तद् रहस्यं पर-मं ब्रब्मप्रोक्तं सनातनम्) 13. 17. 5. F. Who may receive the Stavarāja: It may be taught to one who is devoted (to god), to one who has faith, and one who believes in god; but it should not be taught to a non-believer who is lack of faith in the bodily form and who has not controlled his self (इदं भक्ताय दातव्यं श्रद्दधानास्ति-काय च । नाश्रद्दधानरूपाय नास्तिकाया-जितामने) 13. 17. 16 (Unknown commenta-tor: वेदबोधितफलावश्यंभावनिश्चयः श्रद्धा । वेदाः प्रमाणम् इति ज्ञानवान् आस्तिकः । उक्तविपरीतो नास्तिकः Cr. Ed. 17(2). 1062. on 13. 17. 6); it should not be taught to one who scorns god Pinākin (Śiva); such a person goes to hell with his ancestors and descendants 13. 17. 17; it should be learnt with due effort and then be preserved by one who has controlled his mind (प्रयत्नेनाध्-इगन्तव्यं धार्यं च प्रयतात्मना) 13. 17. 15. G. Rewards obtained: By listen-ing to the name of Śarva listed in the Stava-rāja one obtains all desires 13. 17. 29; by reciting this Stava the sage Kṛṣṇadvaipāyana obtained all his desires while he was practis-ing austerities on mount Meru for a son; he therefore advised Yudhiṣṭhira to recite the स्तव so that he would also obtain all his desires by the grace of Maheśvara 13. 18. 1-3; by praising Śiva with the names in this स्तव one obtains one's Self (प्राप्नोत्य् आत्मानम् आत्मना) 13. 17. 153; god Mahādeva is pleased by the recitation of his names and he establishes his devotees in himself (भक्ता-नुकम्पी भगवान् आत्मसंस्थान् करोति तान्) 13. 17. 155; by its recitation a person who is cleansed of his sins becomes devoted to Bhava (Śiva) which (devotion) leads him to attain the highest perfection (जन्तोर् विशुद्धपापस्य भवे भक्तिः प्रजायते । … तस्यैव च प्रसादेन भक्तिर् उत्पद्यते नृणाम् । यया याति परां सिद्धिम्) 13. 17. 158, 160; the demons, the Yakṣas, the Rākṣasas, the Piśācas, the Yātudhānas, the Guhyakas and the snakes do not put obstacle in the way (of one who recites this स्तव) 13. 17. 170; he who observing rules of purity and celibacy, with controlled sense-organs, recites this स्तव for one year with-out a break in application obtains the fruit of performing an Aśvamedha sacrifice (यः पठेत शुचिर् भूत्वा ब्रह्मचारी जितेन्द्रि-यः । अभग्नयोगो वर्षं तु सोऽ श्वमेध-फलं लभेत् ॥ ) 13. 17. 171; by praising god Mahādeva with the names (in this Stava) Jāmadagnya, who was afflicted by the sin of killing his father and the Brāhmaṇas (? पितृविप्रवधेनाहम् आर्तः;) 13. 18. 10 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 13. 18. 12: पितृ-तुल्या विप्राः ‘ज्येष्ठो भ्राता पितुः समः’ इति स्मृतेर् ज्येष्ठा भ्रातरस् तेषां वधेन), was freed of the sin; in addition the god gave him an axe and divine missiles and made him invincible; god of death would not over-power Jāmadagnya and he would be famous 13. 18. 9-12 (पापं न भविता ते ऽद्य अजेयश् च भविष्यसि । न ते प्रभविता मृत्युर् यशस्वी च भविष्यसि ॥ 12).
स्त्रीपर्वन्: Strīparvan1 nt.: Name of the 81st पर्वन् in the list of a hundred sub-पर्वन्स् of the Bhārata supposed to have been made by Vyāsa in the Parvasaṃgraha 1. 2. 61, 33, 70. Referred to among the contents of the major Strīparvan 1. 2. 191-192; related to the अध्यायस् 11. 9-25 (or 1-25 if one includes the Viśokaparvan mentioned in the colophon at the end of the eighth अध्याय 11. 1-8). [See Strīparvan2]

Strīparvan2 nt.: Name of the eleventh पर्वन् among the eighteen major पर्वन्स् of the Bhārata 1. 2. 191, 194. Described as one in which one finds the rise of compassion (करुणोदय) 1. 2. 191 and one which is very pitiful (अतिकरुणम् महत्) 1. 2. 194; the author of Bhāratākh-yāna has so composed it as to cause distress to the hearts of good people and make them shed tears (सज्जनमनोवैक्लव्याश्रुप्रवर्तक) 1. 2. 195; the contents of the पर्वन् are summarized as follows: where one finds the highly pitiful lamentation of the wives of the (fallen) heroes and the upsurge of anger and the tranquility of mind of Dhṛtarāṣṭra and Gāndhārī respy. (क्रोधावेशः प्रसादश् च गान्धारीधृतराष्ट्रयोः 1. 2. 191); where one saw those brave Kṣatriyas who would not turn back and who were destined to die, sons, brothers, fathers-killed in battle (यत्र तान् क्षत्रियाञ् शूरान् दिष्टान्तान् अनिवर्तिनः । पुत्रान् भ्रातॄन् पितॄंश् चैव ददृशुर् निहतान् रणे 1. 2. 192); where the king, excellent among all those who upheld the law (viz. Yudhiṣṭhira 11. 26. 24-26), ordered cremation of kings to be done in accordance with the prescribed rites (शास्त्रतः) 1. 2. 191-193; the number of the अध्यायस् in this पर्वन् is said to be twentyseven, and the number of श्लोकस् seven hundred and seventy five 1. 2. 194-195. [See Strīparvan1]
स्वर्गपर्वन्: Svargaparvan nt.: Name of the eighteenth पर्वन् among the eighteen major पर्वन्स् of the Bhārata 1. 2. 232-233 (अश्ता-दशैवम् एतानि पर्वाण्य् उक्तान्य् अशेषतः). Described as heavenly (दिव्य) and super-human (अमानुष) 1. 2. 232; its अध्यायस् are counted to be five and श्लोकस् two hundred 1. 2. 232. [See Svargārohaṇika with which this is identical]
स्वर्गारोहणिक: Svargārohaṇika nt.: Name of the 98th पर्वन् in the list of a hundred sub-पर्वन्स् of the Bhārata supposed to have been made by Vyāsa for the Parvasaṃgraha 1. 2. 68 [See Svargaparvan with which this is identical]
सप्तर्षि: Saptarṣi m.: (pl.): The seven stars forming the constellation Ursa Major. A. Description: lofty (उदार) 6. 3. 24. B. Placement in the sky: Suparṇa told Gālava that the place of the Seven Sages was in the north (अत्र (i. e. उत्तरायां दिशि 5. 109. 3) ते ऋषयः सप्त) 5. 109. 12; Mārkaṇḍeya, while instructing Yudhiṣṭhira, told him that to honour the old injunction laid down by Brahman the Saptarṣis shine in the sky; hence no one should violate the injunction considering himself to be strong (धात्रा विधिर् यो विहितः पुराणस् तं पूजयन्तो नरवर्य सन्तः । सप्तर्षयः पार्थ दिवि प्रभान्ति नेशे बलस्येति चरेद् अधर्मम्) 3. 26. 13. C. Auspicious in wars: Bhīṣma told Yudhiṣṭhira that the soldiers in the army, while fighting, should keep the constellation Ursa Major at the back and remain steady like mountains; this way one could wish to win even the unconquerable opponents (सप्तर्षीन् पृष्ठ-तः कृत्वा युध्येरन्न् अचला इव । अनेन विधिना राजञ् जिगीषेतापि दुर्जयान्) 12. 101. 16. D. Omens: Among the omens noticed by Vyāsa before the war one was related to the position of the two planets having copper-red and ruddy crests (Rāhu and Ketu ?) who obscured the brilliance of the lofty stars of the Ursa Major (ग्रहौ ताम्रारुणशिखौ प्रज्वलन्ताव् इव स्थितौ । सप्तर्षीणाम् उदाराणां समवच्छाद्य वै प्रभाम्) 6. 3. 24. E. Similes: (1) The sages in the आश्रम of Tanu sat around the king, father of Bhūridyumna, placing him in front as do the stars of the constellation Ursa Major the Polar star (ततस् ते मुनयः सर्वे परिवार्य नरर्-षभम् । उपाविशन् पुरस्कृत्य सप्तर्षय इव ध्रुवम् ॥ ) 12. 126. 25; (2) The Brāhmaṇa instructed his wife that there was only one relative, no other; he dwelt in our heart; (in saying this) the Brāhmaṇa was only repeating what the relative within had said to him: instructed by the relative within people have relatives; they shine (like ?) the stars of the Ursa Major (एको बन्धुर् नास्ति ततो द्वितीयो यो हृच्छयस् तम् अहम् अनु-ब्रवीमि । तेनानुशिष्टा बान्धवा बन्धुमन्-तः सप्तर्षयः सप्त दिवि प्रभान्ति) 14. 26. 3. [For Saptarṣi also see Section 1. 7]
सिनीवाली: Sinīvālī f.: Name of the first Amāvā-syā day (when the Amāvāsyā extends to two days (see Ait. Br. 32. 9: या पूर्वामा-वास्या सा सिनीवाली योत्तरा सा कुहूः; also cf. Nirukta 11. 31). A. Personification: Personified as the third daughter of Aṅgiras, of matted hair; on account of her thinness people said that she vanished no sooner she was seen (यां कपर्दिसुताम् आहुर् दृश्यादृश्येति देहिनः । तनुत्वात् सा सिनीवालि तृतीयाङ्गिरसः सुता ॥ ) 3. 208. 5 (Nī., however, on Bom. Ed. 3. 218. 5: कपर्दिनो रुद्रस्य सुताम् इव सुतां चन्द्रकलां ललाटे धृतत्वात् । … चतुर्दशी-युक्तामावास्या सिनीवाली). B. Name of Devasenā: Brāhmaṇas called Devasenā, the chief queen of Skanda, by different names, one of them being Sinīvālī (देवसेनां … यां ब्राह्मणाः प्राहुः … सिनीवालीम्) 3. 218. 47. C. Mythological events: (1) Sinīvālī formed one of the reins (योक्त्राणी) of the chariot of Śiva when it was made ready for fight with the Tripuras 8. 24. 74; (2) she was one of those who attended the investiture (अभिषेक) of Kumāra (Skanda) 9. 44. 12.
सूर्य: Sūrya m.: Name of the planet Sun, referred to also as Āditya and by its other synonyms like Arka, Ravi, Bhāskara, Bhānu, Pataṃga. A. Origin and activity: According to Bhīṣma, Āditya, along with Candra, other planets, constellations and stars were born from Viṣvaksena (i. e. Kṛṣṇa) (चन्द्रादि-त्यौ ग्रहनक्षत्रताराः … विष्वक्सेनात् सर्वम् एतत् प्रसूतम्) 13. 143. 31; Puru-sottama (Nārāyaṇa) told the seven sages, Marīci and others, that Sūrya, Candramas, all constellations act in their own prescribed way in their respective spheres and are considered an authority (सुर्याचन्द्रमसौ  … सर्वे च नक्षत्रगणाः … अधिकारेषु वर्तन्ते यथास्वम् … सर्वे प्रमाणं हि 12. 322. 39-40. B. Description: Radiant (गभस्तिमन्त्) 2. 11. 17; (अंशुमन्त्) 6. 32. 21; rich in light (विभारसु) 6. 13. 44; very generous (परमोदार) 6. 13. 44. C. Extent: Dhṛtarāṣṭra asked Saṃjaya to tell him everything about the extent (सर्वं प्रमाणम्) of Arka, to which Saṃjaya agreed 6. 12. 3-4; according to Saṃjaya's information the diameter (विष्कम्भ) of Sūrya was 1000 योजनस् and the circumference (मण्डल) was 30000 योजनस्; (according to the learned Pauraṇīkas) Sūrya's expanse (? विपुलत्व) was 5800 योजनस् (सूर्यस् त्व् अष्टौ सहस्राणि द्वे चान्ये कुरुनदन । विष्कम्भेण, ततो राजन् मण्डलं त्रिंश-तं समम् ॥ अष्टपञ्चाशतं राजन् विपुल्-अत्वेन चानघ । श्रूयते परमोदारः पतंगो ऽसौ विभावसुः । एतत् प्रमाणम् अर्कस्य निर्डिष्टम् इह भारत) 6. 13. 43-44 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 6. 12. 41 interprets विपुलत्वेन as ततो ऽप्य् आधिकेयेन; in that case the circumference of Sūrya will be 30000 + 5800 = 35800 योजनस्; see also the Editor's note on the stanza 6. 13. 41, Vol. 7, p. 765); on account of the larger extent of Rāhu, it covers Candra and Āditya at proper times (स राहुश् छादयत्य् एतौ यथाकालं महत्तया । चन्द्रादित्यौ) 6. 13. 45. D. Importance: (1) Upamanyu while praising Śiva said that he (Śiva) was Sūrya among the planets (ग्रहाणां सूर्य उच्यसे) 13. 14. 156; Sūrya appears in a complex name of Śiva (चन्द्रसूर्यगतिः) 13. 17. 37; (2) Śiva made Bhāskara the chief of the luminous bodies (तेजसां भास्करं चक्रे (ईशम्)) 12. 122. 31; Brahmā told the sages that Sūrya was the chief of the planets (सूर्यो ग्रहाणाम् अधि-पः) 14. 43. 6; Arka was known as the chief of the hot luminaries (अर्को ऽधिपतिर् उष्णानाम्) 14. 43. 7; also cf. आदित्यो ज्योति-षाम् पतिः 6. 7. 14; खेचराणां प्रवरो यथार्कः 1. 83. 7; (3) Bhagavān, while narrating his विभूतिस्, said that he was Ravi among the luminous bodies (ज्योतिषां रविर् अंशुमान्) 6. 32. 21; (4) The divine sages, the Siddhas, and the great sages saw Candra, Āditya and Budha, among others, in the abode of Brahman 1. 203. 4; Āditya, along with Candra and constellations, wait on Brahmadeva in his सभा 2. 11. 17; E. Advent of the Kṛtayuga: Mārkaṇḍeya told the Pāṇḍavas that when Candra, Sūrya, the constellation Tiṣya (Puṣya) and Bṛhas-pati will come together in one राशि, the Kṛtayuga will set in 3. 188. 87 (for citation and Nī.'s commentary on it, see above Puṣya1, p. 257. 1). F. Mythological events: (1) Candra, Āditya, the planets, the stars, the constellations and the denizens of the heaven felt dejected due to the destruction caused by Sunda and Upasunda (चन्द्रादित्यौ ग्रहास् तारा नक्षत्राणि दिवौकसः । जग्मुर् विषादम्) 1. 202. 26; (2) when the gods made ready a chariot for Śiva's fight with the Tripuras, Sūrya and Candramas were made the two wheels of the excellent chariot (सूर्याचन्द्रमसौ कृत्वा चक्रे रथवरोत्तमे) 8. 24. 71. G. Auspicious: (1) Bhīṣma told Yudhiṣṭhira that in war the side which had wind, Sūrya and Śukra favourable to it became victorious; if they were simultaneously present, the former of the two proved stronger (यतो वायुर् यतः सूर्य्ō यतः शुक्रस् ततो जयः । पूर्वं पूर्वं ज्याय एषां संनिपाते युधिष्ठिर ॥ ) 12. 101. 17; (2) Dhṛta-rāṣṭra told Saṃjaya that when he heard that both Śukra and Sūrya were favourable to Pāṇḍavas indicating their victory, he lost all hopes of winning the war (यदा श्रौ-षम् शुक्रसूर्यौ च युक्तौ कौन्तेयानाम् अनुकूलौ जयाय । … तदा नाशंसे विज-याय संजय ॥ ) 1. 1. 129. H. Omens: (1) According to an astronomical event which took place before the war and which was noticed by Vyāsa, अमावास्या occurred on the thirteenth day of the month which was very unusual; on that occasion Candra and Sūrya were untimely swallowed the same month by Rāhu which indicated destruction of the subjects (चतुर्दशीं पञ्चदशीम् भूतपूर्वां च षोडशीम् । इमां तु नाभि-जानामि अमावास्यां त्रयोदशीम् ॥ चन्द्र-सूर्याव् उभौ ग्रस्ताव् एकमासे त्रयोदशीम् । अपर्वणि ग्रहाव् एतौ प्रजाः संक्षपयि-ष्यतः ॥ ) 6. 3. 28-29 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 6. 3. 28: पर्व दर्शाख्यं पञ्चदशे ऽह्नि भवति । एकतिथिवृद्धौ षोडशे वा एकतिथिक्षये चतुर्दशे वाह्नि भवति । तिथिद्वयक्षयस् तु लोके ऽत्यन्तम् अप्रसिद्-ध इत्य् अपर्वणित्य् उक्तम् । ग्रहं यातौ राहुणा ग्रहणं प्राप्तौ एतद् एव प्रजा-संक्षयहेतुत्वेन शास्त्रे दृष्टम् । ); a similar event—Rāhu swallowing both Āditya and Soma simultaneously—also occurred when the Sindhu heroes fought Arjuna and at that time the meteors struck Sūrya and were scattered (उल्काश् च जघ्निरे सूर्यं विकीर्यन्त्यः समन्ततः) 14. 76. 15-16; for Rāhu's swallowing Āditya out of time (अपर्वणि) also cf. 2. 71. 26, and 9. 55. 10; also cf. 5. 141. 10; and 6. 3. 11 (in the last two references अपर्वणि does not occur); (for Nī.'s comment on Bom. Ed. 5. 143. 11 see Rāhu above p. 267. 1 and on Bom. Ed. 6. 3. 11 he says: तत्र तुलास्थम् अर्कं राहुर् उपैति); (2) According to another omen noticed by Vyāsa, Arka, Indu and the constellations were blazing day and night irrespective of the fact whether it was day time or night time; that also indicated des-struction (ज्वलितार्केन्दुनक्षत्रम् निर्विशे-षदिनक्षपम् । अहोरात्रं मया दृष्तं तत् क्षयाय भविष्यति) 6. 2. 22; (3) According to an omen noticed by Karṇa, a line of black clouds covered Bhānu at dawn and dusk which foretold great danger (कृष्णश् च परिघस् तत्र भानुम् आवृत्य तिष्ठति । उदयास्तम्ये संध्ये वेदयानो महद् भयम् ॥ ) 5. 141. 22 (but Nī. on Bom. Ed 5. 143. 23: परिघः परिवेशः); (4) According to the omens noticed by Saṃjaya, when the two armies faced each other at Kurukṣetra, Āditya at its rise appeared as though split into two (द्विधाभूत इवादित्य उदये प्रत्यदृश्यत) 6. 17. 3; (5) When Karṇa marched out for war many unusual happenings (उत्पातस्) occurred, one of them being that seven major planets were seen issuing out of Sūrya (निश्चरन्तो व्यदृश्यन्त सूर्यात् सप्त महाग्रहाः) 8. 26. 34 (Nī., however, on Bom. Ed. 8. 37. 4: निश्चरन्तो युद्धार्थम् इति शेषः । सुआर्यात् सूर्यम् आरभ्य सूर्यादयो ऽन्योन्यम् युध्यन्तीत्य् अर्थः); (6) Yājñavalkya told Janaka that if one saw the moon (Soma) or the sun (Saha-srāṃśu) with a hole (in the middle) like a wheel with a broken nave he had only a week to live (शीर्णनाभि यथा चाक्रं छिद्रं सोमं प्रपश्यति । तथैव च सहस्रां-शुं सप्तरात्रेण मृत्युभाक्) 12. 305. 13. I. Similes: (1) Draupadī's five sons rushed at the demon Ārśyaśṛṅgi (Alambusa) as five planets rush at Ravi (ग्रहाः पञ्च यथा रविम्) 6. 96. 35; (2) Bhīmasena, encircled by the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, looked like Sūrya encircled by fierce planets at the time of the destruction of the people (प्रजासंहरणे सूर्यः क्रूरैर् इव महाग्रहैः) 6. 73. 10; (3) Lakṣmaṇa and Rāma, surrounded by the monkey-chiefs, looked like Candra and Sūrya surrounded by the planets (चन्द्र-सूर्यौ ग्रहैर् वृतौ) 3. 267. 17. [For Sūrya also see Section 1. 7 where other re-ferences to the sun's eclipse can be found]
सोम: Soma m.: Name of the planet moon, referred to also as Candra or Candramas and by its other synonyms such as Indu, Śaśin, Niśākara. A. Origin and activity: According to Bhīṣma, Candra, Āditya and other planets, the constellations and stars were born from Viṣvaksena (i. e. Kṛṣṇa) (चन्द्रादित्यौ ग्रहनक्षत्रताराः … विष्वक्सेनात् सर्वम् एतत् प्रसूतम्) 13. 143. 31; Puruṣottama (Nārāyaṇa) told the seven sages, Marīci and others, that the sun, the moon, all con-stellations act in their own prescribed way in their respective spheres and are considered an authority (सूर्याचन्द्रमसौ … अद्निकारेषु वर्तन्ते यथास्वं … सर्वे प्रमाणं हि) 12. 322. 39-40. B. Born repeatedly, its waxing and waning: The moon is born repeatedly (चन्द्रमा जायते पुनः) 3. 297. 47; vanishes thousands of times (चन्द्रमा इव … सहस्रशः । लीयते) 12. 293. 3; the moon waxes and wanes (क्षयं वृद्धिं च चन्द्रस्य) 12. 290. 46; the moon on the new moon day remains only as a very thin digit (विद्धि चन्द्रमसं दर्शे सूक्ष्मया कलया स्थितम्) 12. 233. 15; the fifteen digits of the moon are its source and abode; the moon also has a sixteenth digit, which is very thin, and that is the real moon; that digit is not used by gods but it favours gods (?) (कलाः पञ्चदशा योनिस् तद् धाम इति पठ्यते । नित्यम् एतद् विजानीहि सोमः षोडशमी कला । … षोडशा तु कला सूक्ष्मा स सोम उपधार्यताम् । न तूप-युज्यते देवैर् देवान् उपयनकति सा ॥ ) 12. 293. 4, 6 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 12. 304. 6: देवैर् इन्द्रियैर् न उपयुज्यते पाल्यते किं-तु देवान् एव सत्तास्फूर्तिप्रदानेन उप-युनक्ति पालयति). C. Description: high-souled (महात्मन्) 6. 13. 42; whose rays are cool (शीतरश्मि) 6. 13. 42; D. Ex-tent: Dhṛtarāṣṭra asked Saṃjaya to tell him everything about the extent (सर्वं प्रमाणम्) of Soma, to which Saṃjaya agreed 6. 12. 3-4; according to Saṃjaya's information the diameter (विष्कम्भ) of Candramas was 11000 योजनस् and its cir-cumference (मण्डलम्) 33000 योजनस्; (according to the learned Paurāṇikas) the expanse (वैपुल्य) of the moon was 5900 योजनस् (चन्द्रमास् तु सहस्राणि राजन्न् एकादश स्मृतः । विष्कम्भेण कुरुश्रेष्ठ त्रयस्त्रिंशत् तु मण्डलम् ॥ एकोनशष्टिर् वैपुल्याच् छीतरश्मेर् महात्मनः) 6. 13. 42 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 6. 12. 41 interprets विपुलत्वेन as ततो ऽप्य् आधिक्येन; in that case moon's circumference will be 33000 + 5900 = 38900; see also the editor's note on the stanza 6. 13. 41, Vol. 7, p. 765); on account of the larger extent of Rāhu, it covers the sun and the moon at proper times (स राहुश् छादयत्य् एतौ यथाकालं महत्-तया । चन्द्रादित्यौ) 6. 13. 45. E. Importance: (1) Upamanyu, while praising Śiva, said that he (Śiva) was Candramas among the नक्षत्रस् (नक्षत्राणां च चन्द्रमाः) 13. 14. 156; Soma appears among the names of Śiva (सोमो नक्षत्र-साधकः) 13. 17. 36; also Candra in a com-plex form (चन्द्रसूर्यगतिः) 13. 17. 37; (2) Soma appears as one of the names of Sūrya taught by Dhaumya to Yudhiṣṭhira 3. 3. 19; (3) God Śiva made moon (Niśā-kara) the chief of the constellations (चक्रे नक्षत्राणां निशाकरम् (ईशम्)) 12. 122. 31; Candramas is known as the chief of the constellations (नक्षत्राणां च चन्द्रमाः (अधिपः)) 14. 43. 6; Indu is known as the chief of the luminous bodies (ज्योतिषाम् इन्दुर् (अधिपतिः) उच्यते) 14. 43. 7; hence Soma is called ग्रहगणेश्वर 13. 66. 12; ग्रहपति 12. 118. 15; 12. 162. 24; Candra and Sūrya are surrounded by the planets (चन्द्रसूर्यौ ग्रहैर् वृतौ) 3. 267. 17; moon is नक्षत्रराज् 3. 226. 10; 12. 29. 123; it is surrounded by the नक्षत्रस् 5. 138. 27; it is accompanied by the नक्षत्रस् (सनक्षत्रः) 6. 7. 14; followed by the planets, constellations and stars 3. 266. 2; shines along with the planets and many con-stellations 3. 179. 12; called ताराधिप 1. 61. 30; 3. 264. 18, 20; 11. 19. 17; 12. 289. 60; 12. 327. 8; 13. 124. 4; तारापति 3. 264. 38; 3. 277. 22; 3. 292. 1; तारकाराज 3. 42. 14. उडुराज् 9. 34. 36; 12. 52. 18; 13. 14. 110; 14. 63. 3; उडुपति 9. 50. 1; उडुप 3. 146. 68; (4) Soma is also the lord of the plants (ओषधीनां पतिः) 14. 43. 8; (5) Candra, along with Āditya and Budha, present in the abode of Brahmadeva 1. 203. 4; Candramas and the constellations wait on Brahmadeva in his सभा 2. 11. 17-18. F. Advent of Kṛta Yuga: When the Moon, the Sun, the Tiṣya (Puṣya) and Bṛhaspati will come in one राशि, the Kṛta age will commence 3. 188. 87 (for the citation and Nī.'s com, on it see Puṣya1, p. 257. 1). G. Mytho-logical events: (1) Pained due to the des-truction indulged in by Sunda and Upasunda, the moon, the sun, the planets, the stars, the constellations and the denizens of the heaven felt dejected (चन्द्रादित्यौ ग्रहास् तारा नक्षत्राणि दिवौकसः । जग्मुर् विषादम्) 1. 202. 26; (2) When the gods made ready an excellent chariot for Śiva's fight with the Tripuras, Sūrya and Candramas were made its wheels (सूर्याचन्द्रमसौ कृत्वा चक्रे रथवरोत्तमे) 8. 24. 71. H. Auspicious conjunction: (1) Kuntī gave birth to Yudhiṣṭhira when the moon was in conjunction with the Aindra (Jyeṣṭhā) नक्षत्र (ऐन्द्रे चन्द्रसमायुक्ते) 1. 114. 4-5; (2) Vyāsa asked first Yudhi-ṣṭhira to take the hand of Draupadī (in marriage) since that was an auspicious day on which Candramas would he in con-junction with the Puṣya constellation (for the citation and Nī.'s comment on it see above Pauṣya p. 259. 1); (3) Daśaratha asked his Purohita to make preparations for the consecration of Rāma as heir-apparent since on that night the moon would be in conjunction with the Puṣya which was an auspicious योग (अध्य पुष्यो निशि ब्रह्मन् पुण्यं योगम् उपैष्यति) 3. 261. 15; I. Omens: (1) While pointing out different bad omens to Kṛṣṇa, Karṇa said that the mark on Soma had disappeared (सोमस्य लक्ष्म व्यावृत्तम्) 5. 141. 10 (But Nī. on Bom. Ed. 5. 143. 11: लक्ष्म व्यावृत्तं क्षीणत्वाद् अमावास्यासान्निध्यात् क्षीणचन्द्रो ऽपि पाप एव); the same bad omen was noticed by Vyāsa also which, according to him, indicated great danger (व्यावृत्तं लक्ष्म सोमस्य भविष्यति महद् भयम्) 6. 2. 32 (Here Nī. on Bom. Ed. 6. 2. 32: व्या-वृत्तं नष्टं लक्ष्महीनश् चन्द्र दृश्यत इत्य् अर्थः); a similar sight was noticeable at the junction of the Tretā and the Dvāpara when there occurred a drought for twelve years; at that time Soma, with its mark disappeared, receded to the south (जगाम दक्षिणं मारगं सोमो व्यावृत्तलक्षणः) 12. 139. 15 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 12. 141. 15: व्यावृत्तं अन्यथाभूतं लक्षणं चिह्नं यस्य); (2) According to another omen noticed by Vyāsa and reported to Dhṛtarāṣṭra the moon on the Kārttikī full moon night, being without lustre, was (sometimes ?) not visible, and (at other times ?) with the colour of fire appeared in the sky which had the same colour (अलक्ष्यः प्रभया हीनः पौर्णमासीं च कार्त्तिकीम् । चन्द्रो ऽभूद् अग्निवर्णश् च समवर्णे नभस्तले) 6. 2. 23; (3) According to a third omen noticed by Vyāsa, whether it was day or night, the sun, the moon and the constellations appeared blazing; that indicated destruction (ज्वलितार्केन्दुनक्षत्रं निर्विशेषदिनक्ष-पम् । अहोरात्रं मया दृष्टं तत् क्षयाय भविष्यति ॥ ) 6. 2. 22; (4) According to another astronomical event, Vyāsa noticed that the अमावास्या had occurred on the thirteenth day of the month which was very unusual; on that day Candra and Sūrya both were swallowed the same month by Rāhu at an improper time 6. 2. 28-29 (for citation and Nī.'s commentary see Sūrya p. 276. 2); (5) A similar event-Rāhu swallowed Āditya and at the same time Soma-occurred when the Sindhu heroes fought with Arjuna (राहुर् अग्रसद् आदित्यं युगपत् सोमम् एव च) 14. 76. 15; (6) Saṃjaya told Dhṛtarāṣṭra that the day on which the two armies gathered at Kurukṣetra, Soma was in the constellation Maghā and the seven principal planets gathered in the sky blazing (for the citation and Nī.'s commen-tary on it see above Maghā, p. 263. 1); (7) Yājñavalkya told Janataka that one to whom the full moon appeared broken towards the south had only a year to live (पुर्णेन्-दुं (दीपम् एव च) । खण्डाभासं दक्षि-णतस् ते ऽपि संवत्सरायुषः ॥ ) 12. 305. 9; (8) He also told Janaka that one who saw Soma with a hole like a wheel with a broken nave had only a week to live (शीर्णनाभि यथा चक्रं छिद्रं सोमं प्रपश्यति । सप्तरात्रेण मृत्युभाक्) 12. 305. 13. J. Similes: (1) Rohiṇī's association with the moon: Sudeva wondered when would Damayantī be associated with Nala, as Rohiṇī with Śaśin, and end her miseries (रोहिणी शशिनो यथा) 3. 65. 21; Śāntā waited on Ṛśyaśrṅga as Rohiṇī on Soma (खे रोहिणी सोमम् इवामुकूला) 3. 113. 22; Kuntī blessed Draupadi after her marriage saying that she might be united with her husbands as Rohiṇī with Soma (रोहिणी च यथा सोमे) 1. 191. 5; also cf. चन्द्रश् च रोहिण्याम् 5. 115. 9; रोहिणी शशिनः 13. 134. 4; (2) Moon's association with the other नक्षत्रस्: (i) Kṛttikās: The king of the Prāgjyotiṣa with a white parasol decorated with garlands (मालयदामवता … श्वेतच्छ-त्रेण) shone like the moon on a full moon day in conjunction with the Kṛttikās (कृ-त्तिकायोगयुक्तेन पौर्णमास्याम् इवेन्दुना) 7. 19. 18; (ii) Sāvitra: Droṇa in the company of the five Pāṇḍava brothers looked like the moon in association with the constel-lation Sāvitra (i. e. Hasta) consisting of five stars (पञ्चतारेण संयुक्तः सावित्रे-णेव चन्द्रमाः) 1. 125. 30 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 1. 135. 30: सावित्रेण हस्तनक्षत्रेण); (iii) Punarvasū: the two Pāñcāla heroes (पाञ्चाल्यौ), guarding the wheels of Yudhi-ṣṭhira, shone like the two Punaravasu stars on the two sides of the moon (रथाभ्याशे चकाशेते चन्द्रस्येव पुनर्वसू) 8. 33. 16; (iv) Viśākhā: Karṇa with the two shin-ing कुण्डलस् in his ears appeared like the bright moon in the sky with two Viśākhā stars on each side (विशाखयोर् मध्य-गतः शशीव विमलो दिवि) 3. 285. 11; the head of the Pāṇḍya king wearing the कुण्डलस् shone like the moon with two Viśākhā stars on two sides 8. 15. 42; also 8. 14. 50; (v) Constellations or stars in general: Balarāma of white complexion and wearing a blue garment (नीलवासाः सित-प्रभः), seated among the kings, appeared like the moon among the constellations (नक्षत्रगणैः परिकीर्णो निशाकरः) 9. 33. 17; 9. 54. 42; Kṛṣṇa told Karṇa that he, among the Pāṇḍavas, would appear like the moon among the नक्षत्रस् 5. 138. 27; the sons of Draupadī, with their followers, stood round Dhṛṣṭadyumna like the multitude of stars around the moon (चन्द्रं तारागणा इव) 8. 32. 6; when king Sagara, followed by his 60000 sons, moved he looked liked the king of the नक्षत्रस् (i. e. the moon) followed by luminous bodies in a cloudless sky at the end of the rainy season (नक्ष-त्रराजं वर्षान्ते व्यभ्रे ज्योतिर्गणा इव) 12. 29. 123; (3) Moon's association with planets: (i) Aṅgāraka: Droṇa entered the arena with Aśvatthāhman as the moon enters a cloudless sky in the company of Aṅgāraka (नभो जलधरैर् हीनं साङ्गारक इवां-शुमान्) 1. 124. 18; (ii) Budha and Śukra: Arjuna, with Kṛṣṇa and Sātyaki by his side in the chariot, looked like the moon destroying the darkness in the company of Budha and Śukra (सहितो बुधशुक्राभ्यां तमो निघ्नन् यथा शशी) 7. 60. 20; (iii) Śanaiścara: Śalya drawing near Yudhi-ṣṭhira looked like the planet Śanaiścara drawing near the moon (चन्द्रमसो ऽभ्याशे शनैश्चर इव ग्रहः) 9. 15. 10; (iv) Planets in general: Lakṣmaṇa and Rāma surrounded by the monkey chiefs look-ed like the moon and the sun surrounded by the planets (चन्द्रसूर्यौ ग्रहैर् इव) 3. 267. 17; the seven Kaurava brothers tormented Bhīmasena (by showering arrows) as do the seven planets the moon at the time of the destruction of the creatures (प्रजासंह-रणे राजन् सोमं सप्त ग्रहा इव) 7. 112. 22; the five sons of Draupadī tormented Ārśyaśṛṅgī as do the five planets the moon at the end of the Yuga (यथा युगक्षये घोरे चन्द्रमाः पञ्चभिर् ग्रहैः) 6. 96. 36; (4) Moon by itself (i) Kaca, coming out of the belly of his teacher, is compared with the moon on the full moon day on the last day of the bright fortnight (शूक्लात्यये पौर्णमास्याम् इवेन्दुः) 1. 71. 49; (ii) The fierce fight of Droṇa and Karṇa with the army of Yudhiṣṭhira appeared like the one between the two oceans which grow large due to rise of the moon (यथा सागरयो राजंश् चन्द्रोदयविवृद्धयोः) 7. 147. 32. [For Soma also See section 1. 7]
स्वाति: Svāti f.: Name of a star. A. Placement: Suparṇa told Gālava that the Svāti was stationed in the north and there it arose (अत्र तिष्ठति वै स्वातिर् अत्रा-स्या उदयः स्मृतः) 5. 109. 12. B. Reli-gious rites: (1) दान: Nārada told Devakī (13. 63. 2-4) that by giving away riches, which one cherished most, under Svāti (स्वाताव् अथ धनं दत्त्वा यद् इष्टतमम् आत्मनः) one obtained auspicious worlds (लोकान् … शुभान्) after death and great fame in this world 13. 63. 18; (2) श्राद्-ध: Yama told Śaśabindu (13. 89. 1) that by offering a काम्य श्राद्ध under the lunar conjunction with Svāti (स्वातियोगे) one (was successful) deriving profit from trade (वाणिज्यम् उपजीवति) 13. 89. 7. C. Omen: According to one of the omens noted hy Vyāsa before the war the harsh planet (Ketu) was stationed between Citrā and Svāti (चित्रास्वात्यन्तरे चैव धिष्ठि-तः परुषो ग्रहः) 6. 3. 16.
स्वायम्भुव: Svāyaṃbhuva nt.: Name of the first मन्वन्तर (a long period of time) presided over by Manu Svāyaṃbhuva. Events: (1) Bhīṣma had heard from his father that the eternal Nārāyaṇa, the world-soul, was born as the son of Dharma and had assumed four forms, viz. Nara, Nārāyaṇa, Hari and Kṛṣṇa; this had happen-ed formerly in the Kṛtayuga of the Svāyaṃ-bhuva Manvantara (नारायणो हि विश्वात्मा चतुर्मूर्तिः सनातनः । धर्मात्मजः संबभूव पितैवं मे ऽभ्यभाषत ॥ कृते युगे महाराज पुरा स्वायंभुवे ऽन्तरे । नरो नारायणश् चैव हरिः कृष्णस् तथैव च ॥ ) 12. 321. 8-9 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 12. 334. 8: चतस्रो मूर्तयः नराद्याः); (2) According to one view Rudra's throat became blue because it was held tightly by Nārāyaṇa in the bygone Svāyaṃbhuva Manvantara (पूर्वे च मन्वन्तरे स्वा-यंभुवे नारायणहस्तबन्धग्रहणान् नीलकण्ठत्वम् एव वा) 12. 329. 15; (3) Hari-Nārāyaṇa asked his speech-born son Apāntaratamas (सुतो वाक्संभवो विभोः 12. 337. 38) to prepare श्रुति for making the Vedas known; accordingly Apāntara-tamas divided the Vedas in the Svāyaṃ-bhuva Manvantara; when this was done the god Hari was pleased with him (वेदाख्याने श्रुतिः कार्या त्वया मतिमतां वर । … तेन भिन्नास् तदा वेदा मनोः स्वायं-भुवे ऽन्तरे । ) ततस् तुतोष भगवान् हरिस् तेनास्य कर्मणा) 12. 337. 39-40.

संवर्तस्य: Saṃvartasya vāpī f.: Name of a sacred tank. Sacred to the brahmanical sage Saṃ-varta; described as not easily accessible (दुर्-लभा); one who visits it becomes handsome and fortunate (रूपस्य भागी भवति सु-भगश् चैव जायते) 3. 83. 28.
संवेद्य: Saṃvedya nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। Described as best (उत्तम); by reach-ing there in the evening (संध्यां समा-साद्य) and by bathing there one undoubtedly becomes learned (उपस्पृश्य नरो विद्वान् भवेन् नास्त्य् अत्र संशयः) 3. 83. 1.
सङ्गम: Saṃgama m., nt. (3. 85. 13): Con-fluence of two rivers, or of a river and the ocean, considered as holy. Various confluences are mentioned: (1) Confluence of the river Gaṅgā: (i) with Yamunā, famous as Prayāga (गङ्गा-यमुनयोर् वीर संगमम् … प्रयागम् इति विख्यातम्) 3. 85. 13-14; A. Descrip-tion: Holy (पुण्य); purifying (पवित्र), best purifier (पावनम् उत्तमम्); liked by sages (ऋषिभिर् जुष्टं); famous in the world (लोकविश्रुत) 3. 85. 13. B. Holi-ness: One who has strictly observed the vows (शंशितव्रतः) if he bathes at this confluence he gets as fruit the religious merit of performing a Rājasūya and an Aśva-medha (पुण्यं स फलं आप्नोति राज-सूयाश्वमेधयोः) 3. 83. 76. C. Epic event: The Pāṇḍavas lived at this confluence; after bathing there they practised best auste-rities (आप्लुत्य गात्राणि तपश् चातस्थुर् उत्तमम्) and gave wealth to Brāhmaṇas 3. 93. 5-6. D. Past event: Formerly Pitāmaha offered a sacrifice there (hence called Prayāga) 3. 85. 14; (ii) with Sarasvatī: One who bathes at the confluence of Gaṅgā and Sarasvatī gets the fruit of an Aśvamedha and goes to heaven 3. 82. 34; (iii) with Saṃgamā: One who bathes at the confluence of Gaṅgā and Saṃgamā gets the fruit of ten horse sacrifices and lifts up his family (कुलं चैव समुद्धरेत्) 3. 82. 31; (iv) with the ocean: Wise say that one who performs a rite related to Pitāmaha at this Saṃgama gets tenfold fruit of a horse sacrifice (कृते पैतामहे विधौ ॥ गङ्गायास् त्व् अथ राजेन्द्र साग-रस्य च संगमे । अश्वमेधं दशगुणं प्रवदन्ति मनीषिणः ॥ ) 3. 83. 3-4; (2) Confluence of the river Sarasvatī, the other river not mentioned (संगमं … सरस्व-त्याः 3. 80. 130): A. Description: Des-cribed as very holy (महापुण्य) and famous in the world (लोकविश्रुत) 3. 80. 130; B. Holiness: (i) Brahmadeva, gods, sages, Siddhas, and Cāraṇas go to this संगम on bright fortnight of the month of Caitra and worship Janārdana (उपासन्ते जनार्दनम्) 3. 80. 130-131; (ii) By bathing there one gets much gold (विन्देद् बहुसुवर्णकम्) and, by purifying himself of all sins, goes to the world of Brahman 3. 80. 132, (iii) By visiting the place there where the sages completed their सत्रस् (सत्रावसानम् आसाद्य) one gets the fruit of giving a thousand cows 3. 80. 133. C. Past events: Sages (in the past) completed their sacrificial session on this confluence of Sarasvatī (ऋषीणां यत्र सत्राणि समाप्तानि) 3. 80. 133; (3) Confluence of rivers Śoṇa and Jyotirathyā: One who is pure (शुचिः) if he lives at the confluence of Śoṇa and Jyotirathyā and satisfies (तर्पयित्वा) manes and gods gets the reward of an Agni-ṣṭoma 3. 83. 8; (4) Confluence of Veṇṇā (and Godāvarī) rivers: One who bathes at this confluence (Godāvarī not directly mentioned) gets the fruit of a Vājapeya 3. 83. 31; (5) Confluence of Varadā (and Godāvarī ?): One who bathes at the confluence of Varadā (and Godāvarī) gets the fruit of gifting a thousand cows 3. 83. 31.
