संगमा: Saṃgamā f.: Name of a river. One who bathes at the confluence of the rivers Gaṅgā and Saṃgamā (गङ्गासंग-मयोश् चैव स्नाति यः संगमे नरः) gets the fruit of ten Aśvamedha sacrifices and lifts up his family 3. 82. 31.
सत्रावसान: Satrāvasāna nt.: Name of an indepen-dent तीर्थ ? (3. 80. 133); see Saṃgama: 2 (iii) Confluence of Sarasvatī.
सदानिरामया: Sadānirāmayā f.: Name of a river. Listed by Saṃjaya among the rivers of the Bhāratavarṣa; people used its water for drinking 6. 10. 31, 13; all the rivers listed by Saṃjaya are described as mothers of the universe and very strong 6. 10. 35 (for cita-tion see Atikṛṣṇā).
सदानीरा: Sadānīrā f.: Name of a river. Listed by Saṃjaya among the rivers of the Bhāratavarṣa; people used its water for drinking 6. 10. 23, 13; all the rivers listed by Saṃjaya are described as mothers of the universe and very strong 6. 10. 35 (for citation see Atikṛṣṇā); Sadānīrā, Gaṇḍakīyā and Śoṇa rise from the same mountain (एकपर्-वतके नद्यः) 2. 18. 27; Bhīma, Arjuna, and Kṛṣṇa had to cross these rivers on their way to the Magadha country 2. 18. 27; (identical with Karatoyinī ?). [See Kara-toyinī]
सन्ध्या: Saṃdhyā f.: Name of a river. By reaching this river and by bathing in it one undoubtedly becomes learned (अथ संध्यां समासाद्य … उपस्पृश्य नरो विद्वान् भवेन् नास्त्य् अत्र संशयः) 3. 83. 1.
संध्या: Saṃdhyā f.: Name of a river. By reaching this river and by bathing in it one undoubtedly becomes learned (अथ संध्यां समासाद्य … उपस्पृश्य नरो विद्वान् भवेन् नास्त्य् अत्र संशयः) 3. 83. 1.
संनिहिती: Saṃnihitī f.: Name of a तीर्थ। Brahmadeva, other gods and ascetics visit the तीर्थ every month and are endowed with great religious merit (मासि मासि समा-यान्ति पुण्येन महतान्विताः) 3. 81. 166; whatever तीर्थस् that exist on this earth or in the mid-region, as well as rivers, male and female, ponds, all kinds of streams, wells, river banks and other holy places, they all undoubtedly visit Saṃnihitī every month (this explains the name of the तीर्थ) (पृथिव्यां यानि तीर्थानि अन्तरिक्षचराणि च । नद्यो नदास् तडागाश् च सर्वप्रस्र-वणानि च ॥ उदपानाश् च वप्राश् च पुण्यान्य् आयतनानि च । मासि मासि समायान्ति संनि-हित्यां न संशयः ॥ ) 3. 81. 168-169; by bathing in Saṃnihitī on the day of solar eclipse one gets for ever the fruit of perform-ing a hundred horse sacrifices (संनिहित्याम् उपस्पृश्य राहुग्रस्ते दिवाकरे । अश्वमेध-शतं तेन इष्टं भवति शाश्वतम्) 3. 81. 167; whatever evil act a man or a woman commits is undoubtedly destroyed by bathing at this तीर्थ and he goes to the world of Brahman riding in a lotus-coloured conveyance (पद्मवर्णेन यानेन ब्रह्मलोकं स गच्छति) 3. 81. 170; Yakṣa Arantuka acts there as a gate-keeper (द्वारपाल); the sacred places Koṭirūpa and Gaṅgāhrada are also there 3. 81. 171-172.
सप्तगङ्ग: Saptagaṅga nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। If one satisfies according to the rites gods and manes at this तीर्थ he is glorified in the world of the holy (पुण्यलोके महीयते) 3. 82. 25; he also gets सुधा to drink if he is born again (सुधां वै लभते भोक्तुं यो नरो जायते पुनः) 13. 26. 15.
सप्तगोदावर: Saptagodāvara nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। One who is controlled and takes limited food if he bathes at this तीर्थ he will get great religious merit and will go to the world of gods (सप्तगोदावरे स्नात्वा नियतो नियता-शनः । महत् पुण्यम् अवाप्नोति देवलोकं च गच्छति ॥ ) 3. 83. 41.
सप्तर्षिकुण्ड: Saptarṣikuṇḍa nt. (pl.): Name of a तीर्थ। Situated at the place known as Brahma-ṇaḥ sthānam or Brahmodumbara 3. 81. 58; one who is pure and has restrained his mind (शुचिः प्रयतमानसः) he, by bathing at this तीर्थ (सप्तर्षिकुण्डेषु स्नातस्य) and by approaching Brahman, is cleansed of all sins and goes to the world of Brahman 3. 81. 59-60. [See Brahmaṇaḥ sthānam1]
सप्तसारस्वत: Saptasārasvata nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। A. Location: Related to the river Sara-svatī (सरस्वतीतीर्थवरम्) 9. 36. 57; on the Himavant (हैमवते गिरौ) 9. 37. 26. B. Name explained: When Sarasvatī was invited again by Brahman for his sacrifice all the seven forms of the river were once more united in a तीर्थ on the Himavant; that तीर्थ became known as the Saptasārasvata tīrtha (ब्रह्मणा यजता पुनः । समाहूता ययौ तत्र पुण्ये हैमवते गिरौ ॥ एकीभूतास् ततस् तास् तु तस्मिंस् तीर्थे समागताः । सप्तसारस्वतं तीर्थं ततस् तत् प्रथितं भुवि ॥ ) 9. 37. 26-27. C. Description: Holy (पुण्य) 9. 37. 28; excellent (तीर्थ-वर) 9. 36. 57; famous on the earth (प्र-थितं भुवि) 9. 37. 27; full of many kinds of birds (नानाद्विजगणायुत) 9. 36. 57; crowded with hundreds of herds of animals (मृगयूथशताकुल) 9. 36. 62; filled with the sound of Vedic studies (स्वाध्यायघोष-संघुष्ट) 9. 36. 62; resorted to often by peaceful and righteous men (अहिंस्रैर् धर्मपरमैर् नृभिर् अत्यन्तसेवितम्) 9. 36. 62; trees growing near the तीर्थ and different ascetics living there mentioned in 9. 36. 58-61. D. Holiness: Mahādeva lives there in the आश्रम of Maṅkaṇaka 3. 81. 114; 9. 37. 48; those who bathe in the Saptasārasvata tīrtha and worship Mahādeva nothing will be unobtainable to them, here in this world or in the next, and they will un-doubtedly go to the world of Sarasvatī (न तेषां दुर्लभं किंचिद् इह लोके परत्र च । सारस्वतं च ते लोकं गमिष्यन्ति न संशयः) 3. 81. 114-115; 9. 37. 49. E. Epic events: (1) Janamejaya asked Vaiśaṃpāyana to tell him why Saptasārasvata was so called (सप्तसारस्वतं कस्मात्) 9. 37. 1; (2) Halāyudha (Balarāma) arrived at this तीर्थ from the Naimiṣeya kuñja of Kurukṣetra (9. 36. 54) 9. 36. 63. F. Past event: At this तीर्थ the great sage Maṅkaṇaka, who was a Siddha, prac-tised austerities 9. 36. 63; once Maṅkaṇaka cut his hand with the tip of a Kuśa blade; from his injured hand flowed the juice of vegetables (पुरा मङ्कणको राजन् कुशा-ग्रेणेति नः श्रुतम् । क्षतः किल करे राजंस् तस्य शाकरसो ऽस्रवत् ॥ ) 3. 81. 98.
समङ्गा: Samaṅgā f.: Name of a river. [See Madhuvilā]
सरक: Saraka nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। Described as famous in the world (लोक-विश्रुत) 3. 81. 62; by visiting (अभिगम्य) Vṛṣadhvaja (Śiva) there on the fourteenth day of the dark fortnight one gets all desires and goes to heaven; there are three crores of तीर्थस् at Saraka and a crore of Rudras in a well and in lakes (तिस्रः कोट्यस् तु तीर्था-नाम् सरके कुरुनन्दन । रुद्रकोटिस् तथा कूपे ह्रदेषु च महीपते); the तीर्थ called Ilāspada is also there 3. 81. 62-63.
सरयू: Sarayū f.: Name of a river; also called Śarayū (3. 212. 21). A. Location: Listed by Saṃjaya twice among the rivers of the Bhāratavarṣa; people used its water for drinking 6. 10. 18, 13; in the east; Bhīma, Arjuna and Kṛṣṇa crossed it to enter the eastern Kosala country (सं-तीर्य सरयूं रम्यां दृष्ट्वा पूर्वांश् च कोसलान्) 2. 18. 28. B. Origin (name explained): Vasiṣṭha brought the river Gaṅgā, flowing towards Kailāsa, to the lake which had received a boon from Brahman (ब्रह्म-दत्तवरं सरः 13. 140. 18); Gaṅgā broke that lake (सरस्) and then became the river Sarayū (कैलासं प्रस्थितां चापि नदीं गङ्गां महातपाः । आनयत् तत् सरो दिव्यं तया भिन्नं च तत् सरः ॥ सरो भिन्नं तया नद्या सरयूः सा ततोऽभवत्) 13. 140. 23-24. C. Description: Pleasing (रम्या) 2. 18. 28; all the rivers listed by Saṃjaya are said to be mothers of the universe and very strong 6. 10. 35 (for citation see Ati-kṛṣṇā). D. Holiness and its limitation: (1) All the rivers listed by Mārkaṇḍeya— Śarayū one of them—are declared to be mothers of the sacrificial hearths, i. e. on the banks of which sacrifices were performed 3. 212. 21 (एता नद्यस् तु धिष्ण्यानां मातरो याः प्रकीर्तिताः 3. 212. 24; for Nī. see Kapilā); (2) The excellent तीर्थ called Gopratāra is on the river Sarayū (सरय्वास् तीर्थम् उत्तमम्) 3. 82. 63; limitation: Gifting cows in very large numbers on the bank of Sarayū is highly meritorious, but not enough to take the donor to Brahmaloka 13. 106. 37. E. Impor-tance: Finds mention in the Daivata-Ṛṣi-Vaṃśa 13. 151. 16, 2. F. Epic event: Bhīma, Arjuna and Kṛṣṇa crossed the river Sarayū on their way to the Magadha country 2. 18. 28. G. Past event: (1) Vīra, one of the fires, begot Siddhi on the river Sarayū (वीरः सरय्वां जनयत् सिद्धिम्) 3. 209. 9-11 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 3. 219. 11: शरय्वां भार्यायां सिद्धिं नाम पुत्रं जनयत्) (2) Asamañjas, the son of Sagara, used to drown the children of citizens in the river Sarayū; he was therefore rebuked by his father and was banished by him 12. 57. 9. H. Simile: The armies of the Kauravas and the Pāṇḍavas clashed with each other with the speed of flooded Gaṅgā and Sarayū in the rainy season (गङ्गासरय्वोर् वेगेन प्रावृषीवोल्बणोदके) 7. 16. 49.
सरला: Saralā f.: Name of a river. Listed by Saṃjaya among the rivers of the Bhāratavarṣa; people used its water for drinking 6. 10. 22, 13 (for other details see Atikṛṣṇā).
सरस्वती: Sarasvatī f.: sg, (pl. 6. 10. 35; 9. 37. 3; 9. 44. 18; 12. 255. 39; 13. 75. 12): Name of a river (in some events conceived as a woman); also called Bhogavatī (3. 25. 20). A. Location: (1) Listed by Saṃjaya among the rivers of the Bhāratavarṣa; people used its water for drinking 6. 10. 13; (2) In the north (उदीच्याम्) 3. 88. 1; on the top of Himavant (प्रस्थे हिमवतः शुभे) 9. 4. 49; Balarāma saw on the Himavant mountain (9. 53. 9), the source of Sarasvatī at Plakṣaprasravaṇa (प्रभवं च सरस्-वत्याः प्लक्षप्रस्रवणं बलः (दृष्ट्वा)) 9. 53. 11; Sarasvatī's origin in an ant-hill near a Plakṣa tree (प्लक्षाद् देवी सृता राजन् महापुण्या सरस्वती ॥ तत्राभिषेकं कुर्-वीत वल्मीकान् निःसृते जले) 3. 82. 5-6; flowing from Himavant (हैमवती) 9. 43. 51; (3) Rises in the lake of Brahman (प्रसृतासि महाभागे सरसो ब्रह्मणः पुरा) 9. 50. 19; 9. 41. 29; (4) The Bāh-līka country was disregarded by Gaṅgā, Yamunā and Sarasvatī (गङ्गया च तिरस्-कृताः । सरस्वत्या यमुनया) 8. 30. 10; (5) Nakula in his march towards the west of Khāṇḍavaprastha (खाण्डवप्रस्थात् प्रतीचीम् अभितो दिशम् 2. 29. 2) conquered people who lived along Sarasvatī (ये चाश्रित्य सरस्वतीम् । वर्तयन्ति) 2. 29. 9; one of the rivers visited by the Pāṇḍavas in their westward march (ययुः … पश्चिमां दिशम्); on its bank is the Kāmyaka forest (सरस्-वतीकूले) 3. 6. 2-3; (6) Flowing through Kurukṣetra (तत्र (i. e. कुरुक्षेत्रे) … सरस्वत्याम्) 3. 81. 3, 92-93; 3. 129. 21-22; 3. 130. 3; flowing through Samantapañcaka 9. 43. 51; Kurukṣetra to the south of Sarasvatī and to the north of Dṛṣadvatī 3. 81. 175; lake Dvaitavana near Sarasvatī 3. 174. 21. B. Description: Auspicious (शिवा) 3. 179. 15; 13. 134. 22; holy (पुण्या) 3. 129. 20; 3. 130. 3; 9. 37. 17; 9. 38. 27; 9. 43. 51; 13. 134. 15; very holy (सुपुण्या) 6. 10. 35; (महा-पुण्या) 3. 82. 5; most holy (पुण्यतमा) 13. 134. 22; brings holiness (to visitors) (पुण्यवहा) 3. 88. 2; holy among all rivers (सर्वनदीषु पुण्या) 9. 53. 35; has holy तीर्थस् on it (पुण्यतीर्था) 3. 179. 14; having hundreds of तीर्थस् on it (तीर्थ-शतोपेता) 9. 38. 27; having waters of all तीर्थस् (सर्वतीर्थोदकैर् युता) 13. 134. 12; purifying (पावना) 6. 7. 45; sinless (अनघा) 9. 42. 11; highly fortunate (महा-भागा) 9. 37. 24; 9. 50. 19, 22, 23; (भगवती) 9. 37. 26; as though the sacrificial ground of gods (आयागभूताम् इव देवतानाम्) 3. 174. 24; divine (देवी) 9. 43. 51; (दिव्या) 3. 130. 3; having heavenly water (दिव्यतोया) 9. 37. 25; 9. 44. 18; excellent river, best or first among rivers (सरिच्छ्रेष्ठा) 3. 82. 5; 9. 36. 36, 38, 44, 47; 9. 37. 11, 14, 23, 24; 9. 40. 33; 9. 41. 19, 23; 9. 42. 12, 13; 9. 43. 51; 9. 50. 19; 13. 134. 22; (सरितां श्रेष्ठा) 9. 37. 18, 19; 9. 41. 12, 20; 9. 42. 8; (सरिद्वरा) 9. 36. 51; 13. 134. 14; (सरितां वरा) 9. 36. 52; 9. 41. 27, 39; 9. 50. 11; 13. 134. 19; (नदीनाम् उत्तमा) 3. 82. 5; 13. 134. 15; (प्रथमा सर्वसरिताम्) 13. 134. 15; shining (शुभा) 9. 50. 23; 13. 139. 26; भामिनी 9. 41. 13; beautiful (वरवर्णिनी) 9. 50. 20; pleasing to look at (प्रियदर्शना) 9. 50. 20; red (अरुणा) 9. 4. 49; always bringing happiness to people (लोकसुखावहा सदा) 9. 53. 35; great river (महानदी) 9. 36. 53; 9. 39. 7 (not named); 9. 42. 20; 9. 50. 10, 18, 24; 12. 335. 46; full of lakes (ह्रदिनी) 3. 88. 2; has placid water (प्र-सन्नसलिला) 3. 179. 15; (as a woman) whose eyes were like a lotus (पुण्डरीक-निभेक्षणा) 9. 41. 17; its banks wide like sky (आकाशनीकाशतटा) 3. 179. 14; having a garland of forests (वनमालिनी) 3. 88. 2; full of नीप and नीवार (on its banks) (नीपनीवारसंकुला) 3. 179. 14; flowing rapidly (शीघ्रगामिनी) 9. 37. 20; 9. 41. 23; (वेगयुक्ता) 9. 37. 13; (ओघवती) 3. 130. 3; flowing to the sea (सागरगामिनी) 13. 134. 15; (सागरगमा) 13. 134. 21; liked by Yakṣas, Gandharvas and great sages (यक्षगन्धर्वमहर्षिकान्ता) 3. 174. 24; resorted to by hosts of Brāhmaṇas (विप्र-संघैर् निषेविता) 9. 38. 27; worshipped by the sages (पूज्यमाना मुनिगणैः) 9. 37. 23; worshipped by good people at all times (सरस्वती नदी सद्भिः सततं पार्थ पूजिता) 3. 88. 9; thronged by people to whom she is the sole resort (एकशरणावृता) 3. 129. 20; famous in the three worlds (त्रिषु लोकेषु विश्रुता) 9. 43. 51; 6. 7. 47; versed in the knowledge of the duties of women (स्त्री-धर्मकुशला) 13. 134. 19; all the rivers listed by Saṃjaya are described as mothers of the universe and very strong (विश्वस्य मातरः सर्वाः सर्वाश् चैव महाबलाः) 6. 10. 35 (also see the next section C). C. Characteristics: (1) Sarasvatī appears and disappears again at various places (दृश्या-दृश्या च भवति तत्र तत्र सरस्वती) 6. 7. 47; the trees growing on the banks of Sarasvatī are (सरस्वतीतीररुहैः … शोभि-तम्): Badara, Iṅguda, Kāśmarya, Plakṣa, Aśvattha, Vibhītaka, Panasa, Palāśa, Karīra, Pīlu, Bandhana, Syandana, Bilva, Āmrātaka, and Pārijāta; there are also on its bank forests of Parūṣaka (परूषकवनैश् चैव) and groves of Atimuktaka (अतिमुक्तक-षण्डैश् च) 9. 36. 58-60; auspicious Śāla forests grow on its banks (शिवेषु । सरस्वती-शालवनेषु तेषु) 3. 26. 1; the big Mahā-śaṅkha tree is on its bank 9. 36. 20; the forests on its bank are inhabited by the righteous who have controlled their self and who wear bark garments and have matted hair and also by hosts of perfected sages (भोगवतीम् उपेत्य धृतात्मनां चीरजटाधराणाम् तस्मिन् वने धर्मभृतां निवासे । ददर्श सिद्धर्षिगणान् अनेकान्) 3. 25. 20; cf. 3. 26. 1; (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 3. 24. 20: भोगवतीं सरस्वतीं नदीम्); always pleasing to Dadhīca (मम प्रीयकरी चापि सततं) 9. 50. 20; Śūdras and hosts of Ābhīras took resort on Sarasvatī and lived on fish (शूद्रा-भीरगणाश् चैव ये चाश्रित्य सरस्वतीम् । वर्तयन्ति च ये मत्स्यैः) 2. 29. 9; there is no pleasure, there are no virtues which are equal to the residence on Sarasvatī (सरस्वती-वास समा कुतो रतिः सरस्वतीवाससमाः कुतो गुणाः) 9. 53. 34; Sarasvatī disappears in the desert at Vinaśana, but appears again at Camasa, Śivodbheda and Nāgodbheda 3. 80. 118; (13. 139. 26); the Siddhas know, due to the wetness of plants and earth, the presence of Sarasvatī there though not seen (स्निग्ध-त्वाद् ओषधीनां च भूमेश् च जनमेजय । जानन्ति सिद्धा राजेन्द्र नष्टाम् अपि सर-स्वतीम् ॥ ) 9. 34. 81; at Camasodbheda all ocean going rivers turn to her (यत्रैनाम् अभ्यवर्तन्त दिव्याः पुण्याः समुद्रगाः) 3. 130. 5. D. Holiness: (1) Vaiśaṃ-pāyana told Janamejaya the holiness of the Tīrthavaṃśa of Sarasvatī (here in particular of the Aujasatīrtha 9. 45. 92) 9. 45. 88; Sara-svatī and the तीर्थस् on Sarasvatī are holier than Kurukṣetra (पुण्यम् आहुः कुरु-क्षेत्रं कुरुक्षेत्रात् सरस्वतीम् । सर-स्वत्याश् च तीर्थानि) 3. 81. 125; by the favour of sage Dadhīca, Sarasvatī was to be at all times holiest among the other holy rivers (पुण्याभ्यश् च सरिद्भ्यस् त्वं सदा पुण्यतमा शुभे । भविष्यसि महाभागे मत्प्रसादात् सरस्वति) 9. 50. 23; (9. 53. 35); (2) By bathing in the river Sarasvatī one washes off one's sins (धूतपाप्मा भविष्यसि) 3. 129. 20; by bathing in Sara-svatī one rides in a विमान (सरस्वत्याम् उपस्पृश्य विमानस्थो विराजते) 3. 82. 139; by visiting Sarasvatī people have gone to heaven; those who have done evil acts if they visit Sarasvatī they never grieve in this or the other world (सरस्वतीं प्राप्य जनाः सुदुष्कृताः । सदा न शोचन्ति परत्र चेह च ॥ ) 9. 53. 34-35; according to the Gāthās sung by Yayāti (12. 148. 8) if one bathes and drinks water at Pṛthūdaka on Sarasvatī one does not have to worry about death in near future (नैव श्वोमरणं तपेत्) 12. 148. 10; this was also told by Ruṣaṅgu to his sons 9. 38. 29; by visiting Sarasvatī and by satisfying there gods and manes one re-joices undoubtedly in the worlds of Sarasvatī (सारस्वतेषु लोकेषु मोदते नात्र सं-शयः) 3. 82. 59; by bathing at the तीर्थ on Sarasvatī gods, Gandharvas, Apsarases, Dvaipāyana, Śuka, Kṛṣṇa, Yakṣas and many others became perfected in Yoga (योग-सिद्धाः) 9. 48. 18-20; one should live on Sarasvatī for a month 3. 81. 3; (3) By bathing at the confluence of Gaṅgā and Sara-svatī one gets the fruit of an Aśvamedha and goes to heaven 3. 82. 34; by visiting the place where Sarasvatī meets the ocean (सरस्वत्याः सागरस्य च संगमे) one gets the fruit of gifting a thousand cows and shining always with lustre like that of fire he is glorified in heaven (स्वर्गलोके महीयते । दीप्यमानो ऽग्निवन् नित्यं प्रभया); living there for three nights one should satisfy manes and gods; he thereby shines like the moon (प्र-भासते यथा सोमः … ) and gets the reward of an Aśvamedha 3. 80. 79-80; at the con-fluence of Sarasvatī (the other river is not named) people worship Janārdana; Brahmā and other gods, as well as sages and Siddhas and Cāraṇas, visit it on the fourteenth day of the bright half of Caitra 3. 80, 130; it is recommended that one should live at Kuru-kṣetra on Sarasvatī for a month (तत्र (कुरु-क्षेत्रे) सरस्वत्यां मासं वसेत्) 3. 81. 3; (4) There are many तीर्थस् on Sara-svatī 5. 154. 33; 9. 34. 33; all these तीर्थस् are holy 3. 81. 125; their holiness described in the Śalyaparvan (शल्यपर्वणि … सर-स्वत्याश् च तीर्थानां पुण्यता परिकीर्तिता) 1. 2. 174-175; these तीर्थस् are: Śaśayāna 3. 80. 120-121; a तीर्थ sacred to Aran-tuka, chief of Yakṣas 3. 81. 42; Śrīkuñja 3. 81. 91; Naimiṣakuñja 3. 81. 92; Devī-tīrtha at the confluence of Sarasvatī and Aruṇā 3. 81. 131; Vinaśana 3. 130. 3; Camasodbheda 3. 130. 5; Janamejaya asked Vaiśaṃpāyana to tell him the origin, the merits, the reward of visiting them, and how one achieves suc-cessful completion of visiting the तीर्थस् on Sarasvatī (सारस्वतानां तीर्थानां गुणोत्-पत्तिं वदस्व मे । फलं च द्विपदां श्रेष्ठ कर्मनिर्वृत्तिम् एव च ॥ 9. 34. 33: Nī. on Bom. Ed. 9. 35. 38: कर्मनिर्वृत्तिं तीर्थयात्राविधिसिद्धिम्); Vaiśaṃpāyana's account includes Prabhāsa 9. 34. 36; Cama-sodbheda 9. 34. 78; Subhūmika 9. 36. 3; Gargasrotas 9. 36. 14, 16; Śaṅkhatīrtha 9. 36. 24; Auśanasa 9. 38. 16, also called Kapālamocana 9. 38. 20; Pṛthūdaka 9. 38. 25-26; a तीर्थ not named 9. 38. 33; 9. 39. 6, 10, 23, 30; (5) The region deserted by Sarasvatī would be bereft of holiness (अपुण्य एष भवतु देशश् त्यक्तस् त्वया शुभे) 13. 139. 26; cows act like Sarasvatīs (pl.) in delivering persons from the remainder of their actions (?), in free-ing them from the body and in the obtain-ment of bliss (शेषोत्सर्गे कर्मभिर् देह-मोक्षे सरस्वत्यः श्रेयसि संप्रवृत्ताः) 13. 75. 12 (But Nī. on Bom. E. Epic events: (1) The Pāṇḍavas, at the beginning of their forest life, lived on the banks of Sarasvatī, Yamunā and Gaṅgā; they next saw the Kāmyaka forest on the bank of Sarasvatī and lived there 3. 6. 3-4; (2) The Pāṇḍavas saw in Dvaitavana the river Bhogavatī (= Sarasvatī) (मनोरमां भोगवतीम् उपेत्य … तस्मिन् वने (i. e. in Dvaitavana)) 3. 25. 20; they sported in the Śāla forests on the bank of Sarasvatī 3. 26. 1; the Pāṇḍavas left Dvaitavana and went to Kāmyaka on the bank of Sarasvatī (ययौ सरस्वतीतीरे काम्यकं नाम काननम्) 3. 37. 37; (3) Shown by Lomaśa to the Pāṇḍavas 3. 130. 3; after crossing the desert they reached Sarasvatī in order to live in Dvaitavana 3. 174. 21; seeing them settled in Dvaitavana ascetics came to them 3. 174. 22; the Pāṇḍavas were happy roaming along the river Sarasvatī 3. 174. 24; they spent the most holy autumnal Kārtika full moon night while living on the bank of Sarasvatī (तेषाम् पुण्य-तमा रात्रिः पर्वसंधौ स्म शारदी । तत्रैव वसताम् आसीत् कार्तिकी जनमे-जय ॥ ) 3. 179. 16; (4) Rāma Jāmadagnya, along with Ambā and other ascetics, went to Kurukṣetra to meet Bhīṣma and stayed near Sarasvatī (न्यविशन्त ततः सर्वे परिगृह्य सरस्वतीम्) 5. 177. 24; (5) After the fall of Karṇa, the Kṣatriyas fighting on the side of the Kauravas went to Sarasvatī flowing near Himavant, and bathed, and drank her water; they felt refreshed and returned for the battle (अरुणां सरस्वतीं प्राप्य पपुः सस्नुश् च तोज्जलम्) 9. 4. 49; (6) Balarāma decided to go on a pilgrimage to visit the तीर्थस् on Sarasvatī as he was not prepared to watch the destruction of those born in the Kuru family (तस्माद् यास्यामि तीर्थानि सरस्वत्या निषेवितुम् । न हि शक्-ष्यामि कौरव्यान् नश्यमानान् उपेक्षितुम्) 5. 154. 33; ha set out on the Maitra नक्षत्र; from the ocean he started his pilgrimage up-stream on the river (प्रतिस्रोतः सरस्वत्याः; सरस्वतीं प्रतिस्रोतः समुद्राद् अभिज-ग्मिवान्) 9. 34. 12, 17-18; Balarāma gave to Brāhmaṇas large दक्षिणास् at the excellent तीर्थस् on Sarasvatī 9. 34. 29-32; the तीर्थस् and other places visited by Balarāma were Prabhāsa 9. 34. 36; Camasodbheda 9. 34. 78-79; Udapāna 9. 34. 80; 9. 35. 1-2; 52-53; Vinaśana where Sarasvatī dis-appeared 9. 36. 1-3; Subhūmika 9. 36. 3-9; Gandharvatīrtha 9. 36. 10-14; Gragasrotas 9. 36. 14-19; Śaṅkhatīrtha where he saw the big tree Mahāśaṅkha 9. 36. 19-26; Dvaitavana, from where he went along the southern bank of Sarasvatī (ततः प्रा-याद् बलो राजन् दक्षिणेन सरस्वतीम्) 9. 36. 26-28; Nāgadhanavan, from where he went towards the east (प्रायात् प्राचीं दिशम्) 9. 36. 29-32; Naimiṣeya kuñja from where hte eastward flowing Sarasvatī again returned to the west (यत्र भूयो निववृते प्राङ्मुखा वै सरस्वती) 9. 36. 35; भूयः प्रतीच्यभिमुखी सुस्राव सरितां वरा) 9. 36. 52; 9. 36. 34-56; Saptasāra-svata 9. 36. 57-63; 9. 38. 1-3; Auśanasa (Kapālamocana) 9. 38. 4, 7, 21; Āśrama of Ruṣaṅgu 9. 38. 21; Pṛthūdaka 9. 38. 23, 30; (7) The prowess (प्रभाव) of Sarasvatī was narrated by Vaiśaṃpāyana to Janamejaya 9. 43. 1 (reference to Adhyāyas 9. 39-42); (8) The Pāṇḍavas and Duryodhana selected a place which had no ditches near a तीर्थ called Svayana to the south of Sarasvatī (दक्षिणेन सरस्वत्याः स्वयनं तीर्थम् उत्तमम् । तस्मिन् देशे त्व् अनिरिणे तत्र युद्धम् अरोचयन् ॥ ) 9. 54. 13 (Nī., however, on Bom. Ed. 9. 55. 18: अनिरिणे अणूषरे); (9) After the mutual destruc-tion of the Yādavas, Arjuna established Yauyudhāni, son of Sātyaki(n), in the region of Sarasvatī (यौयुधानीम् सरस्वत्यां पुत्रं सात्यकिनः प्रियम् । न्यवेशयत) 16. 8. 69; (10) Sixteen thousand wives of Vāsudeva (Kṛṣṇa) enterd the river Sarasvatī (न्यमज्जन्त सरस्वत्याम्); they then became the Apsarases and returned to Vāsu-deva 18. 5. 21. F. Past and Mythological events: (1) King Matināra performed a sacrificial session lasting for twelve years on the bank of Sarasvatī; after the सत्र was over, Sarasvatī chose Matināra for her hus-band; a son was born to Sarasvatī, Taṃsu by name; this is recorded in a stanza describ-ing lineage (अत्रानुवंशो भवति । तंसुं सरस्वती पुत्रं मतिनाराद् अजीजनत्) 1. 90. 25-28); (2) Describing past events in Kṛṣṇa's life Arjuna said that in a सत्र lasting for twelve years on Sarasvatī Kṛṣṇa discarded his upper garment, became thin, having stretched veins (अपकृष्टोत्तरासङ्गः कृशो धमनिसंततः । आसीः कृष्ण सरस्व-त्यां सत्रे द्वादशवार्षिके ॥ ) 3. 13, 13 (Nī. on 3. 12. 14; अपकृष्टोत्तरासङ्गः त्यक्तोत्त-रीयवस्त्रः); (3) Sarasvatī is one of the seven forms assumed by Gaṅgā on the moun-tain Hiraṇyaśṛṅga (6. 7. 40); these forms became famous as seven Gaṅgās in the three worlds 6. 7. 44-45, 47; (4) Trita fell down at night in a well which was not far away from Sarasvatī 9. 35. 24-25; when Trita requested gods to rescue him from the well, Sarasvatī, full of waves, leapt up and threw Trita out of the well (तत्र चोर्मिमती राजन्न् उत्पपात सरस्वती । तयोत्क्षिप्तस् त्रितस् तस्थौ) 9. 35, 46; (5) Sarasvatī, in bygone days, dis-appeared due to her hatred for Śūdras and Ābhīras; the place where she disappear-ed was named by sages Vinaśana tīrtha (शूद्राभीरान् प्रति द्वेषाद् यत्र नष्टा सरस्वती … तस्मात् तद् ऋषयो नित्यं प्राहुर् विनशनेति ह ॥ ) 9. 36. 1-2; (6) Sarasvatī, flowing towards the east, returned from a certain तीर्थ to the west out of her regard for the sages living in the Naimiṣa forest; formerly, in the Kṛta age, many sages from the Naimiṣa forest, after completing सत्र of twelve years, flocked to Sarasvatī for pilgrimage (तीर्थकारणात्); on account of their large numbers the तीर्थस् on the south bank of Sarasvatī appeared like cities (ऋषीणां बहुलत्वात् तु सरस्वत्या विशां पते । तीर्थानि नगरायन्ते कूले वै दक्षिणे तदा ॥ ); these sages resorted to the bank of Sarasvatī as far as the Samantapañcaka on account of their love for तीर्थस् (तीर्थ-लोभात्); due to the fires of their अग्नीहोत्रस् the river shone (अशोभत सरिच्छ्रेष्ठा); the sages, dwelling near Sarasvatī, beautified the river as do gods the Ganges (शोभयन्-तः सरिच्छ्रेष्ठाम् गङ्गाम् इव दिवौकसः); when other sages arrived there to perform a सत्र they found no place in Kurukṣetra; then Sarasvatī showed herself to the despon-dent sages (ततस् तम् ऋषिसंघातं निरा-शं चिन्तयान्वितम् । दर्शयाम् आस राजेन्द्र तेषाम् अर्थे सरस्वती); the river created for them many bowers, returned (ततः कुञ्जान् बहून् कृत्वा संनिवृत्ता सरिद्वरा), and again flowed towards the west thinking “I shall not render the arrival of the sages futile; now I shall go my way”; this is a great wonder that the river perfor-med (भूयः प्रतीच्यभिमुखी सुस्राव सरितां वरा ॥ अमोघा गमनं (अमोघा-गमनम् ?) कृत्वा तेषां भूयो व्रजाम्य् अहम् । इत्य् अद्भुतं महच् चक्रे ततो राजन् महानदी) 9. 36. 35-53; (7) When Maṅkaṇaka, who was observing chastity (कौमारब्रह्मचारिणः) saw by chance a woman taking bath in Sarasvatī his seed fell into water; when it was collected in a jar by the sage, the seed got divided into seven parts; from it were born seven seers, from whom sprang the Maruts (तत्रर्षयः सप्त जाता जज्ञिरे मरुतां गणाः । … एवम् एते समुत्पन्ना मरुतां जनयिष्णवः) 9. 37. 29-32 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 9. 38. 37 (एतेषां तपसा मरुतो ऽदित्याम् उत्पन्ना इति कल्पान्तरविषयो ऽयम् अर्थः); (8) The Brāhmaṇa Ruṣaṅgu, when he decided to give up his body in old age, asked his sons to carry him to Pṛthūdaka, a तीर्थ on Sarasvatī; when he was carried to the river by his sons, he took bath there (आप्लुतः) and, knowing the qualities of the तीर्थ, told his sons: “one who gives up his body on the northern bank of Sarasvatī will not have to worry about iminent death” (नैनं श्वोमरणं तपेत्) 9. 38. 24-29, (9) Baka Dālbhya, when insulted by Dhṛtarāṣṭra, son of Vicitravīrya (9. 40. 1; probably different from the son of Ambikā and the father of the Kauravas), kindled fire at a desolate तीर्थ on Sarasvatī (अवकीर्णे सरस्वत्यास् तीर्थे प्र-ज्वाल्य पावकम् 9. 40. 12; Nī., however, who reads अवाकीर्णम् takes it as the name of a तीर्थ: अवाकीर्णं नाम दाल्भ्यसेवितं तीर्-थं जगाम Bom. Ed. 9. 41. 1) and started giving offerings of flesh of dead animals; as a result the kingdom of Dhṛtarāṣṭra began to waste away; he was therefore advised to propitiate Baka in a bower in the water of Sarasvatī (अपां कुञ्जे सरस्वत्यास् तं प्रसादय पार्थिव) and request Baka to forgive him for his fault 9. 40. 10-21; (also see No. 27 below); (10) For the sacrifice of Yayāti, son of Nahuṣa, Sarasvatī brought in her currents clarified butter and milk (घृतं पयश् च सुस्राव); in that sacri-fice, Sarasvatī fulfilled the wishes of Brāh-maṇas by producing many juices (?) in accordance with their wishes (यत्र यत्र हि यो विप्रो यान् यान् कामान् अभीप्सति । तत्र तत्र सरिच्छ्रेष्ठा ससर्ज सुबहून् रसान्) 9. 40. 30, 33; (11) Viśvāmitra practised severe austerities on an excellent तीर्थ (not named) of Sarasvatī and became a Brāhmaṇa 9. 39. 23, 28-29; the आश्रम of Vasiṣṭha was at Sthāṇutīrtha on the eastern bank of Sarasvatī and that of Viśvāmitra on the western bank; at the तीर्थ Vasiṣṭhāpavāha, Viśvāmitra was able to displace Vasiṣṭha with the help of severe austerities (वसिष्ठं चालयाम् आस तप-सोग्रेण) 9. 41. 4, 8; Viśvāmitra wanted Sarasvatī to bring Vasiṣṭha to him swiftly so that he could kill him (Vasiṣṭha); Viśvā-mitra therefore thought of Sarasvatī; she appeared before him, trembling with fear, and asked him what she might do for him; Viśvā-mitra told the river what he wanted her to do; hearing that Sarasvatī was pained; she just stood there all the while shaking with fear; Viśvāmitra asked her again to bring Vasiṣṭha quickly to him; she was worried what to do as she was afraid of the curses of both the sages; she went to Vasiṣṭha and informed him what Viśvāmitra's desire was; Vasiṣṭha saw her pale and lean and told her to carry him to Viśvāmitra and save herself from the latter's curse; hearing that Sarasvatī reflected on what she might do which would turn out beneficial to Vasiṣṭha as he had been merciful to her; when she saw on the other bank Viśvāmitra engaged in giving offerings she thought that to be the right moment to act swiftly (सरस्-वत्य् अभ्यचिन्तयत् । इदम् अन्तरम् इत्य् एव 9. 41. 26-27); she washed away a part of her bank on the side of Vasiṣṭha so that he was carried on her current to the आश्रम of Viśvāmitra; while he was being thus carried Vasiṣṭha praised Sarasvatī (Sarasvatī's praise 9. 41. 29-31); Sarasvatī informed Viśvāmitra that she had brought Vasiṣṭha; Viśvāmitra began to look for a weapon to kill Vasiṣṭha; being afraid of the sin of killing a Brāhmaṇa Sarasvatī carried Vasiṣṭha back to the eastern bank (ब्रह्महत्याभयान् नदी । अपोवाह वसिष्ठं तु प्राचीं दिशम् अतन्द्रिता 9. 41. 34); she thus did what both the sages asked her to do, but Viśvāmitra was deceived; enraged, he cursed the river to flow with blood; as a result Sarasvatī flew with water mixed with blood for a year; the sages, gods, Gandharvas and Apsarases were excessively pained to see Sarasvatī in that condition; this is how the तीर्थ Vasiṣṭhāpavāha came into existance 9. 41. 11-39; when Sarasvatī carried blood with water in her current, Rākṣasas came there and were happy to drink blood from the river water; once, some sages, while visiting the तीर्थस्, came to Vasiṣṭhā-pavāha they saw the Rākṣasas drinking blood from the river; they decided to do something to save the river; they invited Sarasvatī and found out from her the cause of the disturbed condition of the तीर्थ (कारणं ब्रूहि कल्याणि किमर्थं ते ह्रदो ह्य् अयम् । एवम् आकुलतां यातः 9. 42. 9); on hearing the cause, they decided to free the river from the curse; by their mere word Sarasvatī returned to her normal condition and her water was as placid as before (तेषां तु वचनाद् एव प्रकृतिस्था सरस्वती । प्रसन्नसलिला जज्ञे यथा पूर्-वम् तथैव हि 9. 42. 13); the excellent river shone as before; since the river water was normal again the Rākṣasas were afflicted by hunger and they requested the sages to relieve them from that condition; the sages praised the river and urged her to relieve the Rākṣasas from their condition; knowing what the sages wanted Sarasvatī brought to her current the river Aruṇā (अरुणाम् आनयाम् आस स्वां तनुम्); bathing in that river the Rākṣasas abandoned their bodies and went to heaven 9. 42. 1-25; (12) While Dadhīca was giving offerings to gods on the bank of Saras-vatī (तस्य तर्पयतो देवान् सरस्वत्याम् 9. 50. 8), the Apsaras Alambusā, sent by Indra to disturb the austerities of Dadhīca, approached him; seeing her divine form the seed of Dadhīca spilled into water of Sara-svatī; the river held it in her womb as she desired to have a son and also because the seed might not be wasted (कुक्षौ चाप्य् अदधत् … तद् रेतः … पुत्रहेतोर् महानदी 9. 50. 10; न विनाशम् इदं गच्छेत् त्वत्तेज इति निश्च-यात् 9. 50. 14); when Sarasvatī delivered the child at proper time she took him to Dadhīca; seeing Dadhīca seated in the assembly of sages she handed over the child to him saying it was his son whom she bore out of her devotion to the sage (ब्रह्मर्षे तव पुत्रो ऽयं त्वद्भक्त्या धारितो मया 9. 50. 12); Dadhīca accepted the child and was very much delighted; he then gave the following boon to Sarasvatī: “all gods, manes, Gandharvas and Apsarases will be satisfied when they receive offerings of your water (तृप्तिं या-स्यन्ति सुभगे तर्प्यमाणास् तवाम्भसा 9. 50. 17); the sage then praised the great river (9. 50. 19-20); he declared that this her son will be known as Sārasvata after the mother's name (तवैव नाम्ना प्रथितः पुत्रस् ते लोकभावनः 9. 50. 21); he also declared that by his grace Sarasvatī would be the holiest of all holy rivers (पुण्याभ्यश् च सरिद्भ्यस् त्वं सदा पुण्यतमा शुभे । भविष्यसि महाभागे मत्प्रसादात् सरस्-वति 9. 50. 23); when praised by the sage and having received a boon from him Sarasvatī went away taking her son with her 9. 50. 5-24; (13) Once there was drought lasting for twelve years; when Sārasvata, like other people, wanted to leave the place and go else-where in search of food, Sarasvatī told him not to leave the place; she assured him to provide food to him in the form of excellent fish; Sārasvata therefore lived there; he ate the food offered by the river and preserved the Vedas 9. 50. 36-38; (14) Bharata, son of Duḥṣyanta and Śakuntalā, bound twenty horses for sacrifice on the bank of Sarasvatī (सरस्वतीं विंशतिं च) 12. 29. 41; (15) Gārgya satisfied Śiva by offering a mental sacrifice on the bank of Sarasvatī (सर्स्वत्यास् तटे तुष्टो मनोयज्ञेन पाण्डव); Śiva then gave him wonderful knowledge of time (कालज्ञानं ममाद्भुतम्), a thousand sons, equal to Gārgya, versed in the exposition of Brahman (तुल्यं मम सहस्रं तु सुतानां ब्रह्मवादिनाम्), and very long life to him and to his sons 13. 18. 25-26; (16) Nahuṣa invited Agastya, who was then on the bank of Sarasvatī, to come to him and draw his carriage (वाहनायाजुहाव सः । द्रुतं सरस्वतीकूलात्) 13. 103. 12; (17) Utathya, angered at the abduction of his wife by Varuṇa, began to drink up water everywhere, compelled the ocean to recede and asked Sarasvatī: “Be invisible in a desert land; when deserted by you let the land be unholy” (अदृश्या गच्छ भीरु त्वं सरस्वति मरुं प्रति । अपुण्य एष भवतु देशस् त्यक्तस् त्वया शुभे) 13. 139. 25-26; (18) Sarasvatī was one of the rivers seen by Mārkaṇḍeya in the belly of the Bāla (3. 186. 83 = Nārāyaṇa 3. 187. 3) 3. 186. 96; (19) Janamejaya asked Vaiśaṃpāyana the origin of the Saptasārasvata tīrtha; Vaiśaṃpāyana then began the narration of a past event in which Sarasvatī, when invited for a sacrifice at different places, appeared there under different names 9. 37. 1, 3-4; (i) When Pitāmaha (Brahmadeva) thought of Sarasvatī she first appeared as Suprabhā at Puṣkara to make the sacrifice of Pitāmaha on this earth highly fruitful (महाफलः); Sarasvatī thus showed her respect for Pitāmaha (पितामहं मानयन्तीम्) 9. 37. 11-14; (ii) When Sarasvatī was thought of by the sages performing a सत्र at Naimiṣa forest she appeared there as Kāñcanākṣī to help the sages (सहायार्थं महात्मनाम्); she was honoured by the sages (पूजिता) 9. 37. 15-18; (iii) When she appeared for the sacrifice of Gaya among the people of Gayā (गयेषु), sages called her Viśālā 9. 37. 20; (iv) In the sacrifice of Auddālaki in the northern Ko-salas when she was thought of by Auddālaka the river appeared there for him (आजगाम सरिच्छ्रेठा तं देशम् ऋषिकारणात्) under the name Manohradā (Mānasahradā in 9. 37. 4) since she was carried there by the sages through the agency of their mind (सा हि तैर् मनसा हृता); the river was honoured there by the sages (पूज्यमाना मुनिगणैः) 9. 37. 21-23; (v) In the Ṛṣabhadvīpa the river appeared with the name Suveṇu 9. 37. 24; (vi) In the sacrifice of Kuru at Kurukṣetra. when invoked by Vasiṣṭha, the river Sarasvatī appeared with the name Ogha-vatī 9. 37. 24-25; (vii) In the sacrifice of Dakṣa at Gaṅgādvāra the river appear-ed as Vimalodā 9. 37. 26 (Vimalodakā 9. 37. 4); when Brahman offered a sacri-fice again he called the river back on the Himavant mountain; the तीर्थ where all the seven forms of the river got united became famous as Saptasārasvata 9. 37. 26-28; (20) When the chariot of Śiva was got ready for his fight with Asuras fighting from the Tripuras the Mahānadīs became its hind parts (जङ्घास् तस्य महानदीः) 8. 24. 69 (Sarasvatī could be one of these ‘big rivers’; but cf. the next); (21) Saras-vatī was the परिरथ्य (?) of Śiva's chariot 8. 24. 75 (however, according to Nī. on Bom. Ed. 8. 34. 34, सरस्वती here means speech: परिरथ्या प्रचारमार्गः । सरस्वती वाग्देवीकल्पितः शब्दमात्रशरीर इत्य् अर्थः); (22) When Hari resorted to another body with the head of a horse for the rescue of the Vedas, Gaṅgā and Sarasvatī became his two eyebrows (गङ्गा सरस्वती पुण्या भ्रुवाव् आस्तां महानदी) 12. 335. 46; (23) The gods, led by Brahman, took with them Skanda and went to Himavant and the river Sarasvatī for his consecration as the general of their army 9. 43. 50-52; they consecrated Skanda at Sthāṇutīrtha on Sarasvatī 9. 41. 6-7; gods consecrated Skanda as their general with the holy waters of Saras-vatī having heavenly waters (सरस्वतीभिः पुण्याभिर् दिव्यतोयाभिर् एव तु । अभ्यषिञ्चन् कुमारं वै) 9. 44. 18-19; (24) Dakṣa told gods that the emaciated Soma (moon) would grow again after bathing in the exce-llent तीर्थ on Sarasvatī (सरस्वत्या वरे तीर्थे उन्मज्जन् शशलक्षणः । पुनर् वर्धिष्यते देवाः); Soma then proceeded to the great तीर्थ Prabāsa on Sarasvatī 9. 34. 67, 69; (25) Sthāṇu (Śiva) offered a sacrifice and honoured Sarasvatī and then established Sthāṇutīrtha on the river 9. 41. 8; (26) When Indra was pursued by the head of Namuci, Pitāmaha (Brahman) asked Indra to offer a sacrifice and to bathe in Aruṇā; Indra then offered a sacrifice in the Kuñja of Sarasvatī and bathed in Aruṇā (सरस्वत्याः कुञ्जे … इष्ट्वा … अरुणायाम् उपास्पृशत्) 9. 42. 34-35; (27) At the तीर्थ (not named) situated near the आश्रम of Baka Dālbhya on the river Sarasvatī (9. 39. 32; 9. 40. 1) Bṛhaspati gave offerings of flesh for the prosperity of gods and the decline of Asuras (असुराणाम् अभावाय भावाय च दिवौकसाम्) 9. 40. 26-27; (28) Sarasvatī was one of the rivers whom Umā wanted to consult on स्त्रीधर्म before expounding it to Śiva as these rivers were well-versed in it; Umā thereby wanted to honour the rivers; the rivers appointed Gaṅgā to speak on their behalf to Umā 13. 134. 13, 19-22, 25. G. Importance: (1) One of the rivers who wait upon Varuṇa in his Sabhā (उपा-सते महात्मानम्) 2. 9. 19, 22; (2) Men-tioned twice in the Daivata-Ṛṣi-Vaṃśa reci-ted by Bhīṣma 13. 151. 14, 22, (2). H. Simile: Draupadī having five Pāṇḍavas as her husbands was very happy with them and they with Draupadī as is Sarasvatī with the Nāgas (बभूव परमप्रीता नागैर् इव सरस्वती) 1. 205. 3 (Nī. on 1. 213. 3: नागैर् गजैः; he, however, adds: सरस्वती बहुसरोयुक्ता वनस्थली । सा हि गजैर् युक्तान्यैश् छेत्तुम् अशक्या । तया च गजा बलिनः । एवं ते मिथो वृद्धिहेतवः). [See Bhogavatī2]
सर्पदर्वी: Sarpadarvī f.: Name of a तीर्थ। Sacred to Nāgas; described as best (तीर्-थम् उत्तमम्); by visiting it (समासाद्य) one gets the fruit of an Agniṣṭoma and wins for himself the world of the Nāgas (नाग-लोक) 3. 81. 12. [See Kapilasya tīrtham]
सर्वदेवह्रद: Sarvadevahrada nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। By bathing there one gets the fruit of gifting a thousand cows 3. 83. 36.
सर्वदेवानां: Sarvadevānāṃ tīrtham nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। Perhaps in the Phalakīvana 3. 81. 72; by bathing there one gets the fruit of gifting a thousand cows 3. 81. 74.
सलिलराजस्य: Salilarājasya tīrtham nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। Situated at the place where the river Sindhu meets the ocean (सागरस्य च सिन्धोश् च संगमं प्राप्य); if one who has con-trolled his mind (प्रयतमानसः) bathes in this तीर्थ and gives offerings to manes, gods and sages (तर्पयित्वा पितॄन् देवान् ऋषींश् च) he shines with his own lustre and goes to the world of Varuṇa (प्राप्नोति वारुणं लोकं दीप्यमानः स्वतेजसा); the wise say (प्रवदन्ति मनीषिणः) that if one worships the god Śaṅkukarṇeśvara there one gets the reward of an Aśvamedha ten times (अश्वमेधं दशगुणम्) 3. 80. 85-87.
सह्य: Sahya m.: Name of a mountain. A. Location: Near the (southern) ocean (लवणाम्भसः । समीपे) 3. 266. 42. B. Importance: (1) One of the eleven mountains listed by Brahman as kings of mountains (एते पर्वतराजानः); (are these mountains also supposed to be characterized by the मध्यम गुण, i. e. by the quality of रजस् ? 14. 43. 1; Nī on Bom. Ed. 14. 43. 1: मध्यमो गुणः रजोगुणप्रधानः; (2) Listed by Saṃjaya among the seven princi-pal mountains (सप्तैते कुलपर्वताः) 6. 10. 10. C. Past event: (1) When Nahuṣa was made the king of the heaven he used to sport with Apsarases and Devakanyās on the Sahya and other mountains 5. 11. 8-10; (2) When Hanūmant and others, in search of Sītā, came out of the residence of Maya in a big cave they saw the Sahya and the Malaya mountains (लवणाम्भसः । समीपे सह्यमलयौ) 3. 266. 42.
सागरोदक: Sāgarodaka nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। Listed in the Tīrthavaṃśa narrated by Aṅgiras to Gautama 13. 26. 9, 3-4; by bath-ing in it (विगाह्य) one rides in a विमान and is awakened (in the morning) by the praises sung by the Apsarases (विबोध्यते विमानस्थः सो ऽप्सरोभिर् अभिष्टुतः) 13. 26. 9.
सामुद्रक: Sāmudraka nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। Near Arundhatīvaṭa; by bathing in this तीर्थ (उपस्पृश्य) and by fasting there for three nights one gets the fruit of giving a thousand cows and lifts up his family (कुलं चैव समुद्धरेत्) 3. 82. 37.
सारस्वतमुनेस्: Sārasvatamunes tīrtham nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। At this तीर्थ, formerly when there was drought lasting for twelve years, the sage Sāra-svata taught Vedas to the Brāhmaṇas 9. 50. 2, 22; Balarāma gave there gifts consisting of wealth (तत्रापि दत्त्वा वसु) 9. 50. 51.
साहस्रक: Sāhasraka nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। Near the तीर्थ called Śatasahasraka; described as famous in the world (लोक-विश्रुत); by bathing in both these तीर्थस् one gets the fruit of giving a thousand cows, and his gifts and fasts give him thou-sandfold rewards (दानं वाप्य् उपवासो वा सहस्रगुणितं भवेत्) 3. 81. 137-138.
सिकताक्ष: Sikatākṣa nt.: Name of a lake ? The Pāṇḍavas were to visit Sikatākṣa after performing the rites near the lake of Cyavana and then reach the Saindhavāraṇya 3. 125. 11-12.
सिन्धु: Sindhu m., f.: Name of a river. A. Location: In the west (2. 29. 2, 8); listed twice by Saṃjaya among the rivers of the Bhāratavarṣa; people used its water for drinking 6. 10. 13, 20; the river Gaṅgā, after descending from Brahmaloka, was first established on the Hiraṇyaśṛṅga mountain; from there it began to flow in seven streams, of which Sindhu was the seventh (तत्र त्रिपथगा देवी … सप्तधा प्रतिपद्यते । … सिन्धुश् च सप्तमी) 6. 7. 44-45; the Bāhlīka (Āraṭṭa) country lies within the region of the five rivers with Sindhu as the sixth flowing through it (पञ्चा-नां सिन्धुषष्ठानां नदीनां ये ऽन्तरा-श्रिताः । तान् … बाह्लीकान् परिवर्जयेत्) 8. 30. 11; (सिन्धुषष्ठा बहिर्गताः ॥ आरट्टा नाम ते देशाः) 8. 30. 35-36; (पञ्च नद्यो वहन्त्य् एता यत्र निःसृत्य पर्वतात् । आरट्टा नाम बाह्लीकाः) 8. 30. 43; the rivers which flow through the Kāśmīramaṇḍala reach Sindhu (काश्मीरमण्डले नद्यो याः पतन्ति महानदम् । ता नदीः सिन्धुम् आसाद्य) 13. 26. 8. B. Description: Characterized as a great Nada (महानद) 13. 26. 8 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 13. 25. 8: नदं सिन्धुम्); (नदस्य महतः) 1. 89. 35; all the rivers, including Sindhu, who wait upon god Śiva are described as auspicious (शिवाः) 13. 134. 22; very holy (पुण्यतमाः) 13. 134. 22; excellent rivers (सरिद्वराः) 13. 134. 14; (सरितां वराः) 13. 134. 19; (सरिच्छ्रे-ष्ठाः) 13. 134. 22; having the waters of all तीर्थस् (सर्वतीर्थोदकैर् युताः) 13. 134. 12; and expert in the knowledge of duties of women (स्त्रीधर्मकुशलाः) 13. 134. 19; the source (प्रभव) of the river Sindhu is frequented by the Siddhas and Gandhar-vas (सिद्धगन्धर्वसेवित) 3. 82. 41; all the rivers listed by Saṃjaya are described as mothers of the universe and very strong 6. 10. 35 (for citation see Atikṛṣṇā). C. Holiness: (1) By staying for five nights at the source of Sindhu one gets much gold (सिन्धोश् च प्रभवं गत्वा … । तत्रोष्य रजनीः पञ्च विन्द्याद् बहु सुवर्ण-कम्) 3. 82. 41; (2) In the Tīrthavaṃśa proclaimed by Aṅgiras to Gautama it is said that one who has a good character if he reaches the rivers which meet Sindhu and also Sindhu he goes to heaven (ता नदीः सिन्धुम् आसाद्य शीलवान् स्वर्गम् आप्नुयात्) 13. 26. 8; (3) There is the तीर्थ of Salilarāja (Varuṇa) at the place where Sindhu meets the ocean (सागरस्य च सिन्धोश् च संग-मं प्राप्य) 3. 80. 85. D. Epic events: (1) Nakula, in his expedition to the west before the Rājasūya, subjugated the powerful Grāmaṇeyas (?) who lived along the banks of Sindhu (सिन्धुकूलाश्रिता ये च ग्राम-णेया महाबलाः) 2. 29. 8; (2) Those who lived along the river Sindhu brought various kinds of tribute to Yudhiṣṭhira for Rājasūya (परिसिन्धु च मानवाः । … विविधं बलिम् आदाय … द्वारि तिष्ठन्ति वारिताः) 2. 47. 9-11; (3) Yudhiṣṭhira staked whatever wealth that belonged to different castes (?), in their order, and who lived to the east of Sindhu (यत् किंचिद् अनुवर्णानाम् प्राक् सिन्धोर् अपि सौबल । एतन् मम धनं राजन्) 2. 58. 5. E. Past events: (1) King Saṃ-varaṇa, when attacked and defeated by Pāñcālya, fled with his family members, ministers and friends and took shelter in a thicket (निकुञ्ज) of the Sindhunada, in the region of the river near the mountain; the Bhāratas lived there for a long time taking resort to the inaccessible land (सिन्धोर् नदस्य महतो निकुञ्जे न्यवसत् तदा । नदीविषयपर्यन्ते पर्वतस्य समीपतः । तत्रावसन् बहून् कालान् भारता दुर्गम् आश्रिताः ॥ ) 1. 89. 33-35; (2) Mārkaṇḍeya saw Sindhu, among other rivers, in the belly of the Bāla (3. 186. 83 = Nārāyaṇa 3. 187. 3) 3. 186. 94. F. Importance: (1) Sindhu is one of the rivers which wait upon Varuṇa in his Sabhā 2. 9. 19; (2) Finds mention in the Daivata-Ṛṣi-Vaṃśa 13. 151. 14, 2. G. Limitation: Sindhu is not included among the rivers which are declared as mothers of fire-hearths, i. e. on the banks of which sacrifices were performed (सिन्धुवर्जं पञ्चनद्यः … एता नद्यस् तु धिष्ण्यानां मातरो याः प्रकीर्तिताः) 3. 212. 21, 24 (for Nī. See Kapilā). H. Simile: (1) Suc-cessful emerging of Kṛṣṇa and Arjuna out of the army led by Droṇa (7. 76. 23) com-pared to crossing Sindhu and other five rivers swollen with water at the end of summer (बाहुभ्याम् इव संतीर्णौ सिन्धुषष्ठाः समुद्रगाः । तपान्ते सरितः पूर्णाः) 7. 76. 28 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 7. 101. 28: सिन्धुः षष्ठो यासां ताश् च शतद्रुविपाशेरावती-चन्द्रभागावितस्ताः); (2) The army of the Pāṇḍavas encountering Śalya was check-ed like the current of Sindhu encountering a mountain (सिन्धोर् वेग इवाचलम्) 9. 9. 6. I. Bad omens: Among the bad omens which occurred when Kṛṣṇa left for Hāstinapura is mentioned one according to which great rivers among whom Sindhu was the fore-most, flowing eastwards, began to flow in the opposite direction (प्रत्यग् ऊहुर् महानद्यः प्राङ्मुखाः सिन्धुसत्तमाः) 5. 82. 6 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 5. 84. 6: प्रत्यक् प्रतीपम् ऊहुः प्रवाहं कृतवत्यः; or does सिन्धु here mean ‘river’ ?). [See Sindhūttama, Salilarājasya tīrtham]

Sindhu, Saindhava m. (pl.): Name of a Janapada and its people; also called Rāṣṭra 8. 4. 11, Viṣaya 14. 76. 2, and Deśa 6. 10. 68; 7. 53. 47; 8. 27. 91; very often mentioned along with Sauvīras. A. Location: Listed twice by Saṃjaya, among the northern Janapadas of Bhārata-varṣa (अत ऊर्धवं जनपदान् निबोध) 6. 10. 37, 5; once, along with Sauvīras (काश्मीराः सिन्धुसौवीरा … ) 6. 10. 52, and then, with Pulindakas (भोजाः सिन्धु-पुलिन्दकाः) 6. 10. 39. B. Description of the country, its warriors, and characteristics of the people and horses: (a) country: sinful (पापदेश) 7. 53. 47; 8. 27. 91; (b) Warriors: brave (शूर) 7. 85. 73; fighting with curved प्रासस् (नखरप्रास-योधिन्) 7. 85. 73; 12. 102. 3; arrogant in battles (युधदुर्मद) 14. 77. 9; Arjuna described Sindhu warriors as doing sinful acts in battles (पापाचारा रणाजिरे) 7. 53. 48; (c) People: (1) They ate rice cooked in milk (सर्वक्षीरान्नभोक्तारः) 7. 53. 48; Madrakas, Sindhus and Sauvīras, according to Karṇa, were म्लेच्छस् born in sinful countries and hence incapable of discerning what was proper धर्म (मद्रकाः सिन्धुसौवीरा धर्मं विद्युः कथं त्व् इह । पापदेशोद्भवा म्लेच्छा धर्माणां अविचक्षणाः) 8. 27. 91; (2) A certain Brāhmaṇa told Dhṛtarāṣṭra in the assembly of the Kurus (8. 30. 7-8, 41) that in the opinion of a certain Rākṣasī (राक्षसी काचिद् अब्रवीत्) Vasātis, Sindhus and Sauvīras were, in general, contemptible (वसातिसिन्धुसौवीरा इति प्रायो विकुत्सिताः) 8. 30. 46-47; (3) Sindhu country was the principal one among the ten राष्ट्रस् which were under the control of Jayadratha (सिन्धुराष्ट्रमुखानीह दश राष्ट्राणि यस्य वै । वशे तिष्ठन्ति वीरस्य) 8. 4. 11; (d) The Sindhu horses yoked to the chariot of Jayadratha were obedient to the charioteer; they drew the chariot well, moving in different directions; were large and speedy like wind ( … सारथेर् वश्याः सैन्धवाः साधुवाहिनः । विकुर्वाणा बृहन्तो ऽश्वाः श्वसनोपमरंहसः ॥ ) 7. 42. 2; the horses of the Sindhu country which were chosen by Bāhuka (Nala) to go to the Vidarbha country were endowed with energy and strength, were of noble breed and good temper, free from interior marks, of broad nostrils and large jaws, blameless as they were free from ten curls, and having the speed of wind; though lean they were capable (of going long dis-tances) and enduring on roads (तेजोबल-समायुक्तान् कुलशीलसमन्वितान् । वर्जिताल्̃ लक्षणैर् हीनैः पृथुप्रोथान् महाहनून् । शुद्धान् दशभिर् आवर्तैः सिन्धुजान् वात-रंहसः ॥ ; कृशान् अश्वान् समर्थान् अध्वनि क्षमान्) 3. 69. 12, 11, 17 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 3. 71. 13-14 (सीलं सादिचित्तानु-सारिता हीनैर् लक्षणैः शतपदीप्रभृति-भिर् वर्जितान् । प्रोथं नासिका॑हनुः अधरं मुखफलकम् । शुद्धान् ह्रदा-वर्तादिदुष्टावर्तहीनान् सिन्धुजान् सिन्धु-देशजान् । ). C. Epic events: (1) The kings of Saindhavas, subdued by Pāṇḍavas, attended the Rājasūya of Yudhiṣṭhira and acted as servers (यत्र सर्वान् महीपालान् शस्त्रतेजोभयार्दितान् । … सैन्धवांस् तथा । … यज्ञे ते परिवेषकान् ॥ ) 3. 48. 18, 21-22; (2) Jayadratha suggested to Draupadī to abandon Pāṇḍavas who had lost their kingdom and marry him so that she could, along with him, rule over the entire Sindhu and Suvīra countries (अखिलान् सिन्धुसौवीरान् अवाप्नुहि मया सह) 3. 251. 18; the warriors of the Śibi, Sindhu and Trigarta countries were dejected to see Pāṇḍavas fighting with them 3. 255. 3; Arjuna killed the Saindhavas who happened to come within the range of his arrows (त्रिगर्तान् सैन्धवान् अपि । जघान … बाण-गोचरम् आगतान्) 3. 255. 28; when Jaya-dratha fled, Arjuna asked Bhīma not to kill any longer Saindhava warriors (वारयाम् आस निघ्नन्तं भीमं सैन्धवसैनिकान्) 3. 255. 36; the inmates of the आश्रम were delighted to see Yudhiṣṭhira return with abducted Draupadī after defeating the Sindhu and Sauvīra armies (जित्वा तान् सिन्धुसौवी रान्) 3. 255. 50; (3) Jaya-dratha, of the Sindhu country, joined the army of Duryodhana (जयद्रथमुखाश् चान्ये सिन्धुसौवी रवासिनः) 5. 19. 19: (4) Before the start of the war, the Kṣatriyas of the Sindhu country and others, headed by Bhīṣma, stood in the front position of the army (भीष्मो ऽग्रतः सर्वसैन्यस्य वृद्धः … क्षत्रिया ये च सिन्धौ) 6. 20. 9-10; (5) On the second day of war, Sindhu warriors and Sauvīras (सिन्धु-सौवीराः), led by Śakuni, protected Droṇa who was behind Bhīṣma in the Mahāvyūha of Kauravas 6. 47. 10, 14; (6) On the third day, Sindhu warriors and Sauvīras (सिन्धुसौवीराः) were posted at the ‘neck’ position (ग्रिवायाम्) of the Garuḍa-vyūha of Kauravas 6. 52. 2-3, 5; (7) On the eighth dav, Irāvān, son of Arjuna, attacked the Kaurava army with horses of different countries some of them being those from the Sindhu country (वाजिनाम् ।  … सिन्धुजानां च सर्वशः); the horses were swift like wind (हयैर् वातजवैर् … ) 6. 86. 3, 5-6; (8) On the thirteenth day, Arjuna assured Kṛṣṇa that he would kill the next day the Saindhava warriors along with their kings (मया सराजका बाणैर् नुन्ना नंक्ष्यन्ति सैन्धवाः) 7. 53. 48; (9) On the fourteenth day, Yudhiṣṭhira pointed out to Sātyaki that Arjuna, pro-ceeding towards Jayadratha, was encircled by the Sindhu warriors and Sauvīras (संवृतः सिन्धुसौवीरैः) 7. 85. 73; Sātyaki told Yudhiṣṭhira that Saindhavas were no match for Arjuna (सैन्धव-पौरवाः । … एते ऽर्जुनस्य क्रुद्धस्य कलां नार्हन्ति षोडशीम्) 7. 86. 28-29; on that day the Kaurava army which included Sindhu warriors and Sauvīras ran helter-skelter since they were being killed by the arrows of Bhīma and Karṇa fighting each other (ततो व्युदस्तं तत् सैन्यं सिन्धु-सौवीरकौरवम्); they ran away from them in all directions; the earth was covered with their bodies along with their armours, arrows and banners; when Karṇa saw the destruction of the Kurus Sauvīras and Sain-dhavas he was ablaze with anger (दृष्ट्वा च कुरुसौवी रसैन्धवानां बलक्षयम्) 7. 113. 11-14; 7. 114. 17-18; (10) During the night war (fourteenth-fifteenth day) all Saindhavas and others, afraid, (simply) watched Karṇa who alone could withstand the shower of weapons released at him by Ghaṭotkaca; they respected his compo-sure in battle (असंमोहं पूजयन्तोऽस्य संख्ये) 7. 154. 45; (11) After the war, the women of Sindhu, Sauvīra and other countries kept a watch on the dead body of Jayadratha (सिन्धुसौवी रगान्धार-काम्बोजयवनस्त्रियः) 11. 22. 11; (12) When Arjuna reached the Sindhu country along with Aśvamedha horse, the warriors and their kings fought a fierce battle with him; they encircled Arjuna so that he look-ed like a bird moving in a cage (कोष्ठकी-कृत्य कौन्तेयम् … अयोधयन् । स … ददृशे  … पञ्जरान्तरसंचारी शकुन्त इव … ॥ ) 14. 76. 10, 13; Arjuna swooned for a while due to the shower of the arrows of Sindhu fighters (सैन्धवाः) 14. 76. 21-23; when he recovered, he started showering arrows so that the Saindhava warriors and their kings could not be seen; the Sain-dhavas were afraid due to the sound (of the bow); they ran, wept due to sorrow and lay down on the ground; the army (of Saindhavas) was thus torn by Arjuna (ततस् ते सैन्धवा योधाः सर्व एव सराजकाः । नादृश्यन्त शरैः कीर्णाः … ॥ तस्य शब्देन वित्रेसुर् भयार्ताश् च विदु-द्रुवः । मुमुचुश् चाश्रुशोकार्ताः सुषुपुश् चापि सैन्धवाः ॥ … सैन्यं विदार्य) 14. 76. 28-29, 32; the Saindhava warriors were once again ready to fight with Arjuna and they showered arrows at him; Arjuna told them that he would not kill them if they surrendered; but Saindhava warriors conti-nued to shoot arrows; the kings of the Sindhu country remembering the death of Jayadratha threw प्रासस् and शक्तिस् on Arjuna; he cut off their missiles before they reached him; the warriors, desirous of victory, continued their attack (आपत-तां तेषां योधानां जयगृद्धिनाम्) 14. 77. 18; Arjuna cut off their heads; they ran away but returned and although they were being killed they fought with Arjuna according to their vigour and energy (यथाप्राणं यथोत्साहं योधयाम् आसुर् अर्जुनम्) most of them, whose horses were tired, swooned (कृता विसंज्ञा भू-यिष्ठाः क्लान्तवाहनसैनिकाः); knowing their plight, Duḥśalā, daughter of Dhṛta-rāṣṭra, took her grandson with her and approached Arjuna wishing peace for the surviving warriors (शान्त्यर्थं सर्व-योधानाम्; शमार्थं सर्वयोधानाम्); she requested him to cease fighting with Sain-dhavas (शमं गच्छ धनंजय); thus Arjuna defeated Saindhava warriors 14. 77. 2-43. D. Past event: Vidurā exhorted her son not to let himself be dispirited and be under the control of the maidens of Sindhu country (मा च सैन्धवकन्या-नाम् अवसन्नो वशं गमः) 5. 132. 32; she told him that she would honour him if he was able to kill all Saindhava warriors (अथ त्वां पूजयिष्यामि हत्वा वै सर्वसैन्-धवान्) 5. 133. 19. सिन्धूत्तम: Sindhūttama nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। Situated near the Vasordhārā tīrtha 3. 80. 92; described as famous (ख्यात) and destroying all sins (सर्वपापप्रणाशन); by bathing there one gets much gold (लभेद् बहु सुवर्णकम्) 3. 80. 95; finds mention in the Daivata-Ṛṣi-Vaṃśa 13. 151. 19, 2.
सिन्धोस्: Sindhos tīrtham nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। Described as great (महन्त्); Lopāmudrā met Agastya there and chose him for her husband 3. 130. 6.
सीता: Sītā1 f.: Name of a river. A. Location: One of the seven streams of the divine river Tripathagā into which it was divided after it was established on Hiraṇyaśṛṅga mountain (ब्रह्मलोकाद् अप-क्रान्ता सप्तधा प्रतिपद्यते) 6. 7. 44-45. B. Past event: Sītā was one of the rivers seen by Mārkaṇḍeya in the belly of the Bāla (3. 186. 83 = Nārāyaṇa 3. 187. 3) 3. 186. 93. C. Importance: Finds mention in the Daivata-Ṛṣi-Vaṃśa 13. 151. 22, 2.

Sītā2 f.: Name of a river. A certain river apparently famous for its whirlpools in which boats sink (सीता नाम नदी राजन् प्लवो यस्यां निमज्जति) 12. 83. 44 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 12. 82. 44: यथा बह्वावर्तायां सीतायां प्लवस् तारणोपायः निमज्जति … )

Sītā3 f.: Name of a river. One of the rivers of the Śākadvīpa 6. 12. 30; all the rivers of the Śākadvīpa are said to be holy (पुण्याः) 6. 12. 32, having holy water (नद्यः पुण्यजलास् तत्र) 6. 12. 29, (पुण्योदाः) 6. 12. 31, and excellent (सरिद्-वराः) 6. 12. 32; Indra takes water from these rivers to give it as rain (यतो वर्षति वासवः) 6. 12. 31.
सुकुमारी: Sukumārī f.: Name of a river. One of the rivers of the Śākadvīpa 6. 12. 30 (for other details see Sītā3).
सुगन्धा: Sugandhā f.: Name of a river. Described as famous in the world (लोक-विश्रुता) 3. 82. 32; by visiting it one is glori-fied in heaven (अभिगम्य … स्वर्गलोके महीयते) 3. 82. 9; he is also freed of all sins and is glorified in the world of Brahman (ततो गच्छेत राजेन्द्र सुगन्धाम् … । सर्व-पापविशुद्धात्मा ब्रह्मलोके महीयते) 3. 82. 32.
सुतीर्थक: Sutīrthaka nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। Described as unsurpassed (अनुत्तम) 3. 81. 44; gods and manes are always present there; by bathing there and by worshipping gods and manes (पितृदेवार्चने रतः) one gets the fruit of a horse sacrifice and goes to the world of manes (पितृलोकं च गच्छति) 3. 81. 44-45.
सुदिन: Sudina nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। Mentioned along with the तीर्थ Ahar; described as one of difficult access (सुदुर्-लभ); by bathing there one goes to the world of the sun (सूर्यलोकम् अवाप्नुयात्) 3. 81. 84.
सुधामन्: Sudhāman m.: Name of a mountain. One of the six mountains of the Kuśa-dvīpa; described as full of corals and difficult to be assaulted (पर्वतो विद्रुमैश् चितः । सुधामा नाम दुर्धर्षः) 6. 13. 9; all the six mountains of Kuśadvīpa are said to be the best mountains (षड् एते पर्वतोत्तमाः) 6. 13. 11; the distance between the six moun-tains doubles as one goes from one to the other (तेषाम् अन्तरविष्कम्भो द्विगुणः प्रविभा-गशः) 6. 13. 11.
सुनसा: Sunasā f.: Name of a river. Listed by Saṃjaya among the rivers of the Bhāratavarṣa; people used its water for drinking 6. 10. 30, 13; all the rivers listed by Saṃjaya are said to be mothers of the universe and very strong 6. 10. 35 (for cita-tion see Atikṛṣṇā).
सुन्दरिकातीर्थ: Sundarikātīrtha nt., Sundarikāhrada m.: Name of a तीर्थ, a sacred lake. Described as visited by Siddhas (सिद्-धनिषेवित) 3. 82. 51; by reaching it (सुन्दरिकातीर्थं प्राप्य) one gets a good form; this has been told in the old (text) (रूपस्य भागी भवति दृष्टम् एतत् पुरा-तने) 3. 82. 51; by bathing in the Sundarikā-hrada at proper time and place (?) one receives from the Aśvins good form and lustre in the next birth (देशकाल उपस्पृश्य तथा सुन्दरिकाह्रदे । अश्विभ्यां रूपवर्चस्यं प्रेत्य वै लभते नरः) 13. 26. 19 (Nī., who reads रूपवर्चस्कम्, on Bom. Ed. 13. 25. 21: रूपवर्चसोः समाहारः रूपवर्-चस्कं वर्चस् तेजः । ; on 13. 25. 6 प्रेत्य-भावे जन्मान्तरे).
सुप्रभा: Suprabhā f.: Name of a river. A. Location: Flowing through the Puṣkaras (पुष्करेषु वै । सुप्रभा नाम) 9. 37. 12, 14. B. Description: Flowing with speed (वेगयुक्ता) 9. 37. 13; best among rivers (सरिच्छ्रेष्ठा) 9. 37. 14. C. Past events: One of the seven forms of Sarasvatī which cover the whole world (सप्त सरस्वत्यो याभिर् व्याप्तम् इदं जगत्) 9. 37. 3; when Pitāmaha (Brahman) was offering a sacrifice on this earth (पिता-महस्य महतो वर्तमाने महीतले । वितते यज्ञवाटे 9. 37. 5) the sages said that the sacrifice will not bear great fruit as Sarasvatī was not present; then god Pitā-maha thought of Sarasvatī and invited her to appear at the Puṣkaras; the river appeared there under the name Suprabhā (सुप्रभा नाम राजेन्द्र नाम्ना तत्र सरस्वती; एवम् एषा सरिच्छ्रेष्ठा पुष्करेषु सरस्वती); Sarasvatī appeared there for the sake of Pitāmaha and for the satisfaction of the sages 9. 37. 5-14.
सुप्रयोगा: Suprayogā f.: Name of a river. Listed by Saṃjaya among the rivers of the Bhāratavarṣa; people used its water for drinking 6. 10. 20, 13; all the rivers listed by Saṃjaya are said to be mothers of the uni-verse and very strong 6. 10. 35 (for citation see Atikṛṣṇā); listed by Mārkaṇḍeya among rivers which are famous as mothers of the fire-hearths i. e. on the banks of which sacrifices were performed (एता नद्यस् तु धिष्ण्यानां मातरो याः प्रकीर्तिताः) 3. 212. 24 (for Nī. see Kapīlā).
सुभूमिक: Subhūmika nt., Subhūmikā f.: Name of a तीर्थ। A. Location: Situated on the bank of Sarasvatī (सुभूमिकं … सरस्वत्यास् तटे वरे) 9. 36. 3; (सुभूमिकेति विख्याता सर-स्वत्यास् तटे वरे) 9. 36. 8. B. Descrip-tion: Holy (पुण्य) 9. 36. 5; resorted to by Brāhmaṇas (ब्राह्मणसेवित) 9. 36. 5; auspicious sporting ground of the Apsarases (आक्रीडभूमिः … अप्सरसां शुभा) 9. 36. 8. C. Characteristics: (1) There the shining Apsarases sport at all times without lassitude (तत्र चाप्सरसः शुभ्रा नित्य-कालम् अतन्द्रिताः । क्रीडाभिर् विमलाभिश् च क्रीदन्ति) 9. 36. 4; (2) Hosts of Gandharvas and Apsarases are seen there together as they meet and as long as they wish (समेत्य सहिता राजन् यथाप्राप्तं यथासुखं) 9. 36. 6. D. Holiness: (1) The holy तीर्थ is visited by gods and Gandharvas every month 9. 36. 5; (2) There gods and manes, showered again and again at all times with holy and divine flowers along with plants (?) (सवी-रुधः । पुण्यैः पुष्पैः सदा दिव्यैः कीर्यमानाः पुनः पुनः ॥ ), take delight 9. 36. 7. E. Epic event: Balarāma went to it from Vinaśana; he bathed there and offered wealth to Brāhmaṇas; he heard there heavenly music (of the Apsarases) and sound of musical instruments; he also saw there many shadows of gods, Gandharvas and Rakṣases (छायाश् च विपुला दृष्ट्वा देव-गन्धर्वरक्षसाम्) 9. 36. 3, 9-10.
सुरोद: Suroda m.: Name of an ocean. One of the oceans surrounding the Dvīpas in the north 6. 13. 1-2.
सुवर्णाक्ष: Suvarṇākṣa nt. Name of a तीर्थ। A. Description: Described as famous in the three worlds (त्रिषु लोकेषु विश्रुतम्) 3. 82. 16. B. Holiness: By visiting this तीर्थ (अभिगम्य) and by worshipping there Vṛṣadhvaja (Śiva) one gets the fruit of a horse sacrifice and the status of a Gaṇa-pati (गाणपत्यं च विन्दति) 3. 82. 19. C. Past event: Formerly Viṣṇu propiti-ated Rudra to win his favour; as a result he obtained many boons from Rudra; Rudra, who was satisfied, said that Kṛṣṇa would be more dear (to people) than Śiva and that he would be the foremost in the whole world (अपि चास्मत् प्रियतरो लोके कृष्ण भविष्यसि । त्वन्मुखं च जगत् कृत्स्नं भविष्यति न संशयः ॥ ) 3. 82. 16-18 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 3. 84. 21: त्वन्मुखं त्वत्प्रधा-नम्).
सुवामा: Suvāmā f.: Name of a river. Listed by Saṃjaya among the rivers of the Bhāratavarṣa; people used its water for drinking 6. 10. 27, 13; all the rivers listed by Saṃjaya are said to be mothers of the uni-verse and very strong 6. 10. 35 (for citation see Atikṛṣṇā).
सुवास्तु: Suvāstu f.: Name of a river. Listed by Saṃjaya among the rivers of the Bhāratavarṣa; people used its water for drinking 6. 10. 24, 13; all the rivers listed by Saṃjaya are said to be mothers of the universe and very strong 6. 10. 35 (for cita-tion see Atikṛṣṇā).
सुवेणा: Suveṇā f.: Name of a river. One of the rivers seen by Mārkaṇḍeya in the belly of the Bāla (3. 186. 83 = Nārā-yaṇa 3. 187. 3) 3. 186. 95.
सवेणु: Saveṇu f.: Name of a river. One of the seven forms of the river Sarasvatī which pervade the whole world (याभिर् व्याप्तम् इदम् जगत्) 9. 37. 3-4; when Sarasvatī was invited by sages perform-ing the sacrifice at the holy Ṛṣabhadvīpa the river Sarasvatī appeared there as Suveṇu 9. 37. 24; when Sarasvatī was invited again by Brahman at his sacrifice on the Hima-vant all the seven streams gathered there together in the form of the Saptasārasvata tīrtha 9. 37. 26-27.
सुशृङ्ग: Suśṛṅga m.: Name of a mountain. One of the mountains seen by Arjuna when he, along with Kṛṣṇa, went at night through the sky to propitiate Śiva in order to get his Pāśupata 7. 57. 28, 16-17.
सूर्यतीर्थ: Sūryatīrtha nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। One who has controlled his mind (नियत-मानसः) if he visits this तीर्थ, bathes there, and worships manes and gods while observ-ing fast (उपवासपरायणः) he gets the fruit of an Agniṣṭoma and goes to the world of the sun (सूर्यलोकं च गच्छति) 3. 81. 39.
सूर्योदयगिरि: Sūryodayagiri m.: Designation of the eastern mountain. The mountain from behind which the sun rises; it is situated at the other end of the Himavant, near the Vāriṣeṇa ocean and the river Lohitya (Brahmaputra) (ये परार्धे हिमवतः सूर्योदयगिरौ नृपाः । वारिषेणसमुद्रान्ते लोहित्यम् अभितश् च ये) 2. 48. 8; the kings who lived there and the Kirātas brought various kinds of tributes for the Rājasūya sacrifice of Yudhiṣṭhira 2. 48. 8-11. [See Udaya and Udyant]
सैन्धवारण्य: Saindhavāraṇya nt.: Name of a forest. A. Location: In the west (प्रतीच्याम्) 3. 87. 1. B. Description: Holy (पुण्य), famous (ख्यात), and visited by Brāhmaṇas (द्विजनिषेवित) 3. 87. 12. C. Characteri-stic: There were many canals there; Lomaśa advised Yudhiṣṭhira to visit them (सैन्ध-वारण्यं आसाद्य कुल्यानां कुरु दर्श-नम्) 3. 125. 12.
सोमगिरि: Somagiri m.: Name of a mountain. Described as holy (पुण्य); listed by Bhīṣma in the Daivata-Ṛṣi-Vaṃśa 13. 151. 27, 2.
सोमतीर्थ: Somatīrtha1 nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। On the river Jayantī (in Kurukṣetra 3. 81. 2); by bathing in it one gets the fruit of a Rājasūya 3. 81. 16.

Somatīrtha2 nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। Situated on the river Sarasvatī 3. 81. 93; described as unsurpassed (अनुत्तम); by bathing in it one goes to the world of Soma (सोमलोकम् अवाप्नुयात्) 3. 81. 96, 162 (identical with Somasya tīrtham ?).
सोमश्रवायण: Somaśravāyaṇa nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। The Pāṇḍavas, along with Kuntī, on their way to the Pāñcāla country reached the Somaśravāyaṇa tīrtha on the river Gan-ges; Aṅgāraparṇa, the king of the Gandhar-vas, had come there with his women to sport in the waters of Gaṅgā 1. 158. 2, 4.
सोमस्य: Somasya tīrtham nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। A. Description: Great (महन्त्) 9. 42. 38; 9. 49. 65. B. Epic event: Balarāma reached there from the तीर्थ Vasiṣṭhāpavāha 9. 42. 38; (9. 41. 39); he reached there also from Ādityatīrtha 9. 48. 16; 9. 49. 65; from there he went to the तीर्थ of the sage Sārasvata 9. 50. 2; Balarāma bathed there (उपस्पृश्य) and gave gifts 9. 50. 2. C. Past event: Soma formerly performed Rājasūya sacrifice at this तीर्थ in which Atri acted as the Hotṛ priest; at the end of the sacrifice a fierce battle was fought between the gods and the Dānavas, Daiteyas and Rākṣasas in which Skanda killed Tāraka 9. 42. 39-41; 9. 50. 1; (identical with Soma-tīrtha2 ?).
सौगन्धिकवन: Saugandhikavana nt.: Name of a forest. A. Location: In the north (अस्यां दिशि वरिष्ठायाम् उत्तरस्याम्) 5. 109. 3; in the north-west; the wind blowing from the north-west (पूर्वोत्तरो वायुः) carried with it a lotus flower having heavenly fragrance to Draupadī 3. 146. 6-7; on the Gandhamādana mountain 3. 150. 16; it was on a river, full of golden lotuses and Kāraṇḍaka and Cakra-vāka birds, on this mountain 3. 150. 27. B. Description: Great (महन्त्), causing de-light (प्रीतिजनन), and having the lustre of the morning sun (बालार्कसदृशद्युति) 3. 150. 27. C. Characteristics: (1) Brah-man and other gods, sages practising austeri-ties, Siddhas, Cāraṇas and Gandharvas, Kiṃ-naras, along with big serpents (समहोर-गाः) lived there 3. 82. 3-4; (2) The garden of Kubera, having heavenly lotus flowers, was in Saugandhikavana 3. 149. 22; (3) Suparṇa told Gālava that it was protected by the Nairṛta demons 5. 109. 10. D. Holiness: Just by entering this forest (तद् वनं प्र-विशन्न् एव) one is freed of all sins 3. 82. 4. E. Epic events: (1) Hanūmant showed Bhīma the way to Saugandhikavana 3. 149. 22; (2) Bhīma roamed through the forests and gardens on the Gandhamādana mountain to find out the Saugandhika forest 3. 150. 18; (3) Bhīma saw the forest on a river 3. 150. 27.
सौभद्र: Saubhadra nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। A. Location: One of the five तीर्थस् on the southern ocean (समुद्रे तीर्थानि दक्षिणे) 1. 208. 1; on watery land along the southern ocean (दक्षिणे सागरानूपे) 1. 209. 17. B. Description: Described as an exce-llent तीर्थ of the great sage (Subhadra ?) (सौभद्रम् … महर्षेस् तीर्थम् उत्तमम्) 1. 208. 8; all the five तीर्थस् are said to be holy, very holy (पुण्यानि) 1. 209. 11, 17; (सुपुण्यानि) 1. 208. 1; purifying the wise (पावनानि मनीषिणाम्) 1. 209. 11; pleasing (रमणीयानि) 1. 209. 17; (once) adorned by the ascetics (शोभितानि तपस्विभिः) 1. 208. 1, but later avoided by them and hence desolate (विविक्तानि … वर्ज्यमानानि मुनि-भिः) 1. 208. 2, 4; all the five तीर्थस् became famous as Nārītīrthas 1. 209. 11 C. Epic event: Arjuna asked the ascetics why the तीर्थस् were avoided by sages who discoursed on Brahman (तीर्थानीमानि वर्ज्यन्ते किमर्-थं ब्रह्मवादिभिः) 1. 208. 5; the ascetics told him that they were avoided because of the fear of five crocodiles residing in the तीर्थस् 1. 208. 6; when Arjuna entered the Saubhadra तीर्थ for a bath a crocodile caught hold of him; the crocodile was really an Apsaras, Vargā by name 1. 208. 8, 14; (Arjuna releas-ed the five Apsarases from curse 1. 209. 21) [See Nāritirthāni.]
स्तनकुण्ड: Stanakuṇḍa nt. (pl.): Name of a sacred bathing place. One can reach it by ascending the famous Gaurīśikhara (शिखरं वै महादेव्या गौर्यास् त्रैलोक्यविश्रुतम् । (समारुह्य … स्तनकुण्डेषु संविशेत्); while visiting the place one should be a believer (श्राद्धः); by bathing there (अभिषेकं कुर्वाणः) and by worshipping manes and gods (पितृदेवार्चने रतः) one gets the fruit of a horse sacrifice and goes to the world of Śakra (Indra) 3. 82. 131-132. [See Gauryāḥ śikharaṃ]
स्थाणुतीर्थ: Sthāṇutīrtha nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। A तीर्थ on the river Sarasvatī (तस्मिन् सरस्वतीतीर्थे) 9. 41. 8; at Sthāṇutīrtha, on the eastern bank of the river, was the big आश्रम of Vasiṣṭha; Sthāṇu (Śiva) practised severe austerities there; Sthāṇu offered a sacrifice there, worshipped Sarasvatī and established the तीर्थ, known after him, as Sthāṇutīrtha; at this तीर्थ gods consecrated Skanda as the chief of their army; at this तीर्थ Viśvāmitra moved Vasiṣṭha from the eastern to the western bank 9. 41. 4-8. [See Vasiṣṭhāpavāha]
स्थाणुवट: Sthāṇuvaṭa m.: Name of a तीर्थ। Described as famous in the three worlds (त्रिषु लोकेषु विश्रुतम्); by bathing there and by passing one night there (तत्र स्नात्वा स्थितो रात्रिं) one gets the world of Rudra 3. 81. 155.
स्थूलवालुका: Sthūlavālukā f.: Name of a river. Listed by Saṃjaya among the rivers of the Bhāratavarṣa; people used its water for drinking 6. 10. 14, 13; all the rivers listed by Saṃjaya are said to be mothers of the uni-verse and very strong 6. 10. 35 (for citation see Atikṛṣṇā); Sthūlavālukā is listed among the rivers by visiting which the high-souled ones who have observed vows (महात्मानो धृतव्रताः) obtain heavenly form, become auspicious, and wearing heavenly garlands and rich in holy fragrance they reach the world of cows (गवां लोके 13. 105. 42; मोदन्ति गवां विमाने 13. 105. 44) 13. 105. 46, 48 (for citation see Karatoyinī).
स्वयन: Svayana nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। A. Location: On the southern bank of Sarasvatī (दक्षिणेन सरस्वत्याः स्वयनं तीर्थम्) 9. 54. 13; near Samantapañcaka 9. 54. 5, 7; towards the west of the main battle-field (प्रतीच्यभिमुखं देशम्) 9. 54. 12. B. Description: Best (उत्तम) 9. 54. 13; level land having no holes in the earth (तस्मिन् देशे त्व् अनिरिणे) 9. 54. 13 (Nī., however, on Bom. Ed. 9. 55. 18: अनिरिणे अनूषरे) C. Epic event: A place near this तीर्थ was selected by the warriors for the final duel between Bhīma and Duryodhana (तत्र युद्-धम् अरोचयन्) 9. 54. 13.
स्वयंभुवो: Svayaṃbhuvo vanam nt.: Name of a forest. Shown by Lomaśa to Yudhiṣṭhira; Viśva-karman Svayaṃbhū offered a sacrifice in this forest in which he gave the entire earth as दक्षिणा to Kaśyapa (यस्मिन् यज्ञे हि भूर् दत्ता कश्यपाय महात्मने । सपर्वत-वनोद्देशा दक्षिणा वै स्वयंभुवा) 3. 114. 17-18.
स्वर्गतीर्थ: Svargatīrtha nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। According to the Tīrthavaṃśa proclaimed by Aṅgiras, by bathing in this तीर्थ for a month (उपस्पृश्य, मासं कृतोदकः) one who has controlled his sense organs (जितेन्-द्रियः) gets the fruit of a Puruṣamedha (फलं पुरुषमेधस्य लभेत्) 13. 26. 32, 3.
स्वर्गद्वार: Svargadvāra nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। One who is controlled and takes limited food (नियतो नियताशनः) if he visits this तीर्थ he goes to heaven and reaches the world of Brahman (स्वर्गलोकम् अवाप्नोति ब्रह्म-लोकं च गच्छति) 3. 81. 145.
स्वर्णबिन्दु: Svarṇabindu m.: Name of a तीर्थ। According to the Tīrthavaṃśa proclaimed by Aṅgiras, one who bathes (विगाह्य) in this तीर्थ is awakened in a Vimāna by the praises of Apsarases 13. 26. 9.
स्वस्तिपुर: Svastipura nt. Name of a तीर्थ। Situated at a place where there is Gaṅgāhrada and a Kūpa containing three crores of तीर्थस् 3. 81. 153; described as purifying (पावनं तीर्थम्) 3. 81. 152; a pilgrim (तीर्थसेवी) by visiting this तीर्थ (आसाद्य) and by satisfying manes and gods gets the fruit of an Agniṣṭoma 3. 81. 152.
संयमन: Saṃyamana (nt.), Saṃyamanī f.: The residence of Yama Vaivasvata, also referred to as Vaivasvatī (13. 105. 16), Pretarajasya bhavanam (3. 160. 9.) A. Location: In the southern direc-tion (यमस् तु राजा धर्मात्मा … दक्षि-णाम् आश्रितो दिशम् ॥ एतत् संयमनं  … प्रेतराजस्य भवनम्) 3. 160. 8-9. B. Relationship with Yama Vaivasvata: Yama lived there, hence called प्रेत-राजस्य भवनम् 3. 160. 9; वैवस्वती 13. 105. 16. C. Description: Holy (पुण्य) 3. 160. 9; pleasing (रम्या) 7. 50. 42; of extremely wonderful sight (अतीवाद्भुतदर्-शन) 3. 160. 9; endowed with great perfec-tion (ऋद्ध्या परमया युतम्) 3. 160. 9; vir-tuous people always went there (सदा सुकृति-नां गतिः) 7. 50. 42. D. Characteristics: (1) Controller of people (जनानां संय-मनी) 13. 105. 16 (this explains the name of the residence); (2) Where untruth is not spoken but only the truth (यत्रानृतं नोच्यते यत्र सत्यम्) 13. 105. 16; (3) Where the weak are able to make the strong ones make amends (यत्राबला बलि-नं यातयन्ति) 13. 105. 16. E. Epic events: (1) Lomaśa showed it to Yudhiṣṭhira holding him by his right hand (युधिष्ठि-रं धौम्यो गृहीत्वा दक्षिणे करे) 3. 160. 3, 9; (2) Arjuna said that when Abhi-manyu would reach Saṃyamanī it would be illumined by his lustre and would shine more brightly 7. 50. 42; there Yama (Vaivasvata), Varuṇa, Śatakratu (Indra) and Dhaneśa (Kubera) will praise Abhi-manyu 7. 50. 43. F. Past event: Gautama told king Dhṛtarāṣṭra (really Indra), who was forcibly taking away his elephant, that he would make Indra compensate for his elephant in the abode of Vaivasvata (वैवस्वती संयमनी जनानाम् … तत्र त्वाहं हस्तिनं यातयिष्ये) 13. 105. 16. G. Mode of expression: संयमनीं गम्-or या- ‘to go to the abode of Yama’ used to express the meaning ‘to die’: (1) The charioteer of Sātyaki wondered who, by opposing him in battle, desired to go to the abode of Yama (केषां संयमनीम् अद्य गन्तुम् उत्सहते मनः) 7. 95. 18; (2) Bhūriśravas told Sātyaki that he (Sā.) would reach the abode of Yama when struck by him (Bhūri.) (अद्य संयमनीं याता मया त्वं निहतो रणे) 7. 117. 10.
संजयन्ती: Saṃjayantī f.: Name of a town. Situated to the south of Indraprastha (प्रययौ दक्षिणां दिशम्) 2. 28. 1; (दक्षिणाभिमुखो ययौ) 2. 28. 8; (प्रायाद्  … दक्षिणाम् दिशम्) 2. 28. 37; Sahadeva in his expedition to the south before the Rājasūya subjugated Saṃjayantī by just sending his messengers and made the people pay tribute (नगरीं संजयन्तीं च … दूतैर् एव वशे चक्रे करं चैनान् अदापयत्) 2. 28. 47.
समन्तपञ्चक: Samantapañcaka nt.: Name of a holy place, also called Kurukṣetrasamantapañca-ka and Pitāmahasya uttaravediḥ or Prajā-pater uttaravediḥ (or uttaravedī) 3. 81. 178 = 9. 52. 20, 1; 9. 54. 5. A. Location: Along the southern bank of the river Sarasvatī (सरस्वत्याः … । तीर्-थानि … कूले वै दक्षिणे तदा । समन्त-पञ्चकं यावत् तावत् ते द्विजसत्तमाः । तीर्थलोभान् … नद्यास् तीरं समाश्रिताः ॥ ) 9. 36. 41-42; a part of Kurukṣetra (9. 52. 1-2), hence called Kurukṣetrasamanta-pañcaka; the land between Tarantuka and Arantuka and between the (five) lakes of Rāma and Macakruka—that is the extent of Kurukṣetrasamantapañcaka (तरन्तुकारुन्तकयोर् यद् अन्तरं राम-ह्रदानां च मचक्रुकस्य । एतत् कुरु-क्षेत्रसमन्तपञ्चकम्) 3. 81. 178 = 9. 52. 20. B. Description: Holy (पुण्य) 1. 1. 11; 1. 2. 7, 11; 9. 63. 39; most holy in the three worlds (महापुण्यतमे त्रैलो-क्यस्य) 9. 54. 6; very ancient (सनातन) 9. 54. 6; pleasing (रमणीय) 1. 2. 11; resorted to by twice-born (द्विजनिषेवित) 1. 1. 11; very pious (परमधर्मिष्ठ) 1. 2. 10; free from the defects of the earth (भू-दोषवर्जित) 1. 2. 10; famous in the three worlds (त्रिषु लोकेषु विश्रुते) 9. 63. 39. C. Characteristic: Rāma created at this place five ponds filled with the blood of the Kṣa-triyas killed by him; the place near these five ponds came to be called Samantapañcaka, since the wise say that a place should be called after the characteristic by which it is distinguished (तेषां समीपे यो देशो ह्रदा-नां रुधिराम्भसाम् । समन्तपञ्चकम् इति पुण्यं तत् परिकीर्तितम् ॥ येन लिङ्गेन यो देशो युक्तः समुपलक्ष्यते । तेनैव नाम्ना तं देशम् वाच्यम् आहुर् मनीषिणः ॥ ) 1. 2. 7-8. D. Holiness: (1) The holy तीर्थस् on the southern bank of Sarasvatī became towns and extended as far as Sama-ntapañcaka (सरस्वत्याः … । तीर्थानि नग-रायन्ते कूले वै दक्षिणे तदा ॥ समन्त-पञ्चकं यावत्) 9. 36. 42; (2) It was called the most ancient उत्तरवेदि of Pra-jāpati (or Pitāmaha) (प्रजापतेर् उत्तरवेदिर् उच्यते सनातना राम समन्तपञ्चकम् । 9. 52. 1, 20; 9. 54. 5 (उत्तरवेदी); (पितामह-स्योत्तरवेदिर् उच्यते) 3. 81. 178; a place in heaven was assured for one who died while fighting at Samantapañcaka (तस्मिन् … सं-ग्रामे निधनं प्राप्य ध्रुवं स्वर्गो भ-विष्यति) 9. 54. 6; 9. 63. 39. E. Epic events: (1) Sūta Ugraśravas visited Samantapañ-caka before he arrived at the सत्र of Śaunaka in the Naimiṣa forest (समन्तपञ्-चकं नाम … ।गतवान् अस्मि तं देशम्) 1. 1. 11; the sages expressed their wish to know more about the place Samantapañ-caka 1. 2. 1; (2) Yudhiṣṭhira asked his men to raise tents in thousands outside Samantapañcaka (समन्तपञ्चकाद् बा-ह्यम्) 6. 1. 6; (3) The battle between the Pāṇḍavas and the Kauravas and between all the kings was fought at Samantapañcaka (युद्धं यत्राभवत् पुरा पाण्डवानां कुरूणां च सर्वेषां च महीक्षिताम्) 1. 1. 11; the battle at Samantapañcaka took place at the junction of the Kali and Dvā-para and where the armies, eighteen अक्षौ-हिणीस् in number had gathered for fighting the battle (अन्तरे चैव सम्प्राप्ते कलिद्वा-परयोर् अभूत् । समन्तपञ्चके युद्धं कुरुपाण्डवसेनयोः ॥ … अष्टादश समाज-ग्मुर् अक्षौहिण्यो युयुत्सया) 1. 2. 9-10; (4) While consoling Subhadrā over the death of Abhimanyu, Kṛṣṇa told her that on the following day she would hear that the head of Jayadratha was severed from his body and carried outside Samantapañ-caka (श्वः शिरः श्रोष्यसे तस्य सैन्धव-स्य रणे हृतम् । समन्तपञ्चकाद् बाह्यं) 7. 54. 20; Kṛṣṇa advised Arjuna to remove the head of Jayadratha and let it fall on the lap of Vṛddhakṣatra (father of Jaya-dratha) who was practising austerities in a forest outside Samantapañcaka (वृद्ध-क्षत्रो वनं यातः … तप्यति … तपो घोरं … । समन्तपञ्चकाद् अस्माद् बहिः) 7. 121. 24-26; Arjuna, after he cut the head of Jayadratha, took it outside Samantapañ-caka with arrows which formed a close clu-ster (शरैः कदम्बकीकृत्य काले तस्मिंश् च पाण्डवः । समन्तपञ्चकाद् बाह्यं शिरस् तद् व्याहरत् ततः ॥ ) 7. 121. 34; (5) Duryodhana suggested to go to Samanta-pañcaka for his duel with Bhīma (समन्त-पञ्चकं क्षिप्रम् इतो याम विशां पते) 9. 54. 5; Yudhiṣṭhira, followed by Duryo-dhana, then went to Samantapañcaka 9. 54. 7; (6) From the तीर्थ of Vṛddha-kanyā, Mādhava (Balarāma) came out of Samantapañcaka (समन्तपञ्चकाद् द्वारात् ततो निष्क्रम्य माधवः) 9. 51. 25. F. Past events: (1) At Samantapañcaka, which was known as the Uttaravedi of Prajāpati, gods formerly offered an excellent सत्र (प्रजापतेर् उत्तरवेदिर् उच्यते … समन्तपञ्चकम् । समीजिरे यत्र पुरा दिवौकसो वरेण सत्रेण) 9. 52. 1; (2) Once many sages arrived at the तीर्थस् on Sarasvatī which extended as far as Sa-mantapañcaka with a view to visiting them; they offered there sacrifices and filled the regions with the sound of their vedic reci-tations (समन्तपञ्चकं यावत् तावत् ते द्विजसत्तमाः । तीर्थलोभान् नरव्याघ्र नद्यास् तीरं समाश्रीताः ॥ ) 9. 36. 42-43; (3) Rāma deprived the earth of the Kṣa-triyas twentyone times and filled at Samanta-pañcaka five ponds with blood (त्रिःसप्त-कृत्वः पृथिवीं कृत्वा निःक्षत्रियां प्र-भुः । समन्तपञ्चके पञ्च चकार रुधि-रह्रदान् ॥ ) 3. 117. 9; 1. 2. 3-4. [see Prajāpateḥ vedi2 Vol. 1. 387-88]
सम्भलग्राम: Sambhalagrāma m.: Name of a village. A. Description: Auspicious (शुभ) 3. 188. 90. B.
