Future event: Mārkaṇḍeya told the Pāṇḍavas that in future (कालान्-तरे ऽन्यस्मिन् 3. 188. 86) Kalki Viṣṇuśarman a Brāhmaṇa will be born in the habitation of the Brāhmaṇas at Sambhalagrāma; he will be a sovereign monarch (कल्किर् विष्णुयशा नाम द्विजः … । उत्पत्स्यते … ॥ संभूतः सम्भलग्रामे ब्राह्मणावसथे शुभे । … स धर्मविजयी राजा चक्रवर्ती भविष्यति) 3. 188. 89-91.
सरकस्य: *Sarakasya (? Sarakastasya) āśramaḥ m.: Name of an आश्रम of Saraka (? Sarakasta). In the north, on the river Sarasvatī (उदीच्यां … दिशि पुण्यानि … आयतनानि) 3. 88. 1; (सरस्वती पुण्यवहा ह्रदिनी … यत्र) 3. 88. 2; (सरस्वती नदी सद्भिः … पूजिता) 3. 88. 9; described as extremely holy and famous (अत्यन्तम् आश्रमः पुण्यः सरकस् तस्य (? सरकस्तस्य) विश्रुतः) 3. 88. 8. [For Saraka, a तीर्थ see Vol. I. 466]
सरस्वत्या: Sarasvatyā āyatanam nt.: A holy resort (temple ?) sacred to Sarasvatī. A. Location: Located in the famous forest near Śūrpāraka, not very far from the sea (शूर्पारकं पुण्यतमं ददर्श । तत्रोदधेः कंचिद् अतीत्य देशं ख्यातं पृथिव्यां वनम् आससाद । … सरस्व-त्याः । … आयतनानि तेषां ददर्श) 3. 118. 8-9, 13). For B. Description and C. Epic event See Bhagasya āyatanam.
साध्यगणस्य: Sādhyagaṇasya āyatanam nt.: A holy resort (temple ?) sacred to the Sādhyas. A. Location: Located in a holy forest, famous on the earth, near Śūrpāraka and not very far from the sea (शूर्पारकं ददर्श ॥ तत्रोदधेः कंचिद् अतीत्य देशं ख्यातं पृथिव्यां वनम् आससाद ॥ … साध्यगणस्य चैव … आयतनानि तेषाम् ददर्श) 3. 118. 8-9, 12-13. For B. Des-cription and C. Epic event see Bhagasya āyatanam.
सिंहपुर: Siṃhapura nt.: Name of a city.
सिद्धगणस्य: Siddhagaṇasya āyatanam nt.: A holy resort (temple ?) sacred to the Siddhas. A. Location: Situated in the forest, well known on the earth, near Śūrpāraka, not very far from the sea (शूर्पारकं … ददर्श ॥ तत्रोदधेः कंचिद् अतीत्य देशं ख्यातं पृथिव्यां वनम् आससाद । … सिद्धगणस्य चैव … आयतनानि तेषां ददर्श) 3. 118. 8-9, 13. For B. Description and C. Epic event see Bhagasya āyatanam.
सुधर्मा: Sudharmā f.: Name of the Sabhā of the Yādavas in Dvārakā. A. Designation: Yādavī 16. 8. 7; Dāśārhī 2. 3. 24. B. Equipment: (1) Furnished with hundreds of royal seats (सिंहासनानि); parts of them were made of gold, they were variegated due to gems and corals set in them, were lustrous like burning fire and were spread with precious covers, (जाम्बूनदाङ्गानि स्पर्ध्यास्तरणवन्ति च । मणिविद्रुमचित्राणि ज्वलीताग्निप्रभाणि च ॥ भेजिरे पुरुषव्याघ्रा … सिंहासनानि शत-शः) 1. 212. 13-14; (2) A war-drum was placed in it; it was adorned with gold and, when struck, it produced loud sound (भेरीं सांनाहिकीं । … महाघोषां जाम्बूनद-परिष्कृताम्) 1. 212. 11. C. Management: The Sabhā was supervised by a Sabhāpāla whose duty was to beat the drum and alert the citizens in the event of an emergency (see the next). D. Purpose: Whenever an emergency arose the Sabhāpāla beat the भेरी to produce loud sound; hearing it, the agitated Bhojas, Vṛṣṇis and Andha-kas would leave aside their food and drink and rush to the Sabhā to know the nature of the emergency 1. 212. 11-12. E. Epic events: (1) When Subhadrā was forcibly abducted by Arjuna, the soldiers accom-panying her rushed to the Sudharmā Sabhā and acquainted the Sabhāpāla with what had happened; when the Vṛṣṇi heroes who gathered in the Sabhā sat down on the royal seats, the Sabhāpāla told them about the abduction of Subhadrā by Arjuna 1. 212. 9-10, 15; (2) After the mutual kill-ings by the Yādavas, when Arjuna reached Dvārakā he entered the Sudharmā to meet the ministers of the Vṛṣṇi heroes; when he occupied a seat in the Sabhā the citizens gathered around him 16. 8. 7-8. F. Compa-rison: Sudharmā was not equal to the unrivalled Sabhā constructed by Maya for the Pāṇḍavas (सभा तु सा महाराज … न दाशार्ही सुधर्मा वा … तादृशी … यां चक्रे ऽप्रतिमां मयः) 2. 3. 19, 24.
सुभाण्ड: Subhāṇḍa nt.: Name of a square (?) Along with the Sudarśana वट, it marked the entrance of the royal residence of the Bāhlīka counry; it was referred to by an old Brāhmaṇa while speaking to Dhṛtarāṣṭṛa deriding the Bāhlīkas (तत्र वृद्धः … द्विजोत्तमः । बाह्लीकदेशं … कुत्सयन् वाक्यम् अब्रवीत् ॥ … सुभाण्डं नाम चत्वरम् । एतद् राजकुलद्वारम् आकुमारं स्मराम्य् अहम् ॥ ) 8. 30. 9, 12 (Nī., who reads सुभद्रं नाम चत्वरं in 8. 44. 8, observes: सुभद्रं चत्वरं सुराभाण्डाश्रयभूलम् । एतद् उभयं राजकुलस्य राजगृहद्वारोपलक्षणम्).
सोमकस्य: *Somakasya āśramaḥ m.: आश्रम of king Somaka. A. Location: On the river Yamunā, in the middle of Kurukṣetra (एषा सा यमु-ना) 3. 125. 22, (कुरुक्षेत्रस्य मध्यतः) 3. 126. 42. B. Description: Holy (पुण्य) 3. 128. 18. C. Holiness: If one who has suppressed his anger lives for six nights at Somaka's आश्रम he will be in a happy con-dition (एष तस्याश्रमः (i. e. of Somaka) पुण्यो य एषो ऽग्रे विराजते । क्षान्त उष्यात्र षड्रात्रं प्राप्नोति सुगतिं नरः) 3. 128. 18. D. Epic event: Lomaśa showed it to Yudhiṣṭhira and suggested to him that they all should stay there for six nights controlling themselves; so he asked Yudhi-ṣṭhira to be ready for it (एतस्मिन्न् अपि राजेद्र वत्स्यामो … । षड्रात्रं नियतात्-मानः सज्जीभव कुरूद्वह ॥ ) 3. 128. 19.
सोमपुरप्रभ: Somapuraprabha nt.: Name of a town (?) Aṣṭaka, son of Viśvāmitra from Mā-dhavī, went to the town Somapuraprabha (or to the town shining like Somapura ?) (अथाष्टकः पुरं प्रायात् तदा सोमपुर-प्रभम्) 5. 117. 19.
सोमाश्रम: Somāśrama m.: An आश्रम of Soma. Situated between Urvaśītīrtha and Kumbhakarṇāśrama; one who bathes there is honoured on this earth (स्नात्वा पूज्यते भुवि मानवः) 3. 82. 136.
सौभ: Saubha1 nt.: Name of the city of Śālva, the demon. A. Location: Located in the sky (खस्थ) 5. 47. 73; 7. 10. 14; (खे विषक्-तं हि तत् सौभम्) 3. 21. 25; (वैहायसं  … पुरम्) 3. 16. 3; (दिवम् आस्थितः … सौभेन) 3. 15. 15; 3. 20. 27; (वियद् अभ्या-गमत् पुनः) 3. 22. 1, 3; (सौभस्थं पृथिवीगतम्) 3. 17. 28; (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 3. 12. 32: सौभं खेचरं पुरम्: on 3. 16. 15: सौभेन खेचरेण पुरेण). B. Its ruler and subjects: It was Śālva's town, ruled over by him and protected by him (शाल्वस्य नगरं सौभम्) 3. 15. 2; (शाल्वगुप्त) 7. 10. 14; hence Śālva was called Saubha-pati 3. 13. 29; 3. 17. 1, 31; 3. 18. 19; 3. 21. 31; 3. 23. 20; Saubharāj 3. 15. 11; 3. 17. 32; 3. 18. 15; 3. 20. 12, 14, 16; Saubhā-dhipati 3. 180. 33; Daiteyas and Dānavas were its inhabitants, hence called Daityapura 7. 10. 14; (दैतेयान् … सौभनिवासिनः) 3. 18. 4; (युद्धं … दानवैः सह) 3. 15. 21; (दानवानां) 3. 21. 27; (सौभात् … विबुध-द्विषाम्) 3. 23. 1. C. Description: Moving at will (कामग) 3. 15. 6, 15; (कामगम) 3. 23. 9; difficult to be attacked (दुरासद) 7. 10. 14; having the form of a peak of Meru mountain (मेरुशिखराकार) 3. 23. 39; it lost its lustre (when struck by the चक्र of Kṛṣṇa) and its watch-towers and gateways were shattered (व्यपगतत्विष्) 3. 23. 33 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 3. 14. 6 explains सौभ as: सौभं सुष्ठु भान्ति ते सुभाः काञ्चनादयो धातवस् तज्जम्); (विध्वस्ता-ट्टालगोपुर) 3. 23. 39; called पुर 3. 16. 3; 3. 21. 18; 7. 10. 14; नगर 3. 15. 2; 3. 21. 9; 3. 23. 33. D. Epic events: Kṛṣṇa told Yudhi-ṣṭhira that at the time of the game of dice he had gone to Saubha, the town of Śālva, to kill him (शाल्वस्य नगरं सौभं गतो ऽहम्) 3. 15. 2; in the absence of Kṛṣṇa, Śālva, enraged at the killing of Śiśupāla, rode his Saubha, moving at will, and attacked Dvārakā (आगतः कामगं सौभम् आरु-ह्य) 3. 15. 5-7; when Śālva did not find Kṛṣṇa in Dvārakā, he reviled Kṛṣṇa, rode his Saubha, and flew up in the sky (दिवम् आस्थितः । कामगेन च सौभेन क्षिप्त्वा माम्) 3. 15. 15; therefore Kṛṣṇa, when he returned to Dvārakā from Indraprastha, left for the destruction of Saubha (ततः सौ-भवधायाहं प्रतस्थे) 3. 15. 19; Yudhi-ṣṭhira then requested Kṛṣṇa to tell him the downfall of Saubha in detail (विस्तरेण … सौभस्य वधम् आचक्ष्व) 3. 16. 1; when Śālva reached Dvārakā, he besieged it on all sides, arranging his sky-moving town (all around) in battle positions (अरुन्धत् तां (द्वारवतीं पुरीम्) … सर्वतः … । शाल्वो वैहायसं चापि तत्पुरं व्यूह्य विष्ठि-तः ॥ ) 3. 16. 3 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 3. 15. 3: व्यूह्य स्वरक्षापरोपमर्दयोग्यरचना-विशेषेण स्थापयित्वा); Dvārakā was well protected when Śālva attacked it (तदा सौभसमागमे) 3. 16. 19; when Śālva's heroes were killed in battle, he (went back; but) came again in his Saubha, moving at will, to attack Dvārakā (काम-गेन स सौभेन शाल्वः पुनर् उपागमत्) 3. 17. 27; the army in Dvārakā was dis-tressed seeing Śālva descending from sky on the earth (दृष्ट्वा शाल्वं … सौभस्थं पृथिवीगतम्) 3. 17. 28; Pradyumna assu-red his army that he would defeat in battle the Saubha with its king (Śālva) (न भीः कार्या । सौभराड् अद्य नश्यति॑ … ससौ-भो विनशिष्यति) 3. 17. 30-32; Pradyumna confounded all demons of the Saubha with quickly shifting the bow from palm to palm (स … चापं विहरन् वै तलात् तलम् । मोहयाम् आस दैतेयान् सर्वान् सौ-भनिवासिनः) 3. 18. 4; when defeated by Pradyumna, Śālva abandoned Dvārakā, rode his Saubha and flew up in the sky (सौभम् आस्थाय … दिवम् आचक्रमे) 3. 20. 27; when Kṛṣṇa, on his return to Dvā-rakā, learnt about the attack on Dvārakā by Śālva, he vowed to destroy the town Saubha along with Śālva (सशाल्वं सौभ-नगरं हन्ता) 3. 21. 9; when he learnt that Sālva, in his Saubha, had gone back, he pursued him (प्रयातं सौभम् आस्थाय) 3. 21. 15; Kṛṣṇa left for the destruction of Saubha after asking Sātyaki and others to protect Dvārakā (तेषु रक्षां समाधाय प्रयातः सौभपातने) 3. 22. 17; Śālva then in his Saubha, had taken refuge in the bay of the ocean and remained hidden in its navel (ततः सागरम् आसाद्य कुक्षौ तस्य महोर्मिणः । समुद्रनाभ्यां शाल्वो ऽभूत् सौभम् आस्थाय) 3. 21. 16 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 3. 20. 17: नाभ्यां गर्भे गुप्त इत्य् अर्थः); Kṛṣṇa's arrows could not reach the town (Saubha) (पुरं नासाद्यत शरैः) 3. 21. 18; the Saubha though close to the sky appeared as if it was at a dis-tance of only a क्रोश from Kṛṣṇa (खे विषक्तं हि तत् सौभं क्रोशमात्र इवा-भवत्) 3. 21. 25; when Kṛṣṇa's arrows pierced the bodies of the Dānavas, there was a loud din in the Saubha (ततो हल-हलाशब्दः सौभमध्ये व्यवर्धत) 3. 21. 28; Kṛṣṇa saw Vasudeva falling down from Saubha: but after some time, Saubha, Śālva and Vasudeva disappeared; all this was माया of Śālva (अपश्यं … प्रपतन्-तम् अहं तदा । सौभाच् छूरसुतं) 3. 22. 22; न तत्र सौभं न रिपुं न शाल्वम् पश्यामि वृद्धं पितरं न चापि ॥ ततो ममासीन् मनसि मायेयम्) 3. 22. 29-30; Kṛṣṇa then felled down the heads of the demons from the Saubha (सौभाच् छिरांसि विबुधद्विषाम्) 3. 23. 1; the Saubha then disappeared due to माया of Śālva (ततो नादृश्यत तदा सौभं … । अन्तर्हितं माययाभूत्) 3. 23. 3; Saubha, moving at will, went to Prāgjyotiṣa and, (on its return), was seen again (ततः प्राग्ज्योति-षं गत्वा पुनर् एव व्यदृश्यत । सौभं कामगमम्) 3. 23. 9 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 3. 22. 9: प्राग्ज्योतिषं पूर्वसमुद्रतीरस्थं नगरविशेषं); Kṛṣṇa's charioteer drew his attention to Śālva, the ruler of Saubha (पश्य  … शाल्वं सौभपतिं स्थितम्) 3. 23. 20; Kṛṣṇa then decided to kill Śālva and bring down Saubha (युद्धे मतिम् अधारयम् । वधाय शाल्वराजस्य सौभस्य च निपात-ने ॥ ) 3. 23. 27; he then employed the आग्नेय अस्त्र on his चक्र and commanded “kill Saubha and my enemies” (आग्नेयम् अस्त्रम्  … चक्रम् … अभिमन्त्र्य … जहि सौभं स्ववीर्येण ये चात्र रिपवो मम । इत्य् उक्त्वा … तस्मै प्राहिणवम्) 3. 23. 28. 31; the चक्र struck the town Saubha and cut it into two in the middle; when the Saubha fell down the चक्र came back to Kṛṣṇa's hand (तत् समासाद्य नगरं सौभम् … मध्येन पाटयाम् आस … । द्विधा कृतं ततः सौभम् … तस्मिन् निपतिते सौभे चक्रम् आगात् करं मम) 3. 23. 33-35; see-ing the Saubha on fire, the women (of the Dānavas) fled 3. 23. 39; Kṛṣṇa steadied his chariot near the Saubha and blew his conch (ततो ऽहं समवस्थाप्य रथं सौभ-समीपतः शङ्खं प्रध्माप्य) 3. 23. 38; after killing Śālva and bringing down the Saubha, Kṛṣṇa returned to the Ānarta country (एवं निहत्य समरे शाल्वं सौ-भं निपात्य च । आनर्तान् पुनर् आगम्य) 3. 23. 40; the downfall of Saubha and the killing of Śālva by Kṛṣṇa is referred to at various places: (1) By Arjuna when he recounted the exploits of Kṛṣṇa (त्वया सौभं च पातितम्) 3. 13. 29; (2) By Arjuna again in his message to Dhṛtarāṣṭra through Saṃjaya (अयं सौभं योधयाम् आस खस्थं … सौभद्वारि प्रत्यगृह्णाच् छतघ्नीम्) 5. 47. 73 (reference to 3. 22. 2-3 where attack on Kṛṣṇa with शतघ्नीस् and other missiles is mentioned ?); (3) By Kṛṣṇa when he suggested to Yudhiṣṭhira to send Suyodhana and his allies the way Śālva and Saubha had gone (प्रस्थाप्य-तां पाण्डव धार्तराष्ट्रः सुयोधनः … सौभस्य सौभाधिपतेश् च मार्गम् ॥ ) 3. 180. 33; (4) By Vidura when he remind-ed Duryodhana that a monkey-chief, Dvi-vida by name, covered Kṛṣṇa with rocks at the gate of Saubha in order to arrest him but he did not succeed (सौभद्वारे वानरे-न्द्रो द्विविदो नाम नामतः । शिलावर्षेण महता छादयाम् आस केशवम् ॥ ग्रहीतु-कमो … ग्रहीतुं नाशकत् तत्र) 5. 128. 41-42 (reference to 3. 23. 10-19 where the showering of rocks is attributed to a Dānava who had assumed the form of a monkey दानवो वानराकृतिः); (5) By Dhṛtarāṣṭra when he recounted Kṛṣṇa's wonderful exploits (दिव्यानि कर्माणि 7. 10. 1); he re-ferred to his bringing down Saubha which had taken refuge in the bay of the ocean (सौभं … समुद्रकुक्षौ विक्रम्य पात-याम् आस माधवः) 7. 10. 14 (reference to 3. 21. 16-38); (6) By Bhagavān when he told Nārada that at the conjunction of Dvāpara and Kali he would destroy all those residing in the Saubha (सर्वान् सौ-भनिवासिनः) 12. 326. 87. E. Simile: The falling down of the Saubha, when struck by Sudarśana, compared with the falling down of Tripura tossed up by the arrow of Maheśvara (सौभं सुदऽशनबलाद् धतम् । महेश्वरशरोद्धूतं पपात त्रिपुरं यथा) 3. 23. 34.

Saubha2 nt.: Name of the city of king Śālva. A. Its king: Śālva is referred to as Saubhapati 1. 96. 48; 5. 175. 24; 5. 176. 2; as Saubharāj 5. 176. 36; sometimes the name of the king is identified with the name of the city and hence the king of the city Saubha is referred to as Śālvapati instead of Saubhapati in 5. 171. 6; 5. 172. 2, 10, 14, 18; 5. 174. 3; 5. 175. 22 (मया शाल्वपतिर् वीर मनसाभिवृतः पतिः where पति is repeated; cf. with this 1. 96. 48 where सौभपतिः occurs and not शाल्व-पतिः); 5. 176. 34. B. Epic event: When Śālva was defeated by Bhīṣma, he returned to his town (Saubha) (ततः शाल्वः स्वनगरं प्रययौ) 1. 96. 39; Ambā told Bhīṣma that she had already chosen the king of Saubha as her husband (मया सौभपतिः पूर्वं मनसाभिवृतः पतिः) 1. 96. 48; permitted by Bhīṣma, she went to the town Saubha (गता सौभ-पुरं प्रति) 5. 178. 10; Ambā returned to Śālva, the ruler of Saubha, and told him that she was allowed by Bhīṣma to go to him (शाल्वं सौभपतिं ततः । कन्ये-यं … वचनम् अब्रवीत् ॥ विसर्जितास्मि भीष्मेण) 5. 175. 24-25; Ambā approached the king of Saubha, but he did not accept her (सौभराजम् उपेत्याहम् अब्रुवं दुर्-वचं वचः । न च मां प्रत्यगृह्णात् सः) 5. 176. 36; when rejected by Śālva, Ambā went out of the town (Saubha) and took resort in the आश्रम of the ascetics outside the town (निश्चक्राम पुराद् दीना) 5. 172. 23; 5. 173. 1; (जगाम नगराद् बहिः । आश्रमं … तापसानाम्) 5. 173. 9; Akṛta-vraṇa, the follower of Rāma, told Ambā that if she desired Rāma to enjoin the ruler of Saubha (to accept her), he (Rāma) would do so (यदि सौभपतिर् भद्रे नियो-क्तव्यो मते तव । नियोक्ष्यति … तं रामः) 5. 176. 2 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 5. 177. 2: नियो-क्तव्यस् तव पाणिग्रहणार्थम् इति शेषः).
स्थूलकेशाश्रम: Sthūlakeśāśrama m.: Name of an आश्रम। The आश्रम of the great sage Sthūla-keśa (ऋषिरासीन् महान् … स्थूलकेश इति ख्यातः ॥ ) 1. 8. 4; Menakā abandoned her child, a daughter, begotten on her by the Gandharva king Viśvāvasu, on the bank of a river near the आश्रम of Sthūlakeśa (मेनका … तं गर्भं … । उत्ससर्ज यथाकालं स्थूलकेशाश्रमं प्रति ॥ उत्सृ-ज्य चैव तं गर्भं नद्यास् तीरे जगाम ह) 1. 8. 6-7; Sthūlakeśa saw the new-born child alone on the bank of the river; he brought her to his आश्रम and reared her (तां ददर्श समुत्सृष्टां नदीतीरे महान् ऋषिः । … स तां दृष्ट्वा तदा कन्यां स्थूल-केशो … । जग्राहाथ मुनिश्रेष्ठः … पुपोष च । ववृधे सा … आश्रमपदे) 1. 8. 8-9; she was named Pramadvarā; Ruru, son of Pramati, saw her in the आश्रम and fell in love with her; when Ruru asked for her through his friends, Sthūlakeśa gave his daughter to him (ताम् आश्रमपदे तस्य रुरुर् दृष्ट्वा प्रमद्वराम् । बभूव … मदनानुगतात्मवान् ॥ ) 1. 8. 11-13.
स्थूलशिरास: Sthūlaśirāsa āśramaḥ m.: The आश्रम of Sthūlaśiras. Described as delightful (रमणीय); Yudhiṣṭhira was advised by Lomaśa to give up pride and anger while in that आश्रम (आश्रमः स्थूलशिरसो रमणीयः प्रकाश-ते । अत्र मानं च कौन्तेय क्रोधं चैव विवर्जय ॥ ) 3. 135. 8.
संशप्तक: Saṃśaptaka m. (pl.): A general term to designate the group of five Trigarta brothers and their followers who together took the oath to kill Arjuna; their army in general, which included besides Trigartas also Mālavas and many other Janapadas, is also referred to as Saṃśaptaka; some-times Nārāyaṇas and Gopālas also figure in the context of Saṃśaptakas. A. Description: Heroic (वीर) 3. 240. 33; 7. 17. 30; 8. 12. 4; 8. 14. 18; brave (शूर) 8. 14. 5; 8. 40. 94; 8. 42. 3; tigers among men (नरव्याघ्र) 7. 17. 2; skilled in the use of missiles (कृतास्त्र) 6. 20. 15; fond of battles (युद्धशौन्ड) 8. 31. 14; great chariot-fighters (माहारथ) 1. 1. 131; 7. 26. 10, 18; famous, widely known (प्रख्यात) 3. 240. 22; (नामलब्धानाम् विदितानां समन्ततः) 8. 40. 94. B. Epic events: (1) Saṃśaptakas took away Arjuna from the main battle-field; after Abhimanyu's death, Arjuna killed all the surviving Saṃśaptakas—these two chief points of the epic events mentioned while listing the contents of the Droṇaparvan in the Parvasaṃgrahaparvan 1. 2. 160, 163; (2) Dānavas informed Duryodhana who was taken to Rāsātala by a कृत्या that the Saṃśaptakas were Daityas and Rākṣasas in hundreds and thousands appointed to kill Arjuna and they would kill him; then Dur-yodhana felt assured that (Karṇa and) the Saṃśaptakas were meant to kill Arjuna and that they were capable of accomplishing the task; the mind of the Saṃśaptakas was under the spell of Rākṣasas and, overcome by the qualities रजस् and तमस्, they were eager to kill Arjuna (सांशप्तकाश् च ते वीरा राक्षसाविष्टचेतसः । रजस्तमोभ्यां आक्रान्ताः फल्गुनस्य वधैषिणः ॥ ) 3. 240. 22, 30, 33; (3) Saṃjaya told Dhṛta-rāṣṭra that in the ensuing war the five Kekaya brothers would take on the two chief Trigartas of the Saṃśaptakas (त्रिगर्-तानां च द्वौ मुख्यौ यौ तौ शंश-प्तकाव् इति) 5. 56. 18; (4) An अयुत of Saṃśaptaka chariot-fighters were meant to fight with Arjuna resulting either in the death or victory of Arjuna; they followed Arjuna wherever he went (संशप्तकानाम् अयुतं रथानां मृत्युर् जयो वार्जुनस्येति सृष्टाः । येनार्जुनस् तेन … प्रयाता वै ते) 6. 20. 15 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 6. 20. 15; येन यत्र तेन तत्र); (5) Śuśarman, king of Trigartas, and his five brothers Satyaratha, Satyadharman, Satyavarman, Satyeṣuḥ and Satyakarman together with their army of Trigartas, as well as Mālavas, Tuṇḍikeras, Mācellakas, Lalitthas, Madrakas and many other Janapadas took the oath (शपथ) to kill Arjuna 7. 16. 11, 15-21; the mode of oath, also called प्रतिज्ञा, in which offerings were given in fire, described 7. 16. 22-37; in the description of the war, in the con-text of Saṃśaptakas, besides some of those groups of people mentioned above, also occur Nārāyaṇas, Gopālas (7. 17. 31; 7. 18. 7), and Yaudheyas (7. 18. 16); (6) On the twelfth day of the war, Droṇa planned a battle between Arjuna and the Saṃśaptaka troops and when Arjuna left the main battle-field to fight with them, he arranged his army in the Suparṇavyūha against Pāṇḍavas (विधाय योगं पार्थेन संशप्तक-गणैः सह) 7. 19. 2-4; the Saṃśaptakas arranged their chariots on even ground in the व्यूह called Candrārdha; they were delighted to see Arjuna approaching them for a fight; they roared loudly; Arjuna was surprised to find that they were delighted when actually they should have been grieved; or, he thought, perhaps, they were delighted because they would go to excellent worlds (after death) which were otherwise difficult to be obtained by bad people 7. 17. 1-6; hearing the sound of Devadatta conch blown by Arjuna, the army of Saṃśaptakas became motionless; regaining consciousness they started fighting with Arjuna by showering कङ्कपत्रिन् arrows against him 7. 17. 9-11; the battle des-cribed in which Subāhu, Sudharman and Sudhanvan also participated 7. 17. 12-22; at the death of Sudhanvan, his followers, afraid, ran towards the army of Duryo-dhana 7. 17. 23; Suśarman, king of Tri-gartas, rebuked those who fled; he remind-ed them of their terrific oaths (शप्त्वा तु शपथान् घोरान्); the troops of Saṃśap-takas then blew their conches and returned to fight till death (मृत्युं कृत्वा निवर्त-नम् ॥ ) 7. 17. 27-31; seeing that the troops of Saṃśaptakas were returning Arjuna asked Kṛṣṇa to drive his chariot towards them; he was determined to kill them 7. 18. 1-3; the Vāyavyāstra released by Arjuna to ward off the arrows of the opponents also blew away a large number of Saṃśaptakas along with their chariots, horses, elephants and weapons; Arjuna killed a large number of Saṃśaptakas; their condition as well as the condition of the battle-field described 7. 18. 22-37; Dhṛtarāṣṭra asked Saṃjaya how Arjuna dealt with the army of Saṃśaptakas (संशप्तकबलं प्रति) and how did they encounter him 7. 25. 2; Arjuna left Saṃśaptakas for a while to fight with Bhagadatta who was routing the Pāṇḍava army; fourteen thousand Saṃśaptakas followed him and challenged him; Arjuna hesitated for a while whether to fight with Saṃśaptakas or go to help Yudhiṣṭhira; ultimately he decided to kill Saṃśaptakas (first) (अभवद् भुयसी बुद्धिः संश-प्तकवधे स्थिरा); the great Saṃśaptaka chariot-fighters (संशप्तकमहारथाः) discharged numerous smooth arrows (शत-सहस्राणि शराणां नतपर्वणां) on Arjuna with the result that, covered with the arrows, neither Arjuna, nor Kṛṣṇa, nor his horses, nor chariot, could be seen; when Kṛṣṇa was deluded (मोहम् अनुप्राप्तः … जनार्दनः) Arjuna killed Saṃśaptakas with Vajrāstra 7. 26. 10, 12-14, 18-20; the condition of Saṃśaptakas described 7. 26. 21-27; having killed Saṃśaptakas Arjuna asked Kṛṣṇa to drive his chariot towards Bhagadatta 7. 26. 29; but Suśarman and his Saṃśaptaka brothers followed Arjuna challenging him for a fight (युद्धार्थी पृष्थतो ऽन्वयात् ॥ … सुशर्माह्वयते ऽच्युत ॥ ); Arjuna therefore was again in doubt-whether to kill Saṃśaptakas first or to go to the aid of his side 7. 27. 2-5; he asked Kṛṣṇa to turn back and started fighting with Suśarman; his battle with Saṃśaptaka brothers described in which Suśarman swooned 7. 27. 7-10; later, Arjuna continued to kill the surviving Saṃ-śaptakas and Nārāyaṇas on the southern side of the army (दक्षिणेन तु सेनायाः कुरुते कदनं बलि । संशप्तकावशेषस्य नारायणबलस्य च ॥ ) 7. 30. 29; after killing the Saṃśaptakas, Arjuna returned to attack Droṇa and the Kaurava army 7. 31. 41-44; (7) On the thirteenth day, when Droṇa reiterated the necessity of removing Arjuna from the main battle, Saṃśapta-kas renewed their challenge to Arjuna and took him away to the south of the battle-field (आह्वयन्न् अर्जुनं संख्ये दक्षिणाम् अभितो दिशम्) 7. 32. 15; towards the end of the day, Arjuna proceeded towards his camp after killing Saṃśaptakas 7. 50. 1-3; Yudhiṣṭhira, grieved over the death of Abhimanyu, told Arjuna that after he left to fight with the Saṃśaptaka army, Droṇa made a serious attempt to capture him 7. 51. 1; (8) On the fourteenth day, at the instance of Duryodhana, the army of Kauravas, along with Saṃśaptakas, returned to fight with Sātyaki with great determination (ते पुनः संन्यवर्तन्त कृत्वा संशप्तकान् मिथः) 7. 97. 12; when Duḥśāsana was wounded by Sātyaki, Duryodhana asked Trigartas to fight with Sātyaki; Saṃśaptakas again made a deter-mined effort to attack Sātyaki; Sātyaki killed their five hundred chief warriors, showering arrows on them, at the head of the army (अग्रानीके व्यपोथयत्) 7. 99. 3-7; their condition described 7. 99. 8-11; ultimately they retreated in the direction of Droṇa 7. 99. 12; (9) When Dhṛtarāṣṭra was told that on the sixteenth day, angry Arjuna attacked the Saṃśaptaka troops (संशप्तकगणान् 8. 9. 8) he wished to know the details of the fight between Saṃ-śaptakas and Arjuna; Arjuna entered the large ocean-like troops of Saṃśaptakas (संशप्तकगणं … अर्णवसंनिभम्) and agitated it (व्यक्षोभयत्); the fight in which Arjuna cut off the hands and heads of his opponents with sharp arrows and killed elephants and horses along with their riders as well as chariot-fighters was hair-raising (लोमहर्षणम्) 8. 12. 1, 3-13; at that point Aśvatthāman challenged Arjuna; hence he asked Kṛṣṇa whether he should continue killing Saṃśaptakas or accept the challenge of Aśvatthāman: Kṛṣṇa drove him to Aśvatthāman 8. 12. 21-22; after fighting with Aśvatthāman, Arjuna return-ed to Saṃśaptaka horse-riders, chariot-fighters, elephant-riders and foot-soldiers (ततः संशप्तकान् भूयः साश्वसूतरथ-द्विपान् । ध्वजपत्तिगणान्) 8. 12. 36; battle described in which Arjuna killed all kinds of his opponents (संशप्तकमहार्णवम् । व्यशोषयत दुःशोषम् … ) and returned to fight with Aśvatthāman 8. 12. 37-43, 47; after fighting for a while with him, Arjuna came back to Saṃśaptakas; he cut off the hands, heads, weapons etc. of the opponents who did not turn back (अपराङ्मुखानाम्) 8. 12. 54-58; after Arjuna's one more encounter with Aśvatthāman in which the latter was removed from the battle by his horses, Arjuna continued his battle with Saṃśaptakas 8. 12. 70-71; when there was loud noise to the north of the battle-field (8. 13. 1), Kṛṣṇa advised Arjuna to go there and first fight with Māgadha Daṇḍa-dhāra; he could later kill the Saṃśaptakas 8. 13. 4; accordingly, Arjuna first killed Daṇḍadhāra and his elephant and came back to Saṃśaptakas 8. 13. 25; in the battle that followed, Arjuna killed many Saṃśaptakas, while Kṛṣṇa drove his chariot in various roundabout ways (वक्रानुव-क्रगमनात्) 8. 14. 1; the battle described 8. 14. 2-21; at that moment Kṛṣṇa advised Arjuna not to while away his time with Saṃśaptakas; he should kill them without loss of time and hasten to kill Karṇa (किं क्रीडसे ऽनघ । संशप्तकान् प्रम-थ्यैतांस् ततः कर्णवधे त्वर); Arjuna agreed and killed quickly the remaining Saṃśaptakas (क्षिप्रं शिष्टान् संशप्त-कांस् तदा । आक्षिप्य शस्त्रेण बलाद् … अवधीत्) 8. 14. 22-23; Trigartas, along with Śālvas, Saṃśaptakas, and Nārāyaṇas, led by the king of Trigartas and his brothers, attacked Arjuna 8. 19. 2-4; the battle, in which Saṃśaptakas were killed by hundreds and thousands (शतशो ऽथ सहस्रशः 8. 19. 19) and at one stage they surrounded Arjuna and showered him with weapons, described 8. 19. 5-34; in the end almost the entire Saṃśaptaka army turned back and did not stay to face Arjuna (प्रायशो विमुखं सर्वं नावतिष्ठत संयुगे); Arjuna thus won victory over many Saṃ-śaptaka troops (संशप्तकगणान् बहून्) 8. 19. 34-35; (10) On the seventeenth day, thirty-four thousand chariot-fighters of Śaṃśaptakas determined to fight to the end stood on the left side of the Bārhaspatya-vyūha of Kauravas (चतुस्त्रिंशत्सहस्राणि रथानाम् अनिवर्तिनाम् । संशप्तका … वामं पार्श्वम् अपालयन् … बार्हस्पत्यः  … महाव्यूहः) 8. 31. 14, 26; Śalya drew attention of Karṇa to Saṃśaptakas who had challenged Arjuna; in response, they were being attacked and killed by Arjuna; angered Saṃśaptakas covered him on all sides making Arjuna invisible (संशप्तकैः क्रुद्धैः … छन्नः पार्थो न दृश्यते) 8. 31. 56-57; Dhṛtarāṣṭra asked Saṃjaya to describe to him the battle between Arjuna and Saṃśaptakas; Saṃjaya told him that when the armies were arrayed (अथ व्यूढेष्व् अनीकेषु), Arjuna attacked Saṃśaptakas; wishing to kill Arjuna and determined to win victory not minding death (विजये कृत-संकल्पा मृत्युं कृत्वा निवर्तनम्) they rushed towards Arjuna; their army consi-sted of many horses, elephants, chariot-fighters and foot-soldiers; a fierce battle then took place; Arjuna cut off their hands, holding different weapons, as well as their heads; thinking Arjuna's chariot was drowned in the large army, Saṃśaptakas delightfully raised a roar (तस्मिन् सैन्ये महावर्ते … । निमग्नं तं रथं मत्वा नेदुः संशप्तका मुदा । ) 8. 32. 1-13; at the site where Arjuna was killing Saṃśapta-kas a loud sound of Gāṇḍīva was heard; very much angered Saṃśaptakas, coveting victory (जयगृद्धाः प्रमन्यवः) sho-wered arrows on Arjuna; Arjuna braved their attack and reached Suśarman; when Arjuna started showering arrows on Suśar-man, Saṃśaptakas responded the same way; hearing the roar of the monkey on Arjuna's chariot, the army of Saṃśaptakas was much terrified and became motionless; regain-ing consciousness, the warriors showered arrows on Arjuna and covered his chariot; they held firmly the horses, the wheels and the shaft of Arjuna's chariot and roared loudly (ते हयान् रथचक्रे च रथेषाश् चापि भारत । निगृह्य बलवत्); some mounted on Arjuna's chariot and held him and Kṛṣṇa; shaking his hands Kṛṣṇa felled them down; Arjuna saw Saṃśaptaka great chariot-fighters encircling him and holding his chariot and Kṛṣṇa; he felled many of them down who had mounted the chariot and other foot-soldiers who were close to him by shooting arrows which went short distances (अपातयत् । आसन्नांश् च ततो योधाञ् शरैर् आसन्नयोधिभिः); he made the rest run away; Arjuna pointed out to Kṛṣṇa that he had killed thousands of Saṃśaptakas who had achieved the difficult task of checking his chariot (कुर्वाणान् दारुणं कर्म … रथबन्धं इमं । घोरं); Arjuna and Kṛṣṇa blew Deva-datta and Pāñcajanya conches respy.; hearing that sound, the Saṃśaptaka army shook and became very much afraid (सं-चचाल … वित्रस्ता चाभवद् भृशम्); Arjuna then bound their feet by releasing नागास्त्र; he killed them in that condition; when they were being killed, they gave up fighting with Arjuna and threw down their weapons; then Suśarman released them from their bonds by using सौपर्णास्त्र; once free, they showered arrows and weapons on Arjuna (ससृजुर् बाणसं-घांश् च शस्त्रसंघांश् च); Arjuna cut off the missiles with arrows and killed many elephants, horses and chariot-fighters by using ऐन्द्रास्त्र; the troops of Saṃśaptakas and Nārāyaṇas were then very much afraid; no one was able to fight back Arjuna (न हि कश्चित् पुमांस् तत्र यो ऽर्जुनं प्रत्य-विध्यत); Arjuna then killed an अयुत of the opposing warriors; fourteen thousand (foot) warriors, an अयुत of chariot-fighters, and three thousand elephant-riders of Saṃśaptakas who survived (यानि शिष्टानि) once again surrounded Arjuna determined either to return with victory or die (मर्तवयम् इति निश्चित्य जयं वापि निवर्तनम्); a fierce fighting then was fought between them and Arjuna (8. 37. 1-38); Arjuna destroyed many Saṃśapta-kas; their Kṣatriyas, tormented by him, were killed (ते क्षत्रिया दह्यमानास् … जग्मुर् विनाशम्) 8. 40. 5-61 after killing many Saṃśaptaka troops (निहत्य … सं-शप्तकगणान् बहून्), Arjuna pointed out to Kṛṣṇa the great Saṃśaptaka chariot-fighters who along with their troops ran away as they were unable to resist his arrows (धावन्ति सगणाः संशप्तकमहा-रथाः । अपारयन्तो मद्बाणान्) 8. 40. 78-80; Duryodhana again incited Saṃśaptakas to face Arjuna; then a thousand chariot-fighters, three hundred elephant-riders, fourteen thousand horse-riders and two hundred thousand archers turned towards Kṛṣṇa and Arjuna covering them with arrows; but Arjuna killed ten thousand Saṃśaptakas 8. 40. 92-99; thus Arjuna completely destroyed (कृत्स्नेन व्यध-मत्) the Saṃśaptakas 8. 40. 130; when the armies of Kurus and Sṛñjayas met again only a few Saṃśaptakas had sur-vived (संशप्तकेषु … किंचिच्छिष्टेषु); Arjuna, after defeating Aśvatthāman (8. 42. 51), asked Kṛṣṇa to take him to Saṃ-śaptakas since fighting with them was his main task (कार्यम् एतत् परं मम) 8. 42. 3, 56; Arjuna killed the remaining Saṃ-śaptaka troops with sharp arrows with the result that they became the guests of Indra and became free from grief as they were happy (शक्रस्यातिथिताम् गत्वा विशोका ह्य् अभवन् मुदा) 8. 43. 76-77; when Arjuna told Bhīma that he could not leave the battlefield (to go to enquire about Yudhi-ṣṭhira) without killing Saṃśaptakas who faced him, Bhīma assured him that he himself would fight with the Saṃśaptakas 8. 45. 63-64; Arjuna while explaining to Yudhiṣṭhira why he had not yet killed Karṇa told him that during his fight with Saṃśaptakas, Aśvatthāman had unexpec-tedly intervened (to distract him) 8. 47. 2; later, while boasting about his heroic deeds Arjuna mentioned that he had killed almost all Saṃśaptakas and only a few of them had survived (संशप्तकानां किंचिद् एवावशिष्टम्) 8. 49. 96; at one stage, Duḥśā-sana along with the fully equipped army of Saṃśaptakas (पृतना समृद्धा) attacked Bhīma 8. 53. 9; when Arjuna was proceeding towards Karṇa, Saṃśaptaka chariot-fighters attacked him showering arrows; Arjuna killed many of them along with their chari-oteers, and cut off their bows and banners with sharp arrows; they all fell down from their chariots 8. 59. 3-5; (11) On the seventeenth day, at night, when Saṃjaya reported to Dhṛtarāṣṭra the death of Karṇa (8. 1. 25), he (Dhṛtarāṣṭra), while recalling some of the major events of war, mention-ed the killing of the Saṃśaptaka army by Arjuna 8. 1. 41; in reply to Dhṛtarāṣṭra's question who of the Kurus were still alive and who dead (के नु जीवन्ति के मृताः) 8. 4. 3, Saṃjaya mentioned Saṃśaptaka troops (संशप्तकगणाश् च ये) among those who were killed by Arjuna 8. 4. 38; (12) On the eighteenth day, Arjuna speedily rushed towards Kṛtavarman and Saṃśaptaka troops which were posted on the left side of the Sarvatobhadravyūha of Kauravas 9. 7. 30, 19, 24 (where Saṃ-śaptakas are designated as Trigartas); Arjuna, having killed Saṃśaptakas in battle (हत्वा संशप्तकान् रणे) rushed towards, the army of Kauravas 9. 9. 59; as the day advanced (मध्यंदिनगते सूर्ये), Aśvatthāman, helped by Saṃśaptakas (संशप्तकवृतो रणे), fought with Arjuna; the battle was terrific in which a large number of warriors were killed (तत्र युद्धं महच् चासीत् … यमराष्ट्रविवर्-धनम्) 9. 13. 42-43; (विमर्दस् तु महान् आसीत्) 9. 13. 45; (13) On the nineteenth day, after the war was over, Saṃjaya, having returned early in the morning from the camp (ततः पूर्वाह्णसमये शिबिराद् एत्य संजयः 9. 1. 14), while reporting to Dhṛtarāṣṭra the war-events mentioned Saṃśaptakas among those who were killed in war 9. 1. 26; Dhṛtarāṣṭra lamenting the loss of life in war mentioned that many Saṃśaptakas were killed (संशप्तकाश् च बहवः (निहताः)) 9. 2. 34; (14) Kṛṣṇa, while giving an account of war to Vasu-deva, mentioned that before the fall of Abhimanyu, Saṃśaptakas had challenged Arjuna for a battle and took him away from the main scene (समाहूते तु सं-ग्रामे पार्थे संशप्तकैस् तदा) 14. 60. 19. C. Arjuna is described as the killer of Saṃśaptakas संशप्तकनिषूदन 14. 73. 32, संशप्तकनिहन्तृ 14. 76. 9. [See Trigarta]
संस्थान: Saṃsthāna m. (pl.): Name of a people. On the second day of war, Duryodhana asked Saṃsthāna warriors and others to protect Bhīṣma in the Mahāvyūha of Kauravas (संस्थानाः शूरसेनाश् च … भीष्मम् एवाभिरक्षन्तु … ॥ … अव्यूहन्त महाव्यूहं … ) 6. 47. 7-10.
सन्न्यस्तपाद: Saṃnyastapāda m. (pl.): Name of a people. Saṃnyastapādas were among those who, afraid of Jarāsandha, fied from north to south (तथोत्तरां दिशं चापि परि-त्यज्य भयार्दिताः । … संन्यस्तपादाश् च दक्षिणां दिशम् आश्रिताः ॥ ) 2. 13. 27.
संन्यस्तपाद: Saṃnyastapāda m. (pl.): Name of a people. Saṃnyastapādas were among those who, afraid of Jarāsandha, fied from north to south (तथोत्तरां दिशं चापि परि-त्यज्य भयार्दिताः । … संन्यस्तपादाश् च दक्षिणां दिशम् आश्रिताः ॥ ) 2. 13. 27.
सकच: Sakaca m. (pl.): Name of a Janapada. Listed by Saṃjaya among the northern Janapadas (also called Deśas 6. 10. 68) of Bhāratavarṣa (अत ऊर्ध्वं जनपदान् निबोध) 6. 10. 37, 5; (दर्वीकाः सकचा दर्वा … ) 6. 10. 53.
सकलद्वीप: Sakaladvīpa m., n. (sg.): Name of a country ? Arjuna in his expedition to the north (दिशं धनपतेर् इष्टाम् 2. 23. 9) before the Rājasūya conquered the Sakaladvīpa, its king Prativindhya, and its people (विजिग्ये सकलं द्वीपं प्रतिविन्ध्यं च पार्थिवम् ॥ सकलद्वीपवासाम्श् च) 2. 23. 15-16.
सक्षद्द्रुह्: Sakṣaddruh m. (pl.): Name of a Janapada. Listed by Saṃjaya among the southern Janapadas (also called Deśas 6. 10. 68) of Bhāratavarṣa (अथापरे जनपदा दक्षिणा  … ) 6. 10. 56, 5; (सक्षद्द्रुहः कुन्तलाश् च) 6. 10. 64.
सतिय: Satiya m. (sg. ?): Name of a Jana-pada. Listed by Saṃjaya among the southern Janapadas (also called Deśas 6. 10. 68) of Bhāratavarṣa (अथापरे जनपदा दक्षीणा  … ) 6. 10. 56, 5; (सतियः पत्तिपञ्जकाः) 6. 10. 62.
सप्तद्वीप: Saptadvīpa m., nt. (sg.): Name of some country to the north of Khāṇḍava-prastha ? Arjuna in his expedition to the north (दिशं धनपतेर् इष्टाम् 2. 23. 9) before the Rājasūya conquered the kings of the Saptadvīpa (सप्तद्वीपे च ये नृपाः) 2. 23. 16 (this can impossibly refer to the seven Dvīpas of this earth cf. 6. 12. 4; 12. 49. 31).
समक्ष: Samakṣa m. (pl.): Name of a people. Bhīma in his expedition to the east (ययौ प्राचीं दिशं प्रति 2. 26. 1, 7, 2. 23. 9) before the Rājasūya defeated Sama-kṣas in battle (प्राच्यसुह्मान् समक्षांश् चैव … विजित्य युधि) 2. 27. 14.
समङ्ग: Samaṅga m. (pl.): Name of a Jana-pada. Listed by Saṃjaya among the southern Janapadas (also called Deśas 6. 10. 68) of Bhāratavarṣa (अथापरे जनपदा दक्षिणा  … ) 6. 10. 56, 5; (समङ्गाः कोपनाश् चैव) 6. 10. 59.
समन्दर: Samandara m. (pl): Name of a people (referred to only twice and in both cases along with Piśācas). (1) On the fourteenth day of war, Samandaras along with many others, led by Duryodhana, attacked Sātyaki (दुर्योधन-पुरोगमाः … पैशाचाश् च समन्दराः । अभ्यद्रवन्त शैनेयं) 7. 97. 13-14; (2) On the fifteenth day of war, when Saṃjaya at night (शिबिरात् संजयं प्राप्तं निशि नागाह्वयं पुरम् 7. 1. 7) reported to Dhṛtarāṣṭra the death of Droṇa, he (Dhṛtarāṣṭra) while recounting the past exploits of Kṛṣṇa mentioned his victory over Samandaras (पिशाचांस् च समन्दरान्) 7. 10. 16; (or does समन्दर- mean Piśācas along with Mandaras ? see Mandara).
सागरानूपग: Sāgarānūpaga, Sāgarānūpavāsin adj.: Characterization of peoples living along ocean and marshy land. A. Description: Haughty, fond of battles, strong and firm-fisted (संरम्-भिणो युद्धशौण्डा बलिनो दृब्धपाणयः) 8. 51. 19. B. Epic events: (1) Kṛṣṇa mentioned the people who lived near the ocean and the marshy land (as also those who lived in cities) among those whom he saw attending the Rājasūya sacrifice and acting as servers (सागरानूपगांश् चैव ये च पत्तनवासिनः … आगतान् अहम् अद्रा-क्षम् यज्ञे ते परिवेषकान्) 3. 48. 19, 22; (2) On the seventeenth day of war (अद्य सप्तादशाहानि वर्तमानस्य भारत) 8. 51. 2; Kṛṣṇa in order to encourage Arjuna mentioned the warriors who lived along the ocean and marshy lands among those who had joined the side of Kauravas and whom Arjuna alone was capable of defeat-ing (सागरानूपवासिनः … एते सुयोधन-स्यार्थे संरब्धाः कुरुभिः सह । न शक्या युधि निर्जेतुम् त्वदन्येन परं-तप) 8. 51. 19-20.
सात्वत: Sātvata (Sātvat) m. (pl.): Name of a people who formed a section of the Yādavas; Sātvat occurs only in complex forms except in 1. 210. 12). A. Description of their warriors: Sātvatas were invincible in battles; they hit their targets accurately in battles; they fought in various ways; they were con-querors of gods, demons and Gandharvas, but were not proud; they depended for victory on their own valour and were not dependent on others (न हि शक्या रणे जेतुं सात्वता … ॥ लब्धलक्ष्याश् च संग्रामे बहवश् चित्रयोधिनः । देवदानवगन्धर्वान् विजेतारो ह्य् अवि-स्मिताः । स्ववीर्यविजये युक्ता नैते परस् परिग्रहाः ॥ ) 7. 119. 20-21 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 7. 144. 22; परपरिग्रहाः पराधिनाः); Sātvatas are not specifically mentioned in the army of Sātyaki but his army which consisted of warriors from different coun-tries (तस्य योधा … नानादेशसमागताः) must have also some Sātvatas (as Sātvatas, formed a section of the Yādavas, and Sātyaki is often referred to as a Sātvata, see below section C, A. (5)); these war-riors are described as heroic (वीर, महावीर्य) and fighting with different kinds of weapons (नानाप्रहरण) 5. 19. 2; their weapons detailed in 5. 19. 3-4. B. Epic events: (1) Kṛṣṇa while trying to pacify Baladeva and Vṛṣṇis who were angered at the abduction of Subhadrā by Arjuna by telling them that Arjuna did not think of Sātvatas as covetous of wealth (अर्थलुब्धान् न वः पार्थो मन्यते सात्व-तान् सदा) 1. 213. 3; (2) Aśvatthāman was honoured by Kurus, Pāṇḍavas and Sātvatas (उपास्यमानो बहुभिः कुरुपाण्डवसात्व-तत्ः) 7. 61. 14; (3) Sātvatas, along with Sṛñjayas and Pāñcālas, followed Bhīma and Arjuna who led the attack on Droṇa from the southern and northern side (बीभत्सुर् दक्षिणं पार्श्वम् उत्तरं तु वृकोदरः) 7. 132. 41; (4) Nārāyaṇa had told Nārada that he as Kṛṣṇa would bring about the annihilation of all the chiefs of Sātvatas which was tantamount to the destruction of his kinsmen (सर्वसात्वतमुख्यानां द्वारकायाश् च … । करिष्ये प्रलयं घोरम् आत्मज्ञातिविनाशनम्) 12. 326. 92. C. Sevaral persons referred to as belong-ing to Sātvatas; or as their chiefs, or their best; great chariot-fighters and the like: A. Belonging to the Sātvatas: (a) Sātvata: (1) Kṛtavarman 1. 213. 27; 5. 141. 39; 6. 16. 34; 6. 47. 19; 6. 52. 3; 6. 77. 2; 7. 66. 36; 7. 67. 19; 8. 31. 11; 9. 5. 2; 9. 20. 3, 5; 9. 24. 36, 55; 9. 26. 16; 9. 29. 9; 9. 63. 28; 9. 64. 2; 10. 4. 3, 10; 10. 5. 36; 10. 9. 6; (2) Kṛṣṇa 1. 210. 12 (Sātvat); 1. 215. 1; 3. 46. 41; 5. 69. 3; 9. 2. 64; (3) Ceki-tāna 6. 80. 23-24; (4) Balarāma 9. 53. 1; (5) Sātyaki 6. 55. 82-83; 6. 86. 81; 6. 99. 13; 6. 112. 12; 7. 9. 34; 7. 24. 45; 7. 60. 32; 7. 72. 35; 7. 73. 13; 7. 82. 38; 7. 85. 9, 39, 90, 101; 7. 88. 6, 15, 42; 7. 89. 16, 31, 38; 7. 91. 16, 19, 23, 40, 47, 49, 54; 7. 92. 13, 32, 39; 7. 93. 2, 11, 32; 7. 96. 29; 7. 97. 6, 33; 7. 98. 11; 7. 99. 22; 7. 102. 11; 7. 105. 1, 6; 7. 108. 5; 7. 116. 27; 7. 117. 1, 9, 42, 54; 7. 120. 38, 58; 7. 122. 34, 66, 87; 7. 128. 24; 7. 131. 2, 4, 6, 21, 24; 7. 132. 5-6, 12; 7. 133. 31; 7. 137. 5, 20, 24-25, 33; 7. 141. 9-10; 7. 145. 42, 66; 7. 146. 2; 7. 148. 56; 7. 157. 41; 7. 164. 25, 36, 159; 7. 169. 20, 38; 7. 171. 49; 8. 9. 292; 9. 2. 64; 9. 6. 28; 9. 14. 33; 9. 19. 26; 9. 20. 24. (b) Sātvatī (f.): (1) Devakī सात्वती-(पुत्र) 2. 35. 8 (Kṛṣṇa, son of Sātvatī); (2) Not named (her name Śrutaśravā ac-cording to Harivaṃaśa 1. 24. 10): सात्वती-(सुत) 2. 42. 6 (Śiśupāla, son of Sātvatī); (3) Subhadrā: सात्वती 1. 213. 61; 14. 68. 12; 15. 1. 21; 15. 16. 20; 15. 36. 13; सात्वती-पुत्र (Abhimanyu, son of Sātvatī) 6. 69. 30; 7. 38. 20; 7. 51. 8; B. Chief or best among the Sātvatas (or Sātvats): Kṛṣṇa (i) ऋषभः सर्वसात्वतां 5. 70. 1; 5. 92. 5, 30; 5. 128. 7; (see सात्वतर्षभ below); (ii) °सात्वतपुंगव: Sātyaki 7. 117. 41; (iii) पुरोगः सर्वसात्वताम्: Kṛṣṇa 5. 84. 2; (iv) सात्वतप्रवर: (1) Kṛṣṇa 2. 42. 60; 10. 16. 5; (2) Sātyaki (प्रवरः सात्वतानाम्) 7. 115. 23; 7. 117. 52; (v) सात्वतानां महारथः: (1) Kṛtavarman 8. 5. 94; (2) Sātyaki 5. 19. 1; 7. 97. 45; (vi) सात्वतमुख्य: (1) Kṛṣṇa 2. 43. 22; (2) Pradyumna 3. 20. 5; (3) Sātyaki 7. 94. 8; (vii) सात्वतर्षभ: Sātyaki 7. 122. 32; (viii) सात्वतां वरः: (1) Kṛṣṇa 9. 61. 40; (2) Sātyaki 7. 73. 37; (ix) सात्वतानां वरिष्ठः: Kṛtavarman 8. 4. 92; (x) वृषभः सर्वसात्वताम्: Kṛṣṇa 12. 200. 16; (xi) सात्वतश्रेष्ठ: (1) Kṛṣṇa 6. 102. 60; 9. 62. 28; (2) Sātyaki 7. 117. 58; (xii) सात्वताग्र्य: Sātyaki 6. 22. 4; C. (i) Who is ill-willed towards Sātvatas: सात्वतानां नृशंसात्मा: Śiśu-pāla 2. 42. 6; (ii) Worst among Sātvatas: सात्वताधम: Sātyaki 7. 145. 52; D. Daughter of the Sātvatas: सात्वतात्मजा: Subhadrā 1. 213. 15. [See Yadu, Vṛṣṇi]
सामुद्रनिष्कुट: Sāmudraniṣkuṭa m. (pl.): Name of a Janapada. Listed by Saṃjaya among the northern Janapadas (also called Deśas 6. 10. 68) of Bhāratavarṣa (अत ऊर्ध्वं जनपदान् निबोध) 6. 10. 37, 5; (काक्षाः सामुद्र-निष्कुटाः) 6. 10. 47; (these are probably identical with Vairāmas and others who are mentioned as समुद्रनिष्कुटे जाताः 2. 47. 9-10; cf. also सागरकुक्षिस्थान् म्लेच्छान् 2. 29. 15 and other references to Mlecchas living along the ocean and islands p. 840 and Sāgarānūpaga above).
साल्वेयक: Sālveyaka m. (pl.): Name of a people. Suśarman, the king of Trigartas, com-plained to Duryodhana that he was, in the bygone days, often humiliated and forcibly oppressed by Sālveyakas and Matsyas led by Kīcaka (असकृन् निकृतः पूर्वं मत्स्यैः साल्वेयकैः सह । सूतेन चैव मत्स्यस्य कीचकेन पुनः पुनः । बाधितो  … बलात्) 4. 29. 2-3.
सावित्रीपुत्रकाञ्चल: Sāvitrīputrakāñcala m. (pl.): Name of a people. On the seventeenth day of the war, at night (निशि 8. 1. 25), when Saṃjaya reported to Dhṛtarāṣṭra the death of Karṇa, he asked Saṃjaya who were killed in war and who have survived (के नु जीवन्ति के मृताः) 8. 4. 3; Saṃjaya mentioned Sāvitrī-putrakāñcalas among those that were killed 8. 4. 47.
सिंहल: Siṃhala m. (pl.): Name of a people. A. Origin: Nandinī, the cow of Vasiṣṭha, created Siṃhalas from her foam in order to fight with the army of Viśvā-mitra (सिंहलान् … फेनतः सा ससर्ज ह) 1. 165. 36. B. Description: Dark, having eyes with red corners, clad in garments which were set with gems (संवृता मणि-चीरैस् तु श्यामास् ताम्रान्तलोचनाः) 2. 48. 31. C. Epic events: (1) Siṃhalas were among the people who arrived to attend the Rājasūya of Yudhiṣṭhira 2. 31. 12; they brought with them as tribute for Yudhi-ṣṭhira the quintessence of the ocean viz., Vaiḍūrya, pearls, conches and hundreds of elephant-coverings, but they were stopped at the gate (समुद्रसारं वैडूर्यं मुक्ताः शङ्खांस् तथैव च । शतशश् च कुथांस् तत्र सिंहला समुपाहरन्) 2. 48. 30-31 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 2. 52. 35: सनुद्र-सारं मुक्ताफलादि, on 2. 52. 36: कुथान् करिकम्बलान्); Siṃhalas mentioned by Kṛṣṇa among those whose kings, frightened by the lustre of weapons, attended the Rājasūya and were seen by him working as servants (यत्र सर्वान् महीपालान् शस्त्र-तेजोभयार्दितान् । आगतान् अहं अद्राक्षं यज्ञे ते परिवेषकान्) 3. 48. 18-19, 22; (2) On the twelfth day of the war, Siṃhalas were posted by Droṇa at the neck (ग्रीवायाम्) of the Suparṇavyūha (7. 19. 4-5) of Kauravas 7. 19. 7.
सिद्ध: Siddha m. (pl.): Name of a Janapada. Mentioned by Saṃjaya among the northern Janapadas (also called Deśas 6. 10. 68) of Bhāratavarṣa (अत ऊर्ध्वं जनपदान् निबोध) 6. 10. 37, 5; (बर्बराः सिद्धा … ) 6. 10. 55.
सिराल: Sirāla m. (pl.): Name of a Janapada. Listed by Saṃjaya among the southern Janapadas (also called Deśas 6. 10. 68) of Bhāratavarṣa (अथापरे जनपदा दक्षिणा  … ) 6. 10. 56, 5; (आदिदायाः सिरालाश् च) 6. 10. 62.
सुकुटि: Sukuṭi m. (?) (pl.): Name of a Jana-pada. Listed by Saṃjaya among the northern Janapadas (also called Deśas 6. 10. 68) of Bhāratavarṣa (for citation see Sirāla); (मत्स्याः सुकुट्यः) 6. 10. 38.
सुकुट्ट: Sukuṭṭa m. (pl.): Name of a Jana-pada and its people. A. Location: Listed by Saṃjaya among the northern Janapadas (also called Deśas 6. 10. 68) of Bhāratavarṣa (अत ऊर्ध्वं जनपदान् निबोध) 6. 10. 37, 5; (आदिराष्ट्राः सुकुट्टाश् च) 6. 10. 43. B. Epic event: Afraid of Jarāsandha they, along with many others, took resort in the west (जरासन्धभयाद् एव प्रतिचीं दिशम् आश्रिताः ॥ … सुस्थराश् च सुकुट्टाश् च) 2. 13. 24-25.
सुदामन्: Sudāman m. (pl.): Name of a Jana-pada. Listed by Saṃjaya among the northern Janapadas (also called Deśas 6. 10. 68) of Bhāratavarṣa (अत ऊर्ध्वं जनपदान् निबोध) 6. 10. 37, 5; (सुदामानः सुम-ल्लिकाः) 6. 10. 53.
सुदाशार्ण: Sudāśārṇa m. (pl.): Name of a Jana-pada. Listed by Saṃjaya among the northern Janapadas (also called Deśas 6. 10. 68) of Bhāratavarṣa (for citation see Sudāman); (सुदाशार्णाश् च भारत) 6. 10. 41.
सुदेष्ण: Sudeṣṇa m. (pl.): Name of a Jana-pada. Listed by Saṃjaya among the northern Janapadas (also called Deśas 6. 10. 68) of Bhāratavarṣa (for citation see Sudāman); (मल्लाः सुदेष्णाः) 6. 10. 45.
सुदोष्ण: Sudoṣṇa m. (pl.): Name of a Jana-pada. Listed by Saṃjaya among the northern Janapadas (also called Deśas 6. 10. 68) of Bhāratavarṣa (for citation see Sudāman); (सुदोष्णाः प्रमुदास् तथा) 6. 10. 49.
सुनिक: Sunika m. (pl.): Name of a people. Mentioned along with Yavanas, Pāradas and Śakas who knew the माया of Asuras employed by them while fighting; they are described as very fierce and having fierce eyes; they fought with Arjuna and were killed by him by the माया of his missiles (विदन्त्य् असुरमायां ये सुघोरा घोरचक्षुषः । यवनाः पारदाश् चैव शकाश् च सुनिकैः सह ॥ ) 7. 68. 41; (म्लेच्छान् अशातयत् सर्वान् समेतान् अस्त्र-मायया) 7. 68. 44.
सुन्दरवेग: Sundaravega m. (pl.): Name of a people. Their king Bāhu listed by Bhīma among the eighteen well-known kings who extirpated their kinsmen and friends along with their relatives (अष्टादशेमे राजानः प्रख्याता … । ये समुच्चिच्छिदुर् ज्ञातीन् सुहृदश् च सबान्धवान् ॥ … बाहुः सुन्दर-वेगानाम्) 5. 72. 11, 15.
सुमल्लिक: Sumallika m. (pl.): Name of a Jana-pada. Listed by Saṃjaya among the northern Janapadas (also called Deśas 6. 10. 68) of Bhāratavarṣa (अत ऊर्ध्वं जनपदान् निबोध) 6. 10. 37, 5; (सुदामानः सुमल्लि-काः) 6. 10. 53.
सुराष्ट्र: Surāṣṭra (Saurāṣṭraka) m. (pl.): Name of a Janapada and its people. A. Location: Listed by Saṃjaya among the northern Janapadas (also called Deśas 6. 10. 68: Viṣaya 2. 28. 40) of the Bhāratavarṣa (अत ऊर्ध्वं जनपदान् निबोध) 6. 10. 37, 5; (सुराष्ट्राः केकयास् तथा) 6. 10. 47; near the western ocean (see the next). B. Holiness: There were in Surāṣṭra holy places (आयतनानि) like Camasonmajjana, Prabhāsa in the nearby ocean (प्रभासं चोदधौ तीर्थम्), and Piṇḍāraka; holy cities like Dvāravatī (पुण्या द्वारवती); rivers, lakes and holy mountains (पुण्ये गिरौ) like Ujjayanta (सरितः शैलान् सरांसि च … । सुराष्ट्रेषु … पुण्यान्य् आयतनानि च) 3. 86. 16-24 (for Camason-majjana, Prabhāsa, Piṇḍāraka, Dvāravatī and mountain Ujjayanta see Vol. I). C. Characteristic: According to the demon Kalmāṣapāda people of Surāṣṭra were of mixed caste (संकरा वै सुराष्ट्राः) 8. 30. 73. D. Epic events: (1) Sahadeva in his expedition to the south of Indraprastha before the Rājasūya (प्रययौ दक्षिणां दिशम् 2. 28. 1, 37; 2. 23. 9) brought under control Āhṛti, the king of Surāṣṭras, with great effort; while he lived there (सुराष्ट्र-विषयस्थश् च) he sent for Rukmin, the king of Bhojakaṭa 2. 28. 39-40; (2) Before the start of the war, on the battle-field, Bṛhadbala helped by great chariot-fighters from Surāṣṭra and other countries, ready with their weapons, protected the army of Kauravas in the south (महा-रथैर् … सौराष्ट्रकैर् … आत्तशस्त्रैः । बृहद्बलः … बलं त्वदीयं दक्षिणतो ऽभिपाति) 6. 20. 14; (3) From the countries of the southern ocean, the Aśvamedha horse went to Gokarṇa, Prabhāsa and Dvāravati in Surāṣṭra (सुराष्ट्रान् अभितो ययौ) 14. 84. 12-13. E. Past events: Kuśarddhika, the king of Surāṣṭra, named by Bhīma among the eighteen infamous kings, who extirpated their kinsmen, friends and their relatives (अष्टादशेमे राजानः प्रख्याता … । ये समुच्चिच्छिदुर् ज्ञातीन् सुहृदश् च सबान्धवान् … सुराष्ट्राणां कुशर्द्धिकः) 5. 72. 11, 14. F. Āhṛti, the king of Surāṣṭra, is referred to as सुराष्ट्राधिपति 2. 28. 39.
सुवीर: Suvīra, Sauvīra (Sauvīraka) m. (pl.): Name of a Janapada and its people; they are often mentioned along with Sindhus. A. Location: Listed by Saṃjaya among the northern Janapadas (also called Deśas 6. 10. 68) of Bhāratavarṣa (अत ऊर्ध्वं जनपदान् निबोध) 6. 10. 37, 5; (काश्मीराः सिन्धुसौवीरा … ) 6. 10. 52; once also referred to as राष्ट्र (3. 252. 1). B. Description of their warriors: Excellent young heroes (सौवीरवीराः प्रवरा युवानो  … ) 3. 249. 12; brave (शूर) 6. 18. 13; strong (बलिन्) 3. 249. 12; 7. 85. 73; 6. 20. 10 (?); excellent attackers (प्रवराणां प्रहारिणाम्) 3. 255. 9; ready to lay their bodies (तनुत्यज्) 6. 18. 14; fighting with sharp lances (नखरप्रासयोधिन्) 7. 85. 73; 12. 102. 3. C. Characteristics of the people: Karṇa while deriding Śalya men-tioned Sindhus and Sauvīras as those who did not know धर्म since they were Mlecchas born in sinful countries and those who could not discern between धर्म and अधर्म; they wholeheartedly treaded on despicable paths (आ केशाग्रान् नखाग्राच् च वक्तव्येषु कुवर्त्मसु ॥ … सिन्धुसौवीरा धर्मं विद्युः कथं त्व् इह । पापदेशोद्-भवा म्लेच्छा धर्माणाम् अविचक्षणाः ॥ ) 8. 27. 90-91 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 8. 40. 42: वक्तव्येषु गर्हणीयेषु); he also told him that according to a Rākṣasī, Sindhus and Sauvīras were in general despicable; this was reported by a certain Brāhmaṇa in the Kuru assembly (वसातिसिन्धुसौवीरा इति प्रायो विकुत्सिताः) 8. 30. 41, 46-47. D. Epic events: (1) Kṛṣṇa recalled that Śiśupāla had abducted the unwilling wife of Babhru on her arrival at Suvīra country from Dvārakā (?) (सौवीरान् प्रतिपत्तौ च बभ्रोर् एष यशस्विनः । भार्याम् अभ्य-हरन् मोहाद् अकामां ताम् इतो गताम् ॥ ) 2. 42. 10 (Nī. reads (Bom. Ed. 2. 45. 10) सौवीरान् प्रतियाताम् and explains सौवीरान् देशविशेषान् इतो हस्तिनापुरात् गतां प्रस्थिताम्; he further adds: सौवीरात् प्रतिपत्तौ चेति पाठे प्रति-पत्तौ विवाहकाले बभ्रोर् यादवस्य); (2) When Jayadratha had started for the country of Śālvas (3. 248. 6), heroic, young warriors of Suvīra country accom-panied him (सौवीरवीरा … युवानो … अनु-यान्ति) 3. 249. 12; Koṭikāśya suggested to Jayadratha to abduct Draupadī and return to Suvīra country (सुवीरान् … व्रज) 3. 251. 6; Jayadratha invited Draupadī to be his wife and obtain the mastery of the entire Sindhu and Suvīra countries (अखिलान् सिन्धुसौवीरान् अवाप्नुहि) 3. 251. 18; during the battle with Jayadratha, Yudhiṣṭhira himself killed in a moment a hundred of excellent, attacking Suvīra warriors (राजा स्वयं सुवीराणां प्रवराणां प्रहारिणां । निमेषमात्रेण शतं जघान) 3. 255. 9; Arjuna cut off with भल्ल arrows the bows and heads of all the twelve Suvīra princes (सौवीरका द्वादश राजापुत्राः 3. 249. 9) accompanying Jayadratha (द्वादशानां तु सर्वेषां सौवीराणां … ) 3. 255. 27; the inmates of the आश्रम were happy to see Yudhiṣṭhira return with Draupadī after defeating the Sindhu and Suvīra warriors (जित्वा तान् सिन्धुसौवी रान्) 3. 255. 50; (3) The kings of Sindhu and Suvīra countries (सिन्धुसौवीरवासिनः), led by Jayadratha, joined the side of Duryodhana; their army was an अक्षौहिणी strong (तेषाम् अक्षौहिणी सेना) 5. 19. 14, 19-20; (4) In the arrange-ment of the Kaurava army on the battle-field, Sauvīras (सौवीराः) were among the twelve Janapadas who formed the rear-guard of Bhīṣma (पृष्ठगोपाः); they offered protection to Bhīṣma with their large number of chariot-fighters (महता रथवंशेन) 6. 18. 10, 13-14; 6. 20. 14; (5) On the second day of the war, Sindhu and Suvīra warriors (सिन्धुसौवीराः) pro-tected Droṇa who was behind Bhīṣma in the Mahāvyūha of Kauravas (6. 47. 10-12, 14); protected by Suvīra warriors and others, (प्राच्यसौवीरकेकयैः) Bhīṣma attacked Arjuna 6. 48. 21; (6) On the third day, warriors of the Sindhu and Suvīra countries, along with others, were posted at the ‘neck’ of the Garuḍavyūha of the Kauravas (मद्रकाः सिन्धुसौवीरास् … ॥ … ग्रीवायां संनिवेशिताः) 6. 52. 2-3, 5-6; as directed by Bhīṣma, all Suvīra troops, along with many others, quickly marched towards Arjuna ( … सौवीरगणाश् च सर्वे  … किरीटिनं त्वरमाणाभिसस्रुर् … ) 6. 55. 74; on that day Arjuna killed all Sauvīra troops (सौवीरगणाश् च सर्वे) with his Māhendra (or Aindra 6. 55. 110, 120) missile 6. 55. 130; (7) On the fifth day, the Sauvīra warriors (मद्रसौवीरगान्धा-रैस्) and others, afraid due to the sound of the Gāṇḍīva bow, took refuge with the king of Kaliṅga country and then all together attacked Arjuna (6. 67. 13, 16); (8) On the sixth day, Bhagadatta, accom-panied by the warriors of the Madra, Sauvīra and Kekaya countries, stood at the ‘chest’ position of the Krauñcavyūha of Kauravas (मद्रसौवीरकेकयैः । उरस्य् अभून् … ) 6. 71. 14, 18; (9) On the ninth day, Sauvīra warriors (सौवीराः) were among those who did not forsake Bhīṣma although they were getting killed by sharp arrows (6. 102. 7); (10) On the tenth day, Sauvīra warriors (सौवीराः), emboldened by Duryodhana (6. 112. 102, 105, 107) attacked Arjuna; he burnt (ददाह) them by the use of divine missiles; they then stopped attacking Arjuna who forced them to run away (द्रावयित्वा वरूथिनीम्) 6. 112. 108, 110-117; towards the end of the day, when the Kuru army afflicted by the arrows of Arjuna fled, Sauvīra warriors (सौवीराः) were among those twelve Jana-padas who, though afflicted by arrows and feeling pain due to wounds (शरार्ता व्रणपीडिताः) did not abandon Bhīṣma while he fought with Arjuna 6. 114. 75-77; (11) On the eleventh day, Karṇa led the archers (प्रमुखे सर्वधण्विनाम्) of the Śakaṭavyūha of Kauravas; Duryo-dhana who followed him was at the head of the Sauvīra warriors (सौवीराः), Kitavas and others 7. 6. 7-8, 15; (12) On the fourteenth day, the king of Avanti helped by the Sauvīra warriors (आवन्त्यः सह सौवीरैः) checked the advance of Dhṛṣṭa-dyumna towards Jayadratha 7. 70. 45, 51; Yudhiṣṭhira, at one stage, drew attention of Sātyaki towards Arjuna who was sur-rounded by brave warriors of the Sindhu and Suvīra countries, although their number was very much diminished, using sharp lances while fighting (सिन्धुसौवीरैर् नखरप्रासयोधिभिः । अत्यन्तापचितैः शूरैः) 7. 85. 73; but Sātyaki assured Yudhiṣṭhira that the warriors of Suvīra countries were not at all a match for Arjuna once he was angry (ये च सौवीरका योधास् … । एते ऽर्जुनस्य क्रुद्धस्य कलां नार्हन्ति षोडशीम्) 7. 86. 28-29; the army of Kauravas which included warriors from Sindhu, Suvīra and Kuru countries was scattered by the swift arrows of both Karṇa and Bhīma fighting with each other (ततो व्युदस्तं तत् सैन्यं सिन्धुसौवीरकौर-वम् । प्रोत्सारितं … ); afflicted by arrows and with their horses and men killed and chariots broken (हताश्वनरवाहनाः) they left Bhīma and Karṇa and ran in all direc-tions; thinking that the gods were deluding them for the benefit of Bhīma (नूनं पार्थार्थम् एवास्मान् मोहयन्ति दिवौ-कसः) they stopped shooting arrows and became spectators (शरपातं समुत्सृज्य स्थिता युद्धदिदृक्षवः) 7. 113. 7, 11-14; Karṇa was enraged to see the destruction all around of the army of Kuru, Sindhu and Suvīra countries (कुरुसौवीरसैन्ध-वानां बलक्षयम् … सर्वतः), the dead bodies of elephants, and the earth covered with the armours, banners and weapons 7. 114. 17-18; (13) On the fifteenth day, when Dhṛtarāṣṭra heard the death of Droṇa he remembered that Sātyaki had formerly defeated the large army of a king (not named) of the Suvīra country (सौवीर-राजस्य प्रमथ्य महतीं चमूं) 7. 9. 29; (14) When the war was over, Gāndhārī, on the battle-field, pointed out to Kṛṣṇa women of the Sindhu and Suvīra countries who sat around the dead body of Jayadratha keeping watch over him (तम् एताः पर्युपासन्ते रक्षमाणा महा-भुजम् । सिन्धुसौवीर° °स्त्रियः॑) 11. 22. 9. 11. E. Past events: (1) Vidurā exhorted Saṃjaya not to be under the control of the Sindhu maidens but live, as before, feeling proud of being in the company of the Sauvīra maidens (उष्य सौवीरकन्याभिः श्लाघस्वार्थैर् यथा पुरा । मा च सैन्धवकन्यानाम् अवसन्नो वशं गमः ॥ ) 5. 132. 32; (2) Ajabindu, the king of the Suvīra people, mentioned by Bhīma among those eighteen kings who, born at the end of the aeon, extirpated their kinsmen, friends and relatives (अष्टादशेमे राजानः … ये समुच्चिच्छिदुर् ज्ञातीन् सु-हृदश् च सबान्धवान् ॥ … अजबिन्दुः … सुवीराणां … । … यूगान्ते … संभूताः … ) 5. 72. 11, 14, 17. F. Some persons, especially Jayadratha, are referred to as belonging to the Suvīra country or as pro-tector or king of Suvīra country or people: A. One related to Suvīra country: (i) सौवीर: Jayadratha 3. 251. 6; 3. 255. 8; (ii) सौवीरी (f.): Wife (not named) of Manasyu 1. 89. 7; (iii) सौवीरक: (1) Jayadratha 3. 251. 1; (2) Twelve princes (not named) who accompanied Jayadratha 3. 249. 9; B. Heroes from Suvīra country: सौवीरकवीर: Balāhaka, Anīka, Vidāraṇa (or Anīkavidāraṇa ?) and others, brothers of Jayadratha 3. 249. 12; C. Protector or king of Suvīra country: (i) सुवीरराष्ट्रप: Jayadratha 3. 252. 1; (ii) पतिः सौवीर-(सिन्धूनाम्): Jayadratha 3. 251. 7; (iii) सौवीरभर्तृ: Jayadratha 11. 22. 9; (iv) सौवीरराज: (1) Jayadratha 3. 249. 11; 3. 3. 252. 12-132; (2) A king, not named 7. 9. 29; (v) राजा सुवीराणाम्: (1) Jayadratha 3. 255. 9; (2) Śatruṃtapa 12. 138. 4; (vi) सौवीर (सिन्धूनाम्) ईश्वरः: Jayadratha 7. 53. 11.
सुस्थर: Susthara m. (pl.): Name of a people. Mentioned among many others who, afraid of Jarāsandha, left the north and resorted to the south (सुस्थराश् च सुकु-ट्टाश् च … ॥ ; तथोत्तरां दिशं चापि परि-त्यज्य भयार्दिताः । … दक्षिणां दिशम् आश्रिताः ॥ ) 2. 13. 25, 27.
सुह्म: Suhma m. (pl.): Name of a people. A. Location: Listed by Saṃjaya among the northern Janapadas (also called Deśas 6. 10. 68) of Bhāratavarṣa (अत ऊर्ध्वं जनोपदान् निबोध) 6. 10. 37, 5; (सुह्माश् च विजयास् तथा) 6. 10. 44; the country of Suhmas lay to the north of Hāstinapura (see B. Epic events No. 2 below) and also to the east of Hāstinapura beyond Magadha and Videha (see B. Epic events No. 1. below); a part of it was near the Aṅga country and the other near Vaṅga and Tāmralipta; this latter part was, it appears, designated eastern Suhma (Prācya-suhma) (see B. Epic events No. 3 below). B. Epic events: (1) After his marriage, Pāṇḍu wishing to conquer the whole earth (कृतोद्वाहः … जिगीषमाणो वसुधाम् 1. 105. 7) conquered the Magadha and the Videha countries and then extended the fame of Kurus as far as Kāśis, Suhmas and Puṇḍras (तथा काशिषु सुह्मेषु पुण्ड्रेषु … । … कुरूणाम् अकरोद् यशः ॥ ) 1. 105. 12; (2) Arjuna in his expedition to the north (दिशं धनपतेर् इष्टाम् 2. 23. 9; प्रयाव् उत्तराम् तस्माद् दिशम् धनदपालिताम् 2. 24. 1) before the Rājasūya harassed Suhmas and Colas (सुह्मांश् च चोलांश् च … । … प्रामथत् कुरुनन्दनः) 2. 24. 20; (3) Bhīmasena in his expedition to the east (ययौ प्राचीं दिशं प्रति 2. 26. 1; 2. 27. 9) defeated in battle Suhmas and Prācya-suhmas; he defeated the king of Suhmas (ततः सुह्मान् प्राच्यसुह्मान् … विजित्य युधि कौन्तेयो … ॥ सुह्मानाम् अधिपं चैव) 2. 27. 14, 23 (Suhmas here distin-guished as Suhmas and Prācyasuhmas); (4) On the seventeenth day of war, at night, when Karṇa's death was reported to Dhṛtarāṣṭra (हते कर्णे महाराज निशि … 8. 1. 25; 8. 2. 20; 8. 5. 1) he remembered Karṇa's past exploits one of which was his having defeated the Suhmas and made them pay tribute (सुह्मान् अङ्गांश् च … यो जित्वा समरे वीरश् चक्रे बलिभृतः पुरा) 8. 5. 19-20 (reference to Karṇa's दिग्विजय before the Vaiṣṇavayajña of Duryodhana 3. 241. 32; Cr. edn. Vol. 4. App. 1. 24. 41-44; however, Suhma is not directly mentioned here among the eastern countries).
सृञ्जय: Sṛñjaya m. (pl.): Name of a people, very likely a section of the Pāñcālas; some-times they are almost identified with them, but sometimes mentioned along with them and/or with Somakas. A. Description of their warriors: Magnanimous (महात्मन्) 6. 85. 21; very vigorous (महौजस्) 7. 132. 41; heroic (वीर) 6. 68. 15; of great strength (महा-बल) 6. 86. 76; 6. 103. 11; difficult to be attacked (दुराधर्ष) 6. 103. 10; great archers (महेष्वास) 6. 16. 42; 8. 40. 4; great chariot-fighters (महारथ) 8. 40. 2; tigers among men (पुरुषव्याघ्र) 7. 101. 51. B. Epic events: (1) Bhīma told Yudhiṣṭhira that it was not impossible to get back the kingdom by waging war with Kauravas since Pāṇḍavas could count on the help of Sṛñjayas, Kaikeyas and Kṛṣṇa (in such contexts they are identified with Pāñcālas) 3. 34. 85; he also told him that all his relatives as well as Sṛñjayas wish well of him and keep quiet (only he and Draupadī got excited) (सर्वे ते प्रियम् इच्छन्ति बान्धवाः सह सृञ्जयैः । अहम् एको ऽभिसंतप्तो माता च प्रतिविन्ध्यतः ॥ ) 3. 36. 15; (2) Dhṛtarāṣṭra felt that it was better to give back to Pāṇḍavas their share of kingdom before war broke out in which Yudhiṣṭhira would be backed by Kṛṣṇa, Sātyaki and Sṛñjayas 5. 22. 9; 5. 56. 33; when he sent Saṃjaya to Upa-plavya, he asked him (Saṃjaya) to enquire about the health of all including Sṛñjayas (तेषां भागं … पुरा युद्धात् साधु तस्य प्रदानम् ॥ … अनामयं मद्वचनेन पृ-च्छेः) 5. 22. 8-9, 38; (3) Sañjaya wanted Yudhiṣṭhira to work for peace so that Kauravas, Pāṇḍavas, Sṛñjayas and the rest of the assembled kings would live in happi-ness (शमं कुर्या येन शर्माप्नुयुस् ते) 5. 24. 9; Yudhiṣṭhira asked Saṃjaya to communicate the message of Dhṛtarāṣṭra to the assembly in which Sṛñjayas were also present 5. 25. 1; Saṃjaya appealed to all of them to act in a way that would lead to the well-being of Kurus and Sṛñja-yas (कृताञ्जलिः शरणं वः प्रपद्ये कथं स्वस्ति स्यात् कुरुसृञ्जयानाम्) 5. 25. 14; Yudhiṣṭhira failed to see how there could be well-being for Kurus and Sṛñjayas when Dhṛtarāṣṭra had usurped the pro-sperity of Pāṇḍavas (कथं स्वस्ति स्यात् कुरुसृञ्जयानाम् । आत्तैश्वर्यो धृतराष्ट्रः परेभ्यः । ) 5. 26. 18; Yudhiṣṭhira also told Saṃjaya that Sṛñjayas followed the advice of Kṛṣṇa and hence were cap-able of controlling their enemies and de-lighting their friends (सृञ्जयाश् … । उपासीना वासुदेवस्य बुद्धिं … ) 5. 28. 11; (4) Saṃjaya told Duryodhana that Pāṇḍavas and Sṛñjayas heard attentively all that Arjuna wanted him to convey to the Kurus; Arjuna said that Duryodhana would repent when he saw Dhṛṣṭa-dyumna fighting at the head of the army of Sṛñjayas; he also told Saṃjaya that their Brāhmaṇas who were experts in astrology had predicted the destruction of Kurus and Sṛñjayas in war 5. 47. 5, 37, 93; (5) Dhṛtarāṣṭra envied those who could see and listen to the words of Kṛṣṇa which were meant for the welfare of Sṛñjayas (भारतीम् … शङ्करीं सृञ्जया-नाम्) 5. 69. 2 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 5. 71. 2: शंकरीं कल्याणकरीम्); (6) Kṛṣṇa assured Yudhiṣṭhira that when he met the Kauravas he would try to keep the agitated Kurus and Sṛñjayas away from the noose of death (मोचयेयं मृत्युपाशात् संरब्-धान् कुरुसृञ्जयान्) 5. 70. 81; (7) Before Kṛṣṇa left to meet the Kauravas, Drau-padī told him that the Pāṇḍavas, along with Sṛñjayas would be able to face the army of Kauravas (शक्ष्यन्ति हि महाबाहो पाण्डवाः सृञ्जयैः सह । धार्तराष्ट्र-बलं … प्रतिसमासितुम्) 5. 80. 11 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 5. 82. 11: प्रतिसमासितुं प्रतिपक्षतया स्थातुम्); according to her, severe punishment should be quickly in-flicted on Kauravas by Pāṇḍavas, Sṛñjayas and Kṛṣṇa; he should take care to see that he, along with Pāṇḍavas and Sṛñjayas, was not blamed for not killing one who deserved to be killed 5. 80. 14, 18-19; (8) Kṛṣṇa assured Vidura that he would attempt to bring about reconciliation between Kurus and Sṛñjayas who would otherwise perish in war (संग्रामे विन-शिष्यताम्) 5. 91. 8; (9) Duryodhana wanted to know from Kṛṣṇa what wrong did the Kauravas do to Pāṇḍavas and Sṛñjayas or for what fault of Kauravas did they want to kill Kauravas (किम् अस्मा-भिः कृतं तेषां कस्मिन् वा पुनर् आगसि) 5. 125. 11; (10) When Ulūka was asked by Yudhiṣṭhira to convey to the assembly the view of Duryodhana, he spoke to them who included, among others, all Sṛñjayas 5. 158. 4-5; (11) Bhīṣma assured Duryo-dhana that in case of war Droṇa would kill Sṛñjayas (गच्छेद् अन्तं सृञ्जयानाम्) 5. 164. 15; (12) Before the start of the war, Duryodhana told Duḥśāsana to pro-tect Bhīṣma so that he might kill Pāṇḍavas and Sṛñjayas 6. 16. 14; seeing Bhīṣma at the head of the Kaurava army, Pāṇḍavas and Sṛñjayas, led by Dhṛṣṭadyumna, shivered (समकम्पन्त पाण्डवाः । सृञ्जयाश् च  … धृष्टद्युम्नपुरोगमाः ॥ ) 6. 16. 42; (13) On the third day of the war, due to the quickness of Bhīṣma's action, Pāṇḍavas and Sṛñjayas felt that there were many hundreds and thousands of him (अनेक-शतसाहस्रम् समपश्यन्त लाघवात्) 6. 55. 22 (also cf. st. 21); (14) On the fourth day, at one stage, Kurus and Sṛñja-yas watched the duel between Bhīṣma and Arjuna 6. 56. 28; (15) On the fifth day, towards midday (मध्यन्दिनगते सूर्ये 6. 68. 12), Sṛñjayas fought a very fierce battle with Kurus in which arrows, शक्तिस्, तोमरस् were used 6. 68. 15-16; the battle describ-ed 18-19; the same day, later, Sṛñjayas, when they lost their armours, and their chariots were broken and bows were cut off, and their hair dishevelled, they wrestled with Kurus (बाहुभिः समयुध्यन्त) 6. 69. 39; when the sun was about to set (सूर्ये ऽस्तम् उपगच्छति 6. 70. 34), and when the stopping of the war was declared, Pāṇḍavas, along with Sṛñjayas, went to their camps 6. 70. 37; (16) On the sixth day, when Bhīṣma and Droṇa started killing the Pāṇḍava army, Sṛñjayas and Kekayas fied (पलायनपराभवन्) 6. 71. 32; (17) On the seventh day, when Bhīṣma attack-ed Yudhiṣṭhira, Sṛñjayas riding chariots, elephants and horses trembled for they feared Yudhiṣṭhira would soon be killed (सरथनागाश्वाः समकम्पन्त सृञ्जयाः) 6. 82. 2-3; later in the afternoon (अपरां दिशम् आस्थाय स्थिते सवितरि 6. 82. 28) Bhīṣma neglected the challenge of Śikha-ṇḍin and attacked Sṛñjayas; they were happy to face Bhīṣma (सृञ्जयास् तु ततो हृष्टा … ) and raised loud roars and blew their conches; a fierce battle followed in which chariot-fighters and elephant-riders mingled with one another 6. 82. 26-28; (18) On the eighth day, Bhīṣma started killing Sṛñjayas, Pāñcālas and others; they attacked Bhīṣma not fearing death (Sṛñja-yas not directly mentioned, only Pāñcālas are mentioned); Bhīṣma cut off arms and heads of those riding horses and elephants and deprived the chariot-fighters of their chariots; he also killed elephants 6. 84. 3-7; when Droṇa killed Somakas and Sṛñjayas a loud cry went up from their army; the Kṣatriyas rolled on the ground like those afflicted by ailments; their cry was like one of those who become lean due to hunger (विवेष्टन्तः स्म दृश्यन्ते व्याधिक्लिष्टा नरा इव ॥ … अनिशं श्रूयते शब्दः क्षुत्कृशानां नृणाम् इव ॥ ) 6. 85. 20-23; after the death of Irāvant, there was fierce fighting in which the Kaurava army and Sṛñjayas, not caring for their lives in battle, killed one another; with their hair loose and without their armours, when they were deprived of their chariots and their bows were cut off they wrestl-ed with one another (जुह्वतः समरे प्राणान् निजघ्नुर् इतरेतरम् ॥ मुक्तकेशा विकवचा विरथाश् छिन्नकार्मुकाः । बाहु-भिः समयुध्यन्त समवेताः परस्प-रम् ॥ ) 6. 86. 76-77; when Bhagadatta proceeded to attack Yudhiṣṭhira, he fought a severe battle with Pāñcālas, Sṛñjayas and Kekayas who were ready to fight with their weapons (उद्यतायुधैः) 6. 91. 79-80; Bhīṣma told Duryodhana that since he had dug up enmity with Pāṇḍavas and Sṛñjayas he should fight with them manfully; he him-self also would kill Somakas and Pāñcālas (which term includes Sṛñjayas) (युध्यस्व तान् अद्य रणे … पुरुषो भव) 6. 94. 13-15; (19) At the end of the ninth day, it appeared that Bhīṣma had defeated Pāṇḍavas and Sṛñjayas; so at the start of the night (रात्रिमुखे) Pāṇḍavas, Vṛṣṇis and Sṛñjayas held consultation (मन्त्राय समुपाविशन्) 6. 103. 8, 10-11; (20) At the start of the tenth day, Kaurava army was being destroyed by the sharp arrows of Pāṇḍavas and Sṛñjayas; hence, Bhīṣma, not caring for life, attacked them 6. 104. 23, 26, 29; Dhṛtarāṣṭra asked Saṃjaya how on the tenth day Bhīṣma, when attack-ed by Śikhaṇḍin determined to kill him (6. 104. 45-46), fought with Pāṇḍavas and Sṛñjayas (दशमे ऽहनि) 6. 105. 3; when Bhīṣma began to destroy the Pāṇḍava army, the great chariot-fighters (महारथाः) of Sṛñjayas attacked Bhīṣma to kill him (वधायाभ्यद्रवन् भीष्मम्) 6. 105. 35; as the war advanced Pāṇḍavas, backed by Sṛñjayas (संहताः सह सृञ्जयैः), attacked Bhīṣma 6. 110. 40; Dhṛtarāṣṭra once again asked Saṃjaya how Bhīṣma fought with Pāṇḍavas and Sṛñjayas on the tenth day 6. 111. 1; as advised by Bhīṣma, Arjuna led Sṛñjayas (and Pāñcālas) to attack Bhīṣma and kill him; Sṛñjayas were asked to attack Bhīṣma without fear as they would be protected by Bhīma and Arjuna 6. 111. 15-20; exhorted by Dhṛṣṭadyumna, Somakas and Sṛñjayas attacked Bhīṣma showering weapons on him (शस्त्रवृष्ट्या); angered Bhīṣma fought with them 6. 113. 16-18; the weapons used by Sṛñjayas are detailed in 6. 114. 2-3; Sṛñjayas and Pāṇḍavas raised a loud roar when Bhīṣma fell down 6. 114. 101; at the end of the tenth day when Dhṛtarāṣṭra was informed about Bhīṣma's downfall he wondered who could be the warriors who surrounded Bhīṣma (के वीराः पर्यवारयन्) while he was showering arrows on Pāñcālas and Sṛñjayas; he also wished to know who from among the Kauravas were on the left side of the wheel of Bhīṣma and shot arrows on Sṛñjayas (वामे चक्रे वर्तमानाः के ऽघ्नन् संजय सृञ्जयान्) 6. 15. 25, 28, 32; (21) On hearing the death of Bhīṣma (7. 2. 1), Karṇa admitted that the army which included Pāṇḍavas, Sātyaki, Kṛṣṇa and Sṛñjayas was invincible by kings; 7. 2. 31; (22) On the eleventh day, Pāṇḍavas and Sṛñjayas met with arrows Droṇa's attack on them; Droṇa broke and scattered their army; agitated by the arrows of Droṇa, they were again and again sca-ttered by him (ते कम्प्यमाना द्रोणेन बाणैः पाण्डवसृञ्जयाः । पुनः पुनर् अभ-ज्यन्त) 7. 6. 33, 35, 41; Sṛñjayas, though they tried, were not able to kill the army of Droṇa as it was protected by him; since Droṇa was acting very swiftly, Pāṇḍavas and Sṛñjayas felt as if there were many Droṇas (एकम् आशुकारिणम् आहवे । अनेकम् इव संत्रासान् मेनिरे) 7. 12. 19, 23; Sṛñjayas trembled seeing Droṇa, like fire, burning the army of Pāṇḍavas (साक्षाद् अग्निम् इवो-त्थितम्) 7. 13. 2; Sṛñjayas and others with their weapons raised (उद्यतायुधाः) met the attack of Aśvasena and others; a fierce battle ensued 7. 15. 11-12; at the sunset when the withdrawal of the Pāṇḍava army was declared by Arjuna (स्वान्य् अनीकानि … अवहारयत्), Sṛñjayas greeted him for his deeds during the day 7. 15. 49-50; (23) On the twelfth day, after killing Śatānīka, Droṇa repeatedly defeated Sṛñjayas and others; seeing Droṇa, like fire, burning the army of Pāṇḍavas, Sṛñjayas trembled; due to the heroism of Droṇa, a river carrying the bodies of Kurus and Pāñcālas to the god of death began to flow (नदीम् अन्तक-गामिनीम्) 7. 20. 23-24, 34, 36; when Droṇa killed a Pāñcāla prince, Sṛñjayas and others attacked Droṇa shouting ‘kill Droṇa, kill Droṇa’ (हत द्रोणं हत द्रोणम् इत्य् आसीत् तुमुलं महत् । ); but Droṇa agitated them who were very angry 7. 20. 48-49; when Sṛñjayas and others were agitated and were pushed back (चलितान् … प्रणुन्नान्) by the arrows of Droṇa, Kauravas raised a loud roar 7. 21. 7-8; Duryodhana drew attention of Karṇa towards Bhīma who was deserted by Pāṇḍava warriors and Sṛñjayas (हीनः पाण्डवसृञ्जयैः) 7. 21. 16; (24) On the thirteenth day, Pāñcāla army which included thousands of Sṛñjayas attacked Droṇa; but Droṇa arrested their advance with arrows; then Pāñcālas and Sṛñjayas did not attack him 7. 34. 5-7, 10; when Abhi-manyu defeated Duḥśāsana, Sṛñjayas and others were delighted 7. 39. 11, 17-18; when Subhadrā heard the death of Abhi-manyu, she pitied Sṛñjayas and the rest who did not seem to know when Abhi-manyu was felled down (धिक् केकयांस् … सृञ्जयान् । ये त्वा रणे गतं वीरं न जानन्ति निपातितम्) 7. 55. 13; (25) On the fourteenth day, Sātyaki shot arrows at Droṇa who was as though swallowing (ग्रसन्तम् इव) Sṛñjayas 7. 72. 34; the demon Alambusa made a river flow on the battle-field carrying the dead bodies of Sṛñjayas and others (नदीं प्रवर्तयाम् आस) 7. 83. 30; when the Pāṇḍava army, which included Sṛñjayas, attacked Droṇa there was a loud roar among the Sṛñjayas (तत्रारावो महान् आसीत्); when Droṇa started killing them, Sṛñjayas found no protector 7. 85. 20, 26; Yudhiṣṭhira assured Sātyaki that when he (Sātyaki) would leave to assist Arjuna, Sṛñjayas and others would be there to protect him (Yudhiṣṭhira) 7. 86. 45; Sṛñjayas and others, thrilled, rushed at Droṇa to fight with him with all their might (सर्वशक्त्या); but Droṇa killed them 7. 101. 50-52; Droṇa asked Duryo-dhana to go to help Jayadratha; he himself would obstruct the onward march of Sṛñjayas and others 7. 105. 21; (26) After the death of Jayadratha, before the start of the night war between the fourteenth and fifteenth day, Droṇa pointed out to Duryodhana the armies of Pāṇḍavas and Sṛñjayas marching towards him (Droṇa) 7. 126. 31; he directed Duryodhana to hold back his army if he could, for Kurus and Sṛñjayas would continue to fight even dur-ing the night; with these words, Droṇa mar-ched against Pāṇḍavas and Sṛñjayas (त्वं च दुर्योधन बलं यदि शक्नोषि धारय) 7. 126. 38-39; then, there was fierce fighting in the evening (संध्यायाम्) all around between Droṇa and Sṛñjayas 7. 129. 18; when the fierce fighting progressed during the night, Pāṇḍavas and Sṛñjayas together attacked Droṇa (रात्रियुद्धे तथा घोरे वर्तमाने सुदारुणे); Droṇa forced all of them back killing some of them (तान् सर्वान् विमुखांश् चक्रे कांश्चिन् निन्ये यमक्षयम्) 7. 129. 34-35; Dhṛtarāṣṭra asked Saṃjaya how did Kauravas feel when Droṇa entered the (army of) Sṛñjayas (का वो ऽभूद् वै मतिस् तदा) 7. 130. 1; Sṛñjayas and Pāñcālas followed Bhīma and Arjuna who showered arrows on Droṇa trying to scatter the army of Drupada with Vāyavyāstra 7. 132. 37, 41; 7. 136. 14; Aśvatthāman challenged his opponents to attack him and then killed Pāñcālas and Sṛñjayas; they abandoned Aśvatthāman and fled in all directions (व्यद्रवन्त दिशो दश 7. 135. 19) when their chariots and banners were scattered (विप्रकीर्णरथध्वजाः) 7. 135. 51; Duryodhana asked Duḥśāsana and his other brothers to offer protection to Droṇa who would then kill Sṛñjayas and their kings (सृञ्जयांश् च सराजकान्); when all Sṛñjayas were killed, Aśvatthāman would kill Dhṛṣṭadyumna 7. 139. 24-25; in the fighting that followed Aśvatthāman cover-ed Drupada and Droṇa covered Sṛñjayas with smooth arrows (छादयाम् आसतुः संख्ये शरैः संनतपर्वभिः) 7. 139. 31; when Aśvatthāman swooned while fight-ing with Ghaṭotkaca, Pāñcālas and Sṛñjayas raised a loud roar (सिंहनादं प्रच-क्रिरे) 7. 141. 32; considering that Bhīma had killed Duryodhana, Pāñcālas, Sṛñjayas and others made all effort to attack Droṇa to fight with him (सर्वोद्योगेनाभिजग्मुर्  … ); a fierce battle then was fought 7. 141. 60; when Pāñcālas and Sṛñjayas were being killed by Karṇa, they apprehended his presence nearby even when a blade of grass stirred (तृणप्रस्पन्दनाच् चापि सूत-पुत्रं स्म मेनिरे) 7. 148. 15 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 7. 173. 19: अतिभयात् तृणचलन-मात्रेणापि कर्णं प्राप्तं मेनिरे); they mistook a running warrior on their own side to be Karṇa (अपि स्वं समरे योधं धावमानं विचेतसः । कर्णम् एवाभ्य-मन्यन्त … ); hence, afraid, they ran but Karṇa attacked them from behind (पृष्ठतो विकिरञ् शरान्) 7. 148. 15-17; when Pāñcālas and Sṛñjayas were excessi-vely tormented by the Rākṣasas of Alā-yudha they had no peace of mind (न शान्तिं लेभिरे तत्र) 7. 152. 31; Dhṛta-rāṣṭra wondered why Karṇa, instead of killing Ghaṭotkaca, did not kill Arjuna with the शक्ति given to him by Indra; for, the death of Arjuna would have meant the death of all Pāṇḍavas and Sṛñjayas long ago 7. 157. 2; the same opinion was held by Kṛṣṇa (and hence he deluded the mind of Karṇa whenever he faced Arjuna) 7. 157. 35; Dhṛtarāṣṭra asked Saṃjaya how did Sṛñjayas and Pāñcālas with their armies arrayed and in striking position (व्यूढानी-काः प्रहारिणः) fight with Kurus and how did they attack Droṇa who, not caring for his life, had plunged into their army after the death of Ghaṭotkaca (जीवितं त्यक्त्वा गाहमानं वरूथिनीम्) 7. 158. 13-15; Droṇa killed three grand-sons of Drupada and then defeated Cedis, Kekayas, Sṛñjayas and Matsyas 7. 161. 31-32; (27) On the fifteenth day, Pāñcālas and Sṛñjayas, although they were being killed by Droṇa, attacked him and confused him (मोहयन्तो महारथम्) 7. 164. 60; after killing Vasu-dāna (king of Pāṃśurāṣṭra), Droṇa killed six thousand Sṛñjayas 7. 164. 85; exhorted by Yudhiṣṭhira to assist Dhṛṣṭadyumna, the great chariot-fighters of Sṛñjayas attacked Droṇa in order to kill him; Droṇa with great speed moved against them not mind-ing his death (मर्तव्यम् इति निश्चितः); bad omens occurred; Droṇa, encircled by the armies of Drupada, moved burning host of Kṣatriyas and killed a very large number of them 7. 165. 8-16; when ulti-mately Droṇa was killed by Dhṛṣṭadyumna, Pāṇḍavas and Sṛñjayas attacked the dis-heartened Kurus with the result that their army was shattered (निरुत्साहान् कुरून्  … अभ्यद्रवन् … ततः सैन्यं व्यदीर्-यत) 7. 165. 58; when Aśvatthāman used his नारायणास्त्र, Pāṇḍavas, Pāñcālas and Sṛñjayas were dismayed to see the mid-region filled with different weapons (शस्त्राकृतिभिर् आकीर्णम् अतीव … दृष्ट्वा-न्तरिक्षम् आविग्नाः पाण्डुपाञ्चालसृञ्जयाः) 7. 170. 20; at the end of the day, when Saṃjaya reported to Dhṛtarāṣṭra the death of Droṇa, he asked Saṃjaya what was Droṇa doing on the battle-field when Pāṇḍavas and Sṛñjayas managed to kill him (किं कुर्वाणं रणे द्रोणम् जघ्नुः पाण्डवसृञ्जयाः) 7. 8. 1; Saṃjaya assured Dhṛtarāṣṭra that since he was an eye-witness to the whole event (सर्वं प्रत्यक्षदर्शिवान्) he would narrate to him how Droṇa fell when overpowered (सादितः) by Pāṇḍavas and Sṛñjayas 7. 11. 1; (28) On the sixteenth day, Duryodhana was confident that with Karṇa as their general Pāṇḍavas, Pāñcālas and Sṛñjayas would loose their consciousness (गतचेतसः) 8. 6. 31; Kṛṣṇa pointed out to Arjuna that Karṇa, as intended by Aśvatthāman (अश्व-त्थामनश् च संकल्पाद् … ) had killed Sṛñjayas 8. 16. 5;
