Karṇa brought Sṛñjayas and Pāñcālas within the range of his arrows and crushed them (शरगोचरम् आनयत् । ममर्द); Kurus, Pāṇḍavas and Sṛñjayas fought with great effort not caring for their life (व्यायच्छमानाः सुभृशम् … प्रियान् असून् रणे त्यक्त्वा) 8. 16. 22, 24-25; battle described 8. 16. 26-38; at mid-day (मध्यं गते दिनकरे 8. 17. 100), although Karṇa killed Sṛñjayas they attack-ed him 8. 17. 117; (29) On the seven-teenth day, early morning (प्रभातायां रजन्यां तु 8. 22. 29) before the start of the war, Duryodhana while requesting Śalya to act as a charioteer of Karṇa told him that with a good charioteer like him, Karṇa would be able to destroy Pāṇḍavas, Pāñcā-las and Sṛñjayas 8. 23. 15; at the start of the war on that day, Pāñcālas, Cedis and Sṛñjayas fought a fierce battle with the Kaurava army 8. 32. 15; Dhṛtarāṣṭra remembered that Karṇa had boasted earlier that he alone would kill Sṛñjayas along with Pāṇḍavas 8. 35. 2; Sṛñjayas cut off (शातयाम् आसुः) the arrows shot at them by Kṛpa 8. 38. 4; Karṇa stopped the on-ward march of Sṛñjayas and others who were led by Bhīma 8. 38. 16; Karṇa killed Cedis, Karūṣas and Sṛñjayas in the presence of Bhīma; when Bhīma left Karṇa to fight with the Kuru army, Karṇa killed thou-sands of great archers of Sṛñjayas (सृञ्-जयांश् च महेश्वासान् निजघान सहस्र-शः) 8. 40. 2-4; Sṛñjayas were ‘burnt’ by the fire in the form of Karṇa (कर्णाग्निना  … दग्धा … ) 8. 40. 61; Arjuna pointed out to Kṛṣṇa that the large army of Sṛñjayas was being scattered (दीर्यते) by Karṇa 8. 40. 81; when Bhīma returned to fight (संनिवृत्तो रणं प्रति), Pāñcālas and Sṛñjayas, led by Dhṛṣṭadyumna, followed him 8. 41. 3; Kurus led by Karṇa and Sṛñjayas led by Yudhiṣṭhira faced one another without fear (अभीताः) 8. 42. 1; Kṛṣṇa pointed out to Arjuna that Karṇa, after defeating Pāṇḍavas, Pāñcālas and Sṛñjayas was looking for Arjuna: when the Kuru warriors saw Karṇa displaying his valour by harassing Pāṇḍavas and thousands of Sṛñjayas they raised a loud roar (नदन्ति); Karṇa encouraged Kau-rava warriors to attack Sṛñjayas so that none of them escaped alive (यथा जिवन् न वः कश्चिन् मुच्यते) 8. 43. 36; Kṛṣṇa was glad to point out to Arjuna that Bhīma, along with Sātyaki and Sṛñjayas, had once again returned to the battle-field 8. 43. 52; Yudhiṣṭhira wondered whether the en-counter of Sṛñjayas and Kauravas in which he was humiliated had become known to the fighters (कच्चित् संग्रामे विदितो वा तदायं समागमः सृञ्जयकौरवा-णाम् । यत्रावस्थाम् ईदृशीं प्रापितो ऽहम्) 8. 46. 41; Kṛṣṇa told Arjuna that all Pāñcālas and Sṛñjayas with their followers were prepared to fight when they had resorted to him (एते च सर्वे पाञ्चालाः सृञ्जयाश् च सहान्वयाः । त्वां समासाद्य  … व्यवस्थिताः) 8. 51. 5; while taking stock of some of the events of the battle which had lasted for seventeen days (अद्य सप्तदशाहानि 8. 51. 2), Kṛṣṇa reminded Arjuna that while Bhīṣma was fighting, Sṛñjayas were unable to look at him; Bhīṣma routed Pāṇḍavas and Sṛñjayas and distinguished himself as the sole war hero (एकवीरत्वम् आगतः) 8. 51. 35; Kṛṣṇa pointed out to Arjuna that Bhīma, covered on all sides by Sṛñjayas, was being tormented while fighting with Karṇa: if Karṇa was neglected he might kill Pāṇḍavas, Sṛñjayas and Pāñcālas 8. 51. 105-106; at one stage in the battle, Utta-maujas had engaged Sṛñjayas 8. 53. 6; Arjuna asked Kṛṣṇa to drive his chariot towards Karṇa, lest he destroyed all Sṛñ-jaya great chariot-fighters in battle in their presence (राधेयो ऽप्य् अन्यथा पार्थान् सृञ्जयांश् च महारथान् । निःशेषान् समरे कुर्यात् पश्यतोर् नौ जनार्दन ॥ ) 8. 57. 8; later, Kuru warriors and Sṛñjayas fought with one another using straight-flying and very sharp arrows (शरैस् तदाञ्जोगतिभिः सुतेजनैः) 8. 57. 67; once again a very severe fighting broke out between Kurus and Sṛñjayas in which they used besides arrows weapons like swords, शक्तिस्, lances, maces and परश्वधस् 8. 62. 40; when Karṇa was killed, Arjuna was honoured by Sṛñjayas, Pāñcālas and others 8. 69. 37; on the seventeenth night (निशि 8. 1. 25) while reporting Karṇa's death to Dhṛtarāṣṭra Saṃjaya told him that Karṇa, before his death, had killed Kekayas and Videhas in the presence of all Sṛñjayas and Pāñcālas (स सृञ्जयानां सर्वेषां पाञ्चालानां च पश्यताम् । केकयानां विदेहानाम् अकरोत् कदनं महत् ॥ ) 8. 2. 18; Dhṛtarāṣṭra asked Saṃjaya who among the Kurus and Sṛñjayas were dead and who were alive 8. 4. 3; (30) On the eighteenth day, when Śalya became the general the Madras encouraged him saying that he was capable of defeating in battle even gods and demons, let alone mortals like Somakas and Sṛñjayas 9. 6. 9; a fierce battle was fought by Sṛñjayas with Kurus which terrorized Kurus (कुरूणां भयवर्ध-नम्) 9. 8. 1; as a result of the battle there began to flow a terrific river (नदी रौद्रा) filled with the bodies of Kurus and Sṛñjayas (कुरुसृञ्जयसंकुला) 9. 8. 32; seeing the heroic deeds (विक्रमम्) of Śalya, Duryodhana considered Pāṇḍavas, Pāñcālas and Sṛñjayas (as good as) dead (निहतान् … मेने) 9. 12. 28; finally, when Śalya was killed, Pāṇḍavas and Śṛñjayas chased the shattered (प्रभग्नान्) army of Kauravas 9. 18. 28; when Śālva, riding an elephant, attacked the Pāṇḍava army, Sṛñjayas and others thought his swiftly moving single elephant, to be several thousands (सहस्रशो वै विचरन्तम् एकम्) 9. 19. 6; when the Pāṇḍava army was broken, Kaurava heroes blew, in joy, their conches; Dhṛṣṭadyumna, the general of the armies of Pāṇḍavas and Sṛñjayas, could not bear the sound of the roar indi-cative of the joy of Kauravas (8. 19. 10); seeing the (heroic) deeds of Śālva, Sṛñjayas and others encircled his elephant 9. 19. 21; during the war of eighteen days eleven अक्षौहिणिस् of Duryodhana's army were killed by Pāṇḍavas and Sṛñjayas 9. 28. 14; Duryodhana felt confident to defeat Pāṇḍavas, Pāñcālas and Sṛñjayas with mace as his weapon 9. 31. 30; Bhīma told Yudhiṣṭhira, accompanied by Sṛñjayas (सृञ्जयैः सह तिष्ठन्तम्), that he was prepared to accept the challenge of Duryo-dhana 9. 32. 28; Pāñcālas and Sṛñjayas applauded Duryodhana's words asking Bhīma to prove his words (दर्शयस्व बलं युद्धे) 9. 32. 49-50; when Balarāma came to witness the duel between Bhīma and Duryodhana, he embraced Pāṇḍavas and Sṛñjayas and enquired about their well being (अपृच्छत् कुशलं सर्वान्) 9. 33. 11; Duryodhana asked Yudhiṣṭhira, along with Sṛñjayas, to watch the duel 9. 54. 38-39; when Duryodhana was forced to kneel down by Bhīma, Sṛñjayas raised a loud roar; hearing their roar, Duryo-dhana was enraged 9. 56. 54-55; when Bhīma felled down Duryodhana he told Kṛṣṇa, Pāṇḍavas and Sṛñjayas that he had killed the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra on the strength of Draupadī's तपस् (रणे हतांस् तपसा याज्ञसेन्याः) 9. 58. 9-10; Dhṛtarāṣṭra asked Saṃjaya what did the Sṛñjayas do when Duryodhana was struck down; Saṃjaya told him that they waived their upper garments and raised a loud roar; the earth was unable to bear them who were filled with delight (आविध्यन् उत्तरीयाणि सिंहनादांश् च नेदिरे । नैतान् हर्षसमाविष्टान् इयम् सेहे वसुन्धरा ॥ ) 9. 60. 3-4; some shook their bows, others their bow-strings; still others blew their large conches or struck the दुन्दुभिस्; some made sportive gestures, others laughed (चिक्रीडुस् तथैवान्ये जहसुश् च) 9. 60. 5-6; they praised Bhīma's act in so many words and were happy that he had brought the enmity to an end (वैरस्य च गतः पारम्); they said that the horripilation experienced by them at the time of Duryo-dhana's fall had not yet subsided (दुर्यो-धनवधे यानि रोमाणी हृषितानि नः । अद्यापि न विहृष्यन्ति तानि … ) 9. 60. 7-16; Kṛṣṇa told Sṛñjayas not to rebuke Duryodhana anymore because he was already killed when he refused to give Pāṇḍavas their share although advised to do that, among others, by them (°गाङ्गेवसृञ्जयैः । … प्रोच्य-मानो ऽपि) 9. 60. 20; (31) During the massacre which took place at night of the eighteenth day, Aśvatthāman killed Pāṇḍava warriors and Sṛñjayas who were without weapons and armours and were agitated (अपेतशस्त्रसंनाहान् संरब्धान् पाण्डु-सृञ्जयान्) 10. 8. 74; Kṛpa and Kṛtavarman told Aśvatthāman that they had killed Pāñcālas and Sṛñjayas by thousands (as they were trying to escape from the camp) (विनिकृत्तान् सहस्रशः) 10. 8. 141; (32) More than a hundred Sṛñjayas (सृञ्जयांश् च शताधिकान्) were put on the funeral pyre along with the dead bodies of other fallen heroes and were cremated according to the prescribed rites 11. 26. 30, 33, 38. C. Some person referred to as Sṛñjayas which indicated their relationship with them: (1) Dhṛṣṭadyumna 3. 34. 12 (cf. 3. 23. 46); (2) Hotravāhana (father of Ambā's mother) 5. 175. 7, 12, 28; 5. 176. 4, 17, 20, 26; (3) Vainya, one of the ancient kings 1. 1. 166.
सैरन्ध्र: Sairandhra m. (pl.): Name of a Janapada. Listed by Saṃjaya among the northern Janapadas (also called Deśas 6. 10. 68) of Bhāratavarṣa (अत ऊर्ध्वं जनपदान् निबोध) 6. 10. 37, 5; (ओष्ट्राः पुण्ड्राः ससैरन्ध्राः) 6. 10. 56.
सोमक: Somaka m. (pl.): Name of a people, a section of Pāñcālas, hence often men-tioned along with them as also with Sṛñja-yas; the name, however, often stands for both Pāñcālas and Somakas. A. Description: Versed in the Vedas (वेदाध्ययनसंपन्न) 6. 1. 4; heroic (शूर) 7. 102. 67; 7. 135. 20; 7. 143. 28; (वीर) 6. 1. 2; 6. 104. 25; of great strength (महाबल) 6. 1. 3; great chariot-fighters (महारथ) 6. 103. 4; 6. 112. 75; great archers (महेष्वास) 6. 93 38; welcoming wars (युद्धाभिनन्दिन्) 6. 1. 4; wishing to get victory or die in war (आशंसन्तो जयं युद्धे वधं वाभिमुखा रणे) 6. 1. 4. B. Epic events: (1) Recounting the war events to Saṃjaya, Dhṛtarāṣṭra said that before Bhīṣma's fall he had reduced Soma-kas to a small number (कृत्वा सोमकान् अल्पशेषान्) 1. 1. 127; (2) At the start of the स्वयंवर of Draupadi, the priest of Somakas (in such contexts they are identi-fied with Pāñcālas) gave offerings in fire, asked Brāhmaṇas to pronounce benediction (ब्राह्मणान् स्वस्ति वाच्य च) and then stopped the sound of musical instruments 1. 176. 31-32; (3) Dhṛtarāṣṭra asked Saṃjaya how strong Somakas were with Dhṛṣṭadyumna as their general (धृष्ट-द्युम्नेन सेनान्या सोमकाः किम्बला इव) 5. 49. 9; (4) Duryodhana and others thought that if Kṛṣṇa was arrested Pāṇḍa-vas and Somakas would give up all their effort (निरुद्यमा भविष्यन्ति) 5. 128. 7; (5) When Pāṇḍavas had settled down at Hiraṇvatī, Duryodhana sent Ulūka as his messenger to them and Somakas 5. 157. 3; (6) Bhīṣma had assured Duryodhana that he would kill Pāṇḍavas and Somakas 5. 170. 2; (7) Dhṛtarāṣṭra asked Saṃjaya how did Kurus and Pāṇḍava-Somakas fight with one another at Kurukṣetra; thereupon Saṃjaya described to him how they fought when Somakas, determined to win or die while engaged in fighting, attack-ed Kauravas (आशंसन्तो जयं युद्धे वधं वाभिमुखा रणे) 6. 1. 1-4; Kau-ravas and Pāṇḍava-Somakas sat together before the start of the war and mutually agreed upon certain conventions and rules to be followed in the war (ततस् ते समयं चक्रुः कुरुपाण्डवसोमकाः । धर्मांश् च स्थापयाम् आसुर् युद्धानाम्  … ॥ ) 6. 1. 26, 33; the conventions and rules detailed in 6. 1. 27-32; (8) Duryo-dhana told Duḥśāsana that if Bhīṣma was protected in war he would kill Pāṇḍavas, Somakas and Sṛñjayas 6. 16. 14; (9) When Arjuna got prepared for the war Somakas and others blew their conches 6. 41. 2; (10) On the second day of the war, Dhṛṣṭadyumna and Somakas showered arrows on Droṇa 6. 48. 30; (11) On the third day, Kṛṣṇa noticed Bhīṣma routing Somakas chased by the delighted Kauravas (प्रभग्नान् दृश्य सोमकान्) 6. 55. 68; (12) On the fifth day, when Bhīṣma started killing Pāñcālas and Somakas, they acted nobly and decided to attack Bhīṣma (आर्यां युद्धे मतिं कृत्वा भीष्मम् एवाभिदुद्रुवुः) 6. 68. 31; (13) On the sixth day, Śikhaṇḍin surrounded by Soma-kas and Irāvant stood at the ‘tail’ of the Makaravyūha of Pāṇḍavas (पुच्छे मकरस्य) 6. 71. 4, 11; Somakas were terrified (वित्रेसुः) to hear the sound of Droṇa's conch when he blew it after defeat-ing Drupada 6. 73. 46; (14) On the eighth day, when the Pāṇḍava army attacked Bhīṣma he killed Pāñcālas, Somakas and Sṛñjayas with his arrows; nevertheless, abandoning the fear of death they attacked Bhīṣma (त्यक्त्वा मृत्युकृतं भयम्) 6. 84. 2-4; battle that ensued, in which Bhīṣma cut off their hands and heads and felled down those riding chariots, horses and elephants (विरथान् रथिनश् चक्रे; हयेभ्यो हयसादिनाम्; निर्मनुष्यांश् च मातङ्गाञ् … ), described in 6. 84. 5-7; when Droṇa attacked Somakas and Sṛñjayas in order to kill them (अभ्यद्रवत … प्रेषयिष्यम् यमक्षयम्) a loud cry was raised by Sṛñjayas (by implication also by Somakas) (तत्राक्रन्दो महान् आसीत् सृञ्ज-यानाम्) 6. 85. 20-21; that night, Karṇa assured Duryodhana that he would kill all Pārthas and Somakas if Bhīṣma laid down his arms and left the battlefield 6. 93. 13; Duryodhana then went to Bhīṣma and reminded him that he had assured him (Duryodhana) to kill Somakas; he asked Bhīṣma to carry out his assurance by killing Somakas 6. 93. 37-38; thereupon Bhīṣma once again assured Duryodhana that next day he would either kill Somakas and Pāñ-cālas to delight him or they would kill him (तैर् वाहं निहतः संख्ये गमिष्ये यमसादनम् । तान् वा निहत्य संग्रामे प्रीतिम् दास्यामि वै तव ॥ ) 6. 94. 14-15; (15) On the ninth day, in the morning, Duryodhana asked the kings to get ready with their armies since Bhīṣma was going to kill that day Somakas (अद्य भीष्मो … निहनिष्यति सोमकान्) 6. 95. 1; at mid-day, Bhīṣma fought a fierce battle with Somakas blowing them away by hundreds and thou-sands with his sharp arrows (व्यधमन्  … शतशो ऽथ सहस्रशः) 6. 99. 1-2; in the evening when the sun had set (भास्करे ऽस्तम् उपागते 6. 103. 1), Yudhi-ṣṭhira seeing that great chariot-fighters among Somakas had been defeated and had lost enthusiasm (जितान् दृष्त्वा … निरुत्-साहान् महारथान्) felt like ordering cessation of hostilities for that day (अव-हारम् अरोचयत्) 6. 103. 4; (16) Dhṛta-rāṣṭra asked Saṃjaya how, on the tenth day, did Bhīṣma face Pāṇḍavas while at the same time killing Somakas 6. 104. 25; Dhṛṣṭadyumna, aided by Somakas, attack-ed Droṇa 6. 111. 30; Bhīṣma, when attack-ed by Śikhaṇḍin, killed Somakas who followed Arjuna (पार्थपदानुगान्) 6. 112. 64; none of the great chariot-fighters of Somakas hoped to live after facing Bhīṣma in battle (न … यः संप्राप्य रणे भीष्मं जीविते स्म मनो दधे) 6. 112. 75; exhorted by Dhṛṣṭadyumna, Somakas and Sṛñjayas rushed at Bhīṣma showering weapons on him from all sides (अभ्यद्र-वन्त … शस्त्रवृष्ट्या समन्ततः) 6. 113. 16-17; Somakas and Pāñcālas were delight-ed when Bhīṣma fell down 6. 114. 107; (17) On the fourteenth day, when Droṇa started killing Somakas no one succeeded in facing him, nor was any one able to pierce him (with an arrow) (न चाप्य-भिययुः केचिद् अपरे नैव विव्यधुः) 7. 85. 34; watching the fierce duel between Satyasena and Sātyaki, Kauravas and Somakas praised them 7. 94. 7; in the afternoon of that day, Droṇa again fought with Somakas (अपराह्णे … संग्रामः समपद्यत । … पुनर् द्रोणस्य सोमकल्ः) 7. 101. 1; when the different alignments of the Pāṇḍava army were being agitated by Droṇa (व्यूहेष्व् आलोड्यमानेषु), Pāṇḍavas, Pāñcālas and Somakas went deep into the army of Kauravas (सुदूरम् अन्वयुः); the battle fought was so fierce that it looked like the end of the world (युगान्त इव भारत) 7. 102. 1-2; when Bhīma marched to offer assistance to Arjuna, Pāñcālas and Somakas followed him 7. 102. 67; after the death of Jayadratha, in the evening (अस्तं गच्छति भास्करे), Droṇa fought a fierce battle with Somakas (सोमकैः सार्धम् संग्रामो लोमहर्ष-णः); at that time great chariot-fighters of Somakas made every attempt to kill Droṇa (ते तु सर्वे प्रयत्नेन भारद्वाजं जिघांसवः । … अयुध्यन्त महारथाः ॥ ) 7. 121. 45-46; Droṇa sent a message to Aśvatthāman through Duryodhana not to spare Somakas in order to save his own life (न सोमकाः प्रमोक्तव्या जीवितं परिरक्षता) 7. 126. 33; (18) In the night war (which took place between the fourteenth and the fifteenth day), Duryo-dhana assured his fleeing army that he would himself kill Pārthas together with Pāñcālas and Somakas 7. 134. 54: Duryo-dhana requested Aśvatthāman to kill Pāñcālas and Somakas who, agitated, were moving in his army like a conflagration; he should kill them before they killed Kauravas (एते हि सोमका … मम सैन्येषु संरब्धा विचरन्ति दवाग्निवत्) 7. 134. 76-78; Aśvatthāman assured Duryodhana that for his sake and to delight him he would fight with Pāñcālas, Somakas and Kekayas (एष गच्छामि संग्रामे त्वत्-कृते … । … त्वत्प्रियार्थम्); scorched by his arrows, Somakas and others would run away in all directions; seeing his valour, Yudhiṣṭhira and Somakas would consider the world full of Aśvatthāman (अश्वत्थाममयं लोकं मंस्यन्ते); Yudhiṣṭhira would be dejected seeing the slain Pāñcālas and Somakas; Aśvatthāman would kill only those who engaged him in battle (ये मां युद्धे ऽभियोत्स्यन्ति तान् हनिष्यामि … ); once Somakas were within his reach they would not return alive 7. 135. 10-14; in the battle that followed Pāñcālas and Somakas fled 7. 135. 20; Sṛñjayas, Pāñcālas, Matsyas and Somakas followed Arjuna and Bhīma to attack Droṇa from right and left respectively (बीभत्सुर् दक्षिणं पार्श्वम् उत्तरं तु वृकोदरः) 7. 136. 13-14; Duryodhana advised his brothers to offer protection to Droṇa so that he would be able to kill Pārthas, Somakas and Sṛñjayas along with their kings (सोमकान् हन्यात् सृञ्जयांश् च सरा-जकान्) 7. 139. 21, 24; in the midst of the fierce night war (रौद्रे रात्रियुद्धे), Yudhiṣṭhira exhorted Pāṇḍavas and Soma-kas to attack Droṇa alone in order to kill him; accordingly, they attacked Droṇa uttering frightening cries (अभ्यद्रवत गच्छध्वं द्रोणम् एव जिघांसया । … द्रोणम् एवाभ्यवर्तन्त नदन्तो भैर-वान् रवान्) 7. 140. 2-3; when Karṇa's son Vṛṣasena cut off the armours of Drupada's army, Somakas, frightened, fied (सोमका विप्रदुद्रुवुः); while they were running away they appeared bright due to the light of the torches (ततस् तु द्रुपदानीकं शरैश् छिन्नतनुच्छदम् । संप्राद्रवत्  … । द्रवमाणाश् च सोमकाः व्यराजन्त … प्रदीपैर् अवभासिताः); after defeating great Somaka charriot-fighters Vṛṣasena turned towards Yudhiṣṭhira 7. 143. 21, 24-25, 28; when Śikhaṇḍin, defeated by Kṛpa turned back, Somakas and others covered him on all sides; then the battle started again 7. 144. 25, 27-28; seeing Droṇa kill-ing the Pāṇḍava army (पाण्डवीं चमूम्), Somakas quickly pierced him by showering arrows (विव्यधुः सोमकास् तूर्णं … शरवृष्टिभिः); but Droṇa deprived them of their lives 7. 147. 13-14; Kṛṣṇa drew Arjuna's attention to Bhīma who, cover-ed by Somakas and the Pāṇḍava army, attacked Droṇa and Karṇa (वृतः सोमक-पाण्डवैः) 7. 147. 28; when only the three parts of the (last quarter of the) night remained and the sun was about to rise, Droṇa divided his army into two parts and attacked Somakas and Pāṇḍavas along with Pāñcālas (त्रिभागमात्रशेषायाम् रात्र्यां; अरुणो ऽभ्युदयां चक्रे) 7. 161. 1-3 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 7. 186. 1; त्रिभागमात्रशेषा-यां मुहूर्तत्रयावशिष्टायाम्); (19) On the fifteenth day, Droṇa released ब्राह्म missile trying to kill all Somakas (विनिघ्नन् सर्वसोमकान्) 7. 164. 80; just before the fall of Droṇa, Kurus and Somakas got mixed up with one another in a battle shouting and felling each other with wea-pons (ततः प्रवृत्ते संग्रामे विमिश्राः कुरुसोमकाः । … शस्त्रैर् देहान् अपात-यन् ॥ ) 7. 165. 99; when the fleeing Pāñcāla warriors did not return to fight they were made to stand still where they were by Kṛṣṇa and Arjuna (7. 171. 67-69; 7. 172. 1-2); only Arjuna, along with Somakas and the constituents of their armies (?) returned to fight with Aśvatthāman (एक एव तु बीभत्सुः सोमकावयवैः सह) 7. 172. 3 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 7. 201. 3; सोमकावयवैः सोमकानाम् अवयवरूपैर् माण्डलिकैः); (20) On the sixteenth day, when Aṅgas attacked Nakula, Pāṇḍavas, Pāñcālas and Somakas attacked them to cover Nakula (नकुलं … परि पेतुः … पाण्डुपाञ्चालसोमकाः); then chariot-fighters fought with elephant-riders (रथि-नां हस्तिभिः सह) 8. 17. 21-22; when Somakas were being killed by the arrows of Karṇa, afflicted by pain and wounded by arrows, they hid themselves (अवालीयन्त राजेन्द्र वेदनार्ताः शरार्दिताः); (the Kaurava army too, being killed by Nakula, dispersed in all directions); the two armies then, standing beyond the range of arrows, chose to act as spectators (ते सेने … प्रेक्षकवत् स्थिते) 8. 17. 73-75; (21) Even after the battle of the sixteenth day, Dhṛtarāṣṭra was confident that Karṇa alone was capable of killing Pāṇḍavas and Soma-kas 8. 22. 16; (22) On the seventeenth day, Arjuna felt that by killing Karṇa he would give satisfaction to the great chariot-fighters of Somakas for having fulfilled their task to help their allies in war (कृतं कार्यं च मन्यन्तां मित्रकार्येप्सवो युधि) 8. 52. 25; Karṇa in the afternoon (अपराह्णे) of that day killed all Somakas in the presence of Bhīma 8. 56. 7, 53; Arjuna expressed his fear to Kṛṣṇa that if Kṛpa, Kṛtavarman and Aśvatthāman were not killed they would cause the des-truction of Somakas (अवध्यमानास् ते ऽस्माभिर् घातयिष्यन्ति सोमकान्) 8. 57. 5; Karṇa fought a great battle with Somakas in which he crushed them while destroy-ing their chariots and killing horses and elephants (सुमहत् … चक्रे युद्धं सोम-कान् संप्रमृद्नन्) 8. 60. 14; when Karṇa came up to Arjuna to kill him, Somakas urged (अभ्यक्रोशन्) Arjuna to hasten to pierce Karṇa (with an arrow), cut off his head without delay and shatter the hope of Duryodhana to get kingdom (विध्य कर्णम् । छिन्द्ध्य् अस्य मूर्धानम् अलं चिरेण श्रद्धां च राज्याद् धृतराष्ट्र-सूनोः) 8. 65. 10; when Karṇa cover-ed (समाचिनोत्) Arjuna with a hundred Kṣudraka arrows and pierced (बिभेद) Kṛṣṇa with sixty arrows, Somakas fied; Arjuna stopped them (तदन्तरं सोमकाः प्राद्रवन्त । … पार्थः सोमकान् प्रत्य-गृह्णात्) 8. 65. 32-34; seeing Karṇa lying dead on the ground, Somakas, delighted, made loud noise, sounded musical instru-ments and shook their (upper) garments and hands; others danced and embraced each other saying: “Karṇa is pierced with an arrow as fire is extinguished by a strong wind at the end of a sacrifice or at day-break in a bedroom; Karṇa's body with arrows all over it and smeared with blood shines like sun with his rays; the sun in the form of Karṇa has been forced to set by Kāla in the form of Arjuna; as the sun while setting takes away his light, so has the arrow taken away Karṇa's life” 8. 67. 28-32; after the death of Karṇa, in the evening, at the foot of the Himavant (हैमवते प्रस्थे 9. 5. 1) and near the river Sarasvatī (9. 4. 49), Śalya when requested by Duryodhana to lead the army (9. 5. 26-27), he (Śalya) assured him that he would defeat Pārthas and Somakas in battle 9. 6. 3; after Śalya's election as the general, the great chariot-fighters of Madra-kas while praising Śalya said that he was capable of defeating in battle even gods, demons and men, let alone Somakas and Sṛñjayas (किमु सोमकसृञ्जयान्) 9. 6. 9; that night, in the camp of Pāṇḍavas, Kṛṣṇa encouraged Yudhiṣṭhira to fight with Śalya; after he left, Yudhiṣṭhira gave leave to Pāñcālas and Somakas to leave his camp (विसृज्य पाञ्चालान् अथ सोमकान्) 9. 6. 39; (23) On the eighteenth day when Bhīma attacked Kṛpa, the great chariot-fighters of Somakas too attacked him and others in order to kill their opponents (अभ्य-द्रवन्त … जिघांसन्तः परान् युधि) 9. 7. 31; Somakas fell down by thousands due to the arrows of Śalya; after a while, Śalya again struck down Somakas and Pāṇḍava army and caused distress to Yudhi-ṣṭhira (सोमकाश् च सहस्रशः । पतिताः; शल्यो ऽपि … निघ्नन् सोमकपाण्डवान् । … युधिष्ठिरम् अपीडयत्) 9. 10. 21, 41; when Yudhiṣṭhira announced his decision to kill Śalya, the army of Pāṇḍavas, espe-cially the Pāñcālas, Somakas and Matsyas, expressed delight which helped the fulfil-ment of Yudhiṣṭhira's vow (i. e. encouraged him) (ततः प्रहर्षः सैन्यानां … पाञ्चा-लानां सोमकानां मत्स्यानां च विशेषतः । प्रतिज्ञां तां च सङ्ग्रामे धर्मराजस्य पूरयन्) 9. 15. 26-27; seeing Śalya, killing his opponents, angered Somakas and others, surrounded him (परिवव्रुः) 9. 16. 6; after the death of Śalya, when the Madra army attacked the Pāṇḍava army, Somakas and others covered Yudhiṣṭhira on all sides to protect him (युधिष्ठिरं परी-प्सन्तः समन्तात् पर्यवारयन्) 9. 17. 8; Somakas and others thought that the ele-phant of king Śālva (9. 19. 2-3), though one, was moving in thousand forms around them (तम् एव नागं ददृशुः समन्तात् । सहस्रशो वै विचरन्तम् एकम्) 9. 19. 6; Duryodhana alone halted (अवारयत्) with his sharp missiles the attack of Somakas and others 9. 20. 34; Aśvatthāman assured Duryodhana who had taken shelter in the Dvaipāyana lake that he would kill Soma-kas and others on that very day (अद्य निहनिष्यामि सोमकान्) 9. 29. 19; when Duryodhana's whereabouts became known, delighted Somakas shouted loudly (प्रा-क्रोशन् सोमकास् तत्र) 9. 29. 48; Somakas and others held Duryodhana in high regard (सर्व एवाभ्यपूजयन्) when he cha-llenged Bhīma to prove his boasts 9. 55. 40; after the duel began, Somakas and Pāṇḍavas were afraid when they noticed the velocity of the wind produced by Duryodhana's mace (गदा मारुतवेगं हि दृष्ट्वा) 9. 56. 31; when at one stage Bhīma lost consciousness due to the stroke of Duryodhana's mace on his chest, Soma-kas and Pāṇḍavas, their hopes dashed to the ground, became dejected (भृशोपहत-संकल्पा नहृष्टमनसो ऽभवन्) 9. 56. 49; Somakas were thrilled to see Duryo-dhana fall down (ददृशुः हृष्टरोमाणः) 9. 58. 2; the chief warriors among Somakas, who were righteous, did not approve of Bhīma's putting his foot on the head of fallen Duryodhana (नाभ्यनन्दन् धर्मा-त्मानः सोमकानां प्रबर्हाः) 9. 58. 13; (24) Dhṛtarāṣṭra asked Saṃjaya whether Kṛpa and Kṛtavarman took part in destroying the camp of Pāṇḍavas and in killing them and Somakas while fighting, and then go the way Duryodhana did (i. e. die in battle) (कच्चित् प्रमथ्य शिबिरं हत्वा सोमकपाण्डवान् । दुर्यो-धनस्य पदवीं गतौ परमिकां रणे ॥ ) 10. 8. 3; while moving in the camp, Aśva-tthāman happened to see the sons of Drau-padī and the surviving Somakas (अव-शिष्टांश् च सोमकान्) 10. 8. 44; as far as the destruction of Somakas, who were asleep and not on their guard, was con-cerned that night proved to be extremely cruel (एवंविधा हि सा रात्रिः सोमकानां जनक्षये । प्रसुप्तानां प्रमत्तानाम् आसीत् सुभृशदारुणा ॥ ) 10. 8. 142; Aśvatthāman was delighted that Somakas and the Mat-syas who had survived were all killed by him; he felt that he and his associates had done their duty; he wanted to give that very delightful news to Duryodhana if he was still alive (सोमका मत्स्यशेषाश् च सर्वे विनिहता मया ॥ इदानीं कृत-कृत्याः स्म … । यदि जीवति नो राजा तस्मै शंसामहे प्रियम् ॥ ) 10. 8. 150-151. C. Certain persons referred to as the leader or the prominent among the Somakas: A. सोमकानां धुरंधर-: Drupada 5. 5. 1; B. सोमकानां प्रबर्ह-: (1) Dhṛṣṭadyumna 1. 185. 1; 5. 22. 17; 5. 47. 39; (2) Some prominent Somakas, not named 9. 58. 13.
सोमकुल: Somakula (nt., sg.): The lineage of Soma. The king of Gāndhāra country (not named) born in this lineage, was killed by Māndhātṛ (सोमकुलोत्पन्नो गान्धारा-धिपतिर् महान्) 3. 126. 40 [See the next two entries].
सोमवंश: Somavaṃśa m. (sg.): The lineage of Soma. Bhīma told Hanūmant that he, a Kaurava, was born in the lineage of Soma (कौरवः सोमवंशीयः कुन्त्या गर्भेण धारितः) 3. 147. 3 [See Somakula and the next entry].
सोमान्ववाय: Somānvavāya m. (sg.): The lineage of Soma. Yayāti, son of Nahuṣa, was born in the lineage of Soma (अस्ति सोमान्ववाये मे जातः कश्चिन् नृपः सखा । यायातिर् नाम राजर्षिर् … ) 5. 112. 6-7 (This is what Su-parṇa told Gālava). [See the preceding two entries].
सौध: Saudha m. (pl.): Name of a Janapada. Listed by Saṃjaya among the northern Janapadas (also called Deśas 6. 10. 68) of Bhāratavarṣa (अत ऊर्ध्वं जनपदान् नि-बोध) 6. 10. 37, 5; (सौधा मद्रा … ) 6. 10. 40.
सौबल्य: Saubalya m. (pl.): Name of a Jana-pada. Listed by Saṃjaya among the northern Janapadas (also called Deśas 6. 10. 68) of Bhāratavarṣa (मत्स्याः सुकुट्यः सौब-ल्याः) 6. 10. 38; (for other citation see above Saudha).
